News.title: Shocking moment bloody brawl erupts between knife-wielding men in broad daylight – as 2 arrested after armed cops swoop
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment a street brawl breaks out in broad daylight as bloodied men armed with knives and sticks batter each other.

The chaos was caught on camera after tempers flared on a residential road in Burton upon Trent, Staffordshire, leading to two arrests.



Footage shows a group of five men, some with bloodied faces, exchanging blows as the scrap spirals out of control.

Passersby in cars are heard beeping their horns as they drive past and according to one witness, schoolchildren were also watching on.



In shocking video obtained by The Sun, one of the group appears to be wielding a knife and blood can be seen pouring from the back of another.

A man in a black jumper and shorts can then be seen grabbing a plank of wood before raising it in the air and slamming it down onto another man’s head.



Police were called and armed cops swarmed Horninglow Road at about 4.30pm on Monday before two men were arrested.

Later footage showed police on the scene and the road taped off in all directions.



One resident, who was eating a pizza and watching a film when he heard a commotion, told The Sun: “I heard screaming outside.

“There were a lot of school children walking past coming back home from school. It was frightening.

“No one has been allowed in or out the street since it happened.

“A large fight with a knife is only going to end one way.

“The people involved in the fight were already gone when police arrived ten minutes later.”



A spokesperson for Staffordshire Police said: “Two men have been arrested following a fight in Burton-upon-Trent.

“We were called at 4.25pm yesterday (October, 5) to William Street following reports that a group of men were fighting and carrying weapons.

“Officers attended the scene and seized a knife.



“Two 25-year-old men, both of Burton-upon-Trent, have been arrested on suspicion of affray.

“They remain in custody for questioning.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We are appealing for anyone with CCTV, doorbell or dashcam footage of the area at the time to contact us. Call 101, quoting incident 662 of 5 October, or use Live Chat on our website.

“To report anonymously, call Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.”

News.title: Meghan Markle spotted having dinner with Nobel Prize winner at Claridges amid UK return – would you have clocked them?
News.content:
Next

MEGHAN Markle has been spotted enjoying a posh dinner with a Nobel Prize winner upon her return to the UK.

The wife of Prince Harry was seen out at Claridges with other diners spotting her with a fellow famous face – but would you have clocked them?



Meghan, 45, was in fact having dinner with activist, Malala Yousafzai.

A group of pals who were also at the famous eatery uploaded a clip to TikTok in which Meghan and Malala could be seen chatting over dinner.



The friends could be seen sharing a cheers with a glass of wine as they added the light-hearted caption: “POV: Claridge’s decided to seat Meghan Markle and Malala in front of you.”

Meghan was wearing a white turtleneck jumper as she sat opposite the Pakistani activist and award winner.

The pair are long believed to have had a friendship and held a public appearance with one another in October 2020 when Meghan supported her International Day of the Girl event.

The virtual event saw the pair, along with the Prince, discuss barriers to education for young women, particularly given the COVID pandemic of the time.



Meghan and Harry quietly returned to the UK over summer – having previously opted to quit the country for a new life in Los Angeles.

They previously walked away from their royal duties to live as private citizens in the US but they are now firmly back in England with their two children, Archie and Lillibet.

Earlier this month, they were snapped stepping out in public for the first time since their arrival back in the country.

The couple, who are understood to be residing in the Cotswolds, were seen heading to a local pub called The Falkland Arms.

They were seen glancing at a menu board outside the 16th-century pub, which is round the corner from the Beckhams home in Great Tew, Oxfordshire.



Inside the pub, Meghan dined on a £18.25 portion of gluten-free beer-battered haddock and chips with mushy peas and tartare sauce.

Harry chose a £17.95 chicken, ham and leek pie with seasonal greens, creamy mashed potatoes and gravy.

The boozer still retains most of its traditional features, including flagstone floors and low beamed ceilings.

Their return comes with the couple, who are no longer working royals, still battling for taxpayer-funded, armed police protection.

News.title: Giant 42ft-high ‘monstrosity’ that ‘looks like a WW2 watch tower’ is slammed by locals in UK seaside resort
News.content:
Next

A GIANT lift in one of the UK’s most popular seaside resorts has been slated for looking like a “WW2 watch tower”.

Some local residents have described the 42ft-high lift that overlooks the English Channel as “a monstrosity”.



The iconic sealift is in the process of being repaired as part of a £750,000 revamp of the Victorian Madeira Terraces in Brighton.

Labour councillor David McGregor said the lift “looks brilliant” and shared images of the new design on social media.



He said: “Went down to check on the progress of the Madeira Terraces and lift works.

“It’s coming along incredibly well. The arches look amazing, the iron work has been done to such a fantastic standard.

“The lift looks brilliant and will be a key part of the city for so many.

“After decades of delays, it was this Labour Council that finally started the work to revive this iconic structure and keep our seafront as accessible as possible.”

But the new design has split opinion among locals, with one resident writing: “The lift looks a bloody monstrosity really out of keeping.”

Another posted: “That lift is butt ugly and totally not in keeping with the terraces!” A third resident said: “Looks like a WW2 watch tower.”



Not everyone was disparaging, though, with one person writing: “I really like the design of the new lift and it is great that disabled and elderly people will be able to more easily access the seafront.”

Another said: “Blimey the moaners are out in force. I think it looks great. Clean, simple, elegant, functional.”

The Sun has contacted Brighton and Hove City Council for comment.

News.title: How tragic loophole left Danielle Jones’ uncle to abuse girls under family’s nose for 20 years… before murdering teen
News.content:
Next

WHEN 15-year-old Danielle Jones disappeared without a trace, alarm bells started ringing immediately.

Quiet and considerate, she never left home without leaving mum Linda a note and, scared of the dark, she was always home before sunset.



Her distraught parents called police and the entire local community of East Tilbury, Essex, launched a search for the teenage schoolgirl.

But one man was conspicuous by his absence from the search party – her 43-year-old uncle Stuart Campbell.



The builder had recently developed a strange obsession with Danielle which had left both her and her parents uneasy.

But without concrete evidence, and fearful of causing a huge family fall-out by making accusations of inappropriate behaviour, her parents had kept quiet.

It was a decision that would have devastating consequences.

Now a new True Crime documentary, Britain’s Countryside Killers: Betrayal by Blood, reveals that, unbeknown to the family, Campbell was a sexual predator who for years had posed as a modelling agent to persuade young girls to come to his home for pictures where he would then assault them.



And he had previous convictions for indecent assault on teenage girls.

But he had managed to hide his evil sordid past from his family – meaning he had access to groom and manipulate Danielle.

Crime journalist Danny Shaw says: “When police looked into Stuart Campbell’s background they found he had a history of grooming young girls.

“He would approach them on the street and then invite them back to his house.

“He said he was a representative from a modelling agency called Cinderella’s.



“But it was clearly an attempt to groom girls and presumably sexually assault them.”

It was June 18, 2001, when Danielle set off for school as normal – but never arrived.

Her school alerted her mum at 2.30pm to say Danielle was absent – something that was completely out of character for her.

When Danielle hadn’t returned home by sunset, mum Linda immediately knew something was wrong because Danielle was scared of the dark and police were called.

And her family’s unease at the attention her uncle Stuart Campbell had been paying to the teenager began to take a sinister turn.



Campbell was married to Danielle’s dad’s sister and was part of the close-knit family.

But Danielle’s parents, Linda and Tony, had never quite trusted him, and had become concerned about his behaviour towards Danielle.

Retired detective Maddie Hennah explains: “Stuart’s attention towards Danielle became slightly obsessive.



“When she finished school he would be in his blue van waiting for her.

“Danielle found this very embarrassing amongst her peers to have him waiting for her when she got off the school bus.”

Something clearly was not right in the relationship between Campbell and Danielle, but with no clear evidence her family were reluctant to make any accusations for fear of blowing the whole family apart.

Criminologist Dr Honor Doro Townshend explains: “It was a really difficult situation for the family to be in.

“If they tried to make accusations about Campbell being inappropriate with Danielle that could fracture the family, and if they don’t have any grounds for it, that is almost one of the worst social accusations that could occur.



“So whilst they are feeling uncomfortable they haven’t actually seen anything inherently wrong yet.

“They are keeping an eye out, but actually progressing that any further and keeping him away is a very difficult situation.

“And that is exactly why predators choose their targets exactly like that.



“The majority of sexual offences against children happen with somebody in the family or in the immediate circle of friends and family.

“That is because they are relying on that social pressure to not accuse someone of such a crime.

“And that is exactly what Stuart Campbell was counting on.”

Danielle tried to distance herself from her uncle and her family hoped their issues with Stuart would be resolved soon.

But everything changed the morning she disappeared without a trace.



Because of their previous fears, Danielle’s dad Tony went round to Campbell’s house as soon as he heard she was missing.

Danny Shaw says: “He peered through the window and what he noticed was quite surprising.

“He saw what looked like cameras and some sort of photography set up in the living room.”



Very quickly Campbell was becoming a person of interest to the police as Danielle’s family flagged their previous concerns about his interest in the teenager.

And investigators soon found issues with Campbell’s statement.

He told police he was out of town buying tools in a DIY shop that day.

But mobile phone data disproved his story.

He was also on the police radar because a blue van matching the one that Campbell owned had been seen talking to a girl matching the description of Danielle.



Police put Campbell under surveillance and in a shock twist Danielle’s mobile phone began to show signs of life.

Dr Townshend says: “Campbell himself starts receiving texts after Danielle has gone missing and it is from Danielle saying that she has left and that she doesn’t want to be contacted, she doesn’t want to be found.

“This is giving the family some hope that she is OK and she has run away.



“In actual fact though forensic linguistics which look at how people communicate and text very quickly identified that it doesn’t follow the normal texting pattern of Danielle, there are differences in how she is spelling things, how she is using punctuation that don’t line up with her usual texting pattern.

“So instead what actually happened is the perpetrator is texting from Danielle’s phone, trying to divert attention, giving false hope to Danielle’s family.

“It is actually a very cruel and manipulative process by this perpetrator who clearly thinks they are going to get away with this.

“This is Campbell himself showing these messages to the family and really trying to manipulate the situation, control the situation, but still ultimately thinking that he is not going to be apprehended.”

But police continued to make further discoveries into Campbell’s strange fascination with Danielle.



During a search of Danielle’s home, they found some inappropriate notes from Campbell to Danielle in a pencil case.

And detectives looking into Campbell made some dark discoveries about his past.

In 1989 he had falsely imprisoned a 14-year-old girl and taken indecent images of her, but he only received a 12 month suspended sentence.

“In addition the sex offenders register was not implemented until 1997, so if that crime had been committed after 1997 he would have had to be on the sex offenders register and he would have had to disclose that to his future family and partner,” explains Dr Townshend.

Police arrested Campbell on suspicion of abducting Danielle and during a search of his house they found a diary that he had been keeping, detailing every interaction he had had with her in the days leading up to her disappearance.



And even more alarmingly they found photography equipment, indecent images of girls along with handcuffs and lingerie.

Dr Townshend adds: “Following Campbell’s arrest around 30 women came forward to tell police that over a span of around 20 years he had regularly been posing as a fake model agency to get young girls to come into his home to take pictures of them, often in very inappropriate states of undress, often making them feel very uncomfortable, and he had also assaulted multiple of these young girls.

“Now this is very significant because it picks up a clear modus operandi for Campbell.

“This is clearly someone who has a sexual interest, a sexual fascination with young girls.

“Sexually motivated offenders are at very high risk of repeat offending and that is because the sexual gratification wears off.



“So while they get gratification for controlling and manipulating the situation and putting these young girls into very vulnerable situations, it only lasts so long and that is when they seek it again.

“And that is exactly what Campbell has been repeatedly been doing for over 20 years before turning his sights to a young girl within his immediate family giving him more scope to control and manipulate.”

Also during the search of Campbell’s home they found a pair of stockings with a speck of blood on them.

Tests revealed the DNA was a mixture of Campbell’s and Danielle’s.

The text messages, the DNA, and Campbell’s background of having a predilection for girls of Danielle’s age made a compelling case against him.



In November 2001 he was charged with abduction and murder.

Despite Danielle still not being found, police began preparing for the murder trial.

With only circumstantial evidence, they faced an uphill battle to get justice for Danielle and her family.

Campbell’s trial started in October 2002. He maintained his innocence and pleaded not guilty.

Dr Townshend says: “Trials like this are fairly uncommon and, at the time, this was a pretty landmark case in terms of being able to use this variety of evidence to gain a conviction.



“They didn’t have an admission of guilt, they didn’t have Danielle’s body, they didn’t have any CCTV directly showing this happening.

“What they had to rely on was building a picture of Campbell as someone capable of these crimes of abduction and murder.”

On December 19, 2002, the jury found Campbell guilty on all counts.

He was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum term of 20 years, and he was also sentenced to a 10 year concurrent sentence for abduction.

To this day Danielle’s body has never been found.



Stuart Campbell remains behind bars and, due to Helen’s Law, which requires parole boards to consider a killer’s refusal to disclose the whereabouts of a victim’s body, he faces a lifetime in jail.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Dr Townshend says: “Because Campbell has refused to admit his guilt, and crucially share where Danielle’s body is, it is likely now after Helen’s law that he will never get out.”

Britain’s Countryside Killers Season 3 airs on Thursdays at 10 pm on the TRUE CRIME channel.

News.title: Mum ‘caught having sex with pet dog Rancher’ can still ‘spend time’ with pet every night… life after ‘sick CCTV’ leak
News.content:
Next

AS you approach the smart detached home in the middle-class Florida enclave, you are instantly greeted by the barking of two large dogs.

A sign reads “Welcome home” and the children’s shoes on the doorstep would leave you mistaken for thinking this is a normal family abode. But one of those dogs is at the centre of a shocking and depraved case that has gripped America.



Mum-of-two Malia Nummerdor, who owns the £70,000 house in the small coastal town of Punta Gorda, is accused of performing depraved sex acts with her canine pal Rancher.

She is now out on bail.

The Sun can reveal that the insurance agent is allowed to have dinner at her house where the dogs are still living and so can “spend time with them”.



And we can also exclusively confirm exactly which dog – seen in social media snaps of her pets – Malia Nummerdor is alleged to have had sexual activity with.

Sources said Malia, 38, has been granted permission to eat at home in the evenings because she has nowhere else to go and is currently staying with friends “couch surfing”.

It is unclear why she is not allowed to stay the night.

Her career is in ruins and she has moaned to friends that she can’t work anymore because of the stigma that the story has created for her.

It has rocked the quiet neighbourhood, which is a four-hour drive west of Miami, lined with small farms, plant nurseries, and colourful family homes.



She used to spend her days caring for her two sons and dropping them off at school but now friends tell The Sun she has to battle threats in the post sent by angry animal lovers.

And despite being released over two weeks ago, police still have her phone.

Last night an insider said: “Malia believes she has done nothing wrong.



“She has never broken the law prior to this allegation.

“She is confident that all of this will be dropped.

“Malia is angry and upset by it all.”

Incredibly, Malia has gained a number of supporters who have set up a Go Fund Me page for her claiming she is innocent.

They have asked for donations as she has been “displaced from her home” and needs cash for “personal and household needs”.



And on her Facebook page, which is still open, hundreds of people who knew her have offered their support and pledged to stand by her.

One wrote: “Just wanted to say no matter what anyone does in their life, right or wrong, it’s not okay to get blasted on social media for it.

“Your kids love you. Remember that! That’s what matters.”

It all started with Malia’s estranged husband Erik Nummerdor, who himself has a string of past convictions, one of them being for grand theft.

On September 11, Erik alleged on the social media site that Malia had engaged in sexual activity with the family dog.



Police from the Charlotte County Sheriff’s office reviewed posts and comments which, according to official documents seen by The Sun, included statements that he had photographic proof.

When questioned by the detective three days later, Erik said that he had installed two surveillance cameras inside the house, including in the bedroom, to try and find out who had been taking money from a coin jar.

The detective wrote in the affidavit: “He stated the bedroom camera was visible, displayed a blinking red light, and was known to household members.



“The camera recorded continuously in rolling intervals, overwriting older footage.”

While reviewing recordings, Erik said he found a video depicting his then wife engaging in sexual conduct with the family dog Ranger and that she was “partially nude”.

The detective went on: “I reviewed the images and observed an adult female, identified by Erik as Malia, nude from the waist down, positioned with the dog in a manner consistent with sexual activity.”

When Malia was questioned by police, she confirmed she was the individual in the room and that the dog was hers, but denied anything sexual had occurred.

She, however, “could not provide a consistent explanation for what was seen on the camera”.



Malia claimed Erik had installed cameras without her knowledge and had accessed her social-media accounts to post images and videos, per the affidavit.

There is some confusion as to whether the footage was taken in 2024, which she told police in her interview, or in 2025, which Erik has told his Facebook followers.

Sources close to Malia told The Sun she has now confirmed that the footage was taken at the end of 2025.

And they said her two sons, who are from a different relationship, are now living with their father and she has not been allowed to see them.

When Malia posed for her mugshot on the day of her arrest, she flashed a toothy grin.



Sheriff Bill Prumell slammed her in a statement following the snap, saying: “There are only a few times in my career that I have been at a loss for words.

“This is one of those times.

“I simply cannot comprehend this behaviour.

“And then to smile in the mugshot? I don’t know what there is to smile about when you’ve been arrested for something as disgusting as this.”

As Malia awaits her court appearance on October 19, her husband Erik, continues to post to his Facebook disputing her claims and even suggests that the fundraiser is fake.



He asked: “How do you become displaced from your home when you own the home?

“And how do you lose a job that you never had?

“I know the whole story.

“These are questions that should be asked.”

As one source – close to the two of them – aptly put it: “Who knows what the truth is.



“Is this a bitter divorce battle or a heinous crime?

“We will have to wait and see.”

News.title: Horrifying moment packed party bus overturns during graduation celebration as students thrown onto pavement after crash
News.content:
Next

THIS is the horrifying moment a double-decker bus crashes and topples over during a graduation party – throwing students overboard.

The “chiva” truck – modified to have a second floor – was packed full of schoolgirls when it suddenly overturned.



Harrowing footage shows the overloaded bus edging its way out of a junction in Ecuador before it slowly tips to the side.

The entire top deck of partying schoolgirls is thrown out onto the busy pavement.



Several people were injured in the terrifying crash.

Just moments earlier the girls had been singing and dancing on the top deck – with even the driver in sunglasses boogying in his seat.

Music blared over the speakers as the bus rumbled through Azogues in a street parade organised by Catholic school La Providencia Educational Unit.

Pupils were hanging over the side of the bus – which was strung with balloons – when the vehicle suddenly lost its balance.

The terrifying traffic crash unfolded over several agonising seconds around 1pm on October 3.

The collapsing truck narrowly missed flattening a car waiting to cross the street.



Firefighters, police and paramedics raced to the scene as passers-by desperately tried to help the injured pupils.

As medical services tended to the wounded the number of injured climbed higher and higher.

At least 22 people were rushed to Clemed Hospital in Azogues, according to the hospital’s director Fernando Quevedo.



Three had injuries to their chest and head while another broke his arm and a fifth had a sternum injury – the rib cage bone covering the heart.

More passengers were taken to other hospitals in the area as medics scrambled to treat all the wounded.

Thankfully, nobody was killed in the horror accident.

Early investigations have suggested that the party bus collided with something on the road surface.

Another theory is that the double-decker was too overloaded with passengers.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The party bus had been part of a graduation party and celebration for the 140th anniversary of Catholic school La Providencia Educational Unit.

A banner hung on the double-decker read “The last prom ’26” as teenage students danced and sang on the upper deck.

News.title: Halloween ‘Scarefest’ warning in NINE cities across UK over ‘convincing’ ticket trick that could lose you over £100
News.content:
Next

CUSTOMERS are being warned of fake ‘Scarefest’ tickets sold in major cities across the UK.

Halloween Nights Fear, the company behind the sales, advertised ticket prices range from £14 to £140 and three venues have already come forward to say the listings are fake.



They are listed in London, Liverpool, Bristol, Southampton, Leicester, Salford, Edinburgh, Cardiff and Swansea.

James Dymond, Director of Bradgate Park in Leicester, said: “It’s a huge concern for all the different venues.



“All we can say to people is check with us, check our social media and our website first.

“If there is an event here that we are running or that we’re sanctioning someone else to run, it will be there.”



Halloween Nights Fear’s phone number is not recognised, the company is not registered on Companies House, its social media has been shut down and there has been no response via email.

Technology expert David McClelland has acknowledged how understandable it is that people fell for this alleged scam.

He said: “The website looks so convincing, it’s one of the most impressive scams I’ve seen – there’s so much content on there.

“Sometimes one of the tells that you might expect from a scam website is that they’re quite shallow – there isn’t very much text or there aren’t very many pictures – but this Halloween Nights Fear website is huge.”



Leicestershire Trading Standards said: “We are taking steps to contact the website operator and have requested that the site is deactivated.

“Anyone who has purchased tickets and believes they may have been affected should contact their bank as soon as possible to discuss potential recovery options.

“They can also seek advice from the Citizens Advice Consumer Service on 0808 223 1133, which shares information with Trading Standards.”

News.title: Air fryer warning over cooking common side dish this week issued by Philips expert
News.content:
Air fryer warning over cooking common side dish this week issued by Philips expert

Air fryer chef at Philips, Martin Senders, has issued a word of warning to people cooking at home

View 3 Images Expert warns against airfryer shortcut that could 'fill your kitchen with smoke' (Image: Getty)

An air fryer expert has issued a warning to anyone using the popular kitchen appliance this week to cook a certain food item. It comes as UK households celebrate National Curry Week, which ends on October 11.

‌



‌



People taking part in this week's celebrations by cooking their favourite curry at home have been warned against using air fryers for one particular side dish. Experts say that making the 'mistake' could ruin the meal and potentially fill their kitchens with smoke.

‌



While air fryers have gained widespread popularity as go-to appliances for quick meals, experts warn that attempting to cook poppadoms in them can quickly go wrong. Martin Senders, an air fryer chef at Philips, cautions that the delicate structure of poppadoms makes them completely unsuitable for air fryer cooking.

‌



According to Senders, the primary issue lies in the appliance's intense hot air circulation. "Air fryers are amazing cooking appliances, and are brilliant for cooking food, but poppadoms simply cannot handle the intense airflow," Senders explained.

View 3 Images Think twice before air-frying this curry favourite, expert says

The aggressive air currents hit the poppadom surface too forcefully, causing uneven cooking, scorched edges, curled-up discs, and rapid burning. In some cases, attempting this shortcut can even cause appliances to overheat and trigger smoke alarms within seconds. "They burn, buckle, and in some cases trigger smoke alarms within seconds," he warned.

‌



To achieve light, crispy poppadoms without any kitchen chaos, Senders advises sticking to cooking methods designed for quick bursts of open heat. Poppadoms are best prepared traditionally in hot oil, under a grill, or briefly inside a microwave.

"The reason for this is that poppadoms are designed to cook in a quick burst of open heat, either in hot oil, under a grill, or in the microwave. However, in the air fryer, the rapid airflow hits the poppadom surface too aggressively, causing uneven cooking and sudden burning."

View 3 Images The expert says attempting to cook poppadoms in an air fryer can quickly go wrong

Article continues below

However, curry fans do not need to leave their air fryers entirely idle during National Curry Week. Senders points out that other popular Indian side dishes perform exceptionally well in air fryers.

Classics such as onion bhajis and samosas turn out deliciously crisp on the outside and juicy on the inside, making them ideal alternatives for air fryer cooking. "Let the air fryer handle other tasty sides, such as onion bhajis or samosas, that turn out deliciously crisp and juicy and are perfect to cook in the air fryer," he said.

Poppadoms are authentic Indian flatbreads that originated on the Indian subcontinent, where they are traditionally made from lentil, chickpea, or rice flour and eaten as a crunchy side dish or snack. However, the common practice of serving them as a distinct pre-meal appetiser alongside a tray of chutneys and pickles is a specific British Indian Restaurant (BIR) tradition rather than a native South Asian custom.

News.title: Key strain of flu detected in UK 'mutates' as NHS warns of 'ominous' signs
News.content:
Key strain of flu detected in UK 'mutates' as NHS warns of 'ominous' signs

Flu is at the ‘highest levels we’ve seen’ by this date as people urged to get vaccinated

View Image People are being urged to get flu vaccines as cases rise in the UK (Image: Getty)

The NHS has given a warning about ‘ominous’ signs as cases of flu are higher than they’ve been for the last 4 years. At a press conference this afternoon (Thursday), officials said flu trends have been rising since August and there are possible signs that we may see an early flu season.

‌



‌



Prof Frankie Swords, National Medical Director at NHS England, told a press conference this afternoon that flu was at the ‘highest levels we’ve seen’ by this date and said hospitals were already under pressure with high bed occupancy rates.

‌



It is thought that the increases in flu are being driven by young adults, including those returning to university. Prof Swords said levels were the ‘highest we’ve seen’ and added “there are ominous signs of increased pressure.” She said beds had seen 90% occupancy in September and urged people to get their vaccinations. One of the key flu strains has also changed a lot since the vaccine was created.

‌



Flu positivity increased with a positivity rate of 6.5% compared with 5% on the previous week. UKHSA scientists said flu activity throughout September has been higher than in the same period during all past four winter seasons. Flu trends have been rising since August and there are possible signs that the UK may see an early flu season, officials said.

A recent World Health Organization (WHO) technical report indicated that one of the flu A(H1N1) viruses that has recently been seen at low levels in Europe, and recently in the UK, has ‘drifted’ compared to the virus component used in this year’s flu vaccine. Last year UKHSA said it also saw a ‘drifted’ A(H3N2) flu virus, but the vaccines still gave good protection.

It added: “It is still too early in the season to say with any certainty whether this drifted A(H1N1) virus will circulate widely in the UK or how effective the vaccine will be against it. Flu is still at very low levels, but the subtyping data available so far this season shows there is an equal mix of subtypes A(H3N2) and A(H1N1) in England.

‌



“Importantly, the flu vaccine contains components to help protect against all 3 types of flu viruses (Flu A subtypes H1N1 and H3N2 - and Flu B). Flu is unpredictable, some seasons one flu virus will dominate, and some seasons all 3 flu viruses could circulate at different times during winter. As we saw with last year’s A(H3N2) virus, which dominated, flu vaccines typically remain effective at preventing severe flu, even when drifted strains are seen.” Drift consists of small changes (or mutations) in the genes of influenza viruses.

Modelling indicated that, in England last winter, the vaccination programme prevented around 100,000 hospital admissions and 7,000 deaths.

Dr Jamie Lopez Bernal, Consultant Epidemiologist, said: “Flu levels are increasing with the possibility of an early flu season, so now is the time for those eligible to get vaccinated.

‌



“The vaccine contains components to help protect against all three types of flu virus. We may see one flu virus dominating at different times during winter, or all three circulating at similar levels throughout. As we saw with last year’s dominant virus, flu vaccines typically remain effective at preventing severe flu, even when drifted strains are seen.”

Members of the public who are eligible for a free vaccine can check their eligibility and book an appointment through the NHS App, online, or by contacting their GP practice or a local pharmacy.

XFG American Covid strain and its impact on UK hospitals - everything we know READ MORE :

Thousands of people across the UK are falling ill with the dominant strain of Covid, XFG, dubbed American Covid after rapidly spreading across the USA.

‌



New data released this afternoon by the UK Health Security Agency showed hospitalisations have increased, as have positive tests. While the strain has been known since last year, it has now become dominant in several countries, with medical experts warning that it has some unique symptoms. New figures from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) show hospital admissions relating to Covid increased by almost 50% in a week. And, some parts of the country have seen much sharper increases.

Officials also said that levels of flu and hospitalisation are already higher than for the last five years. The data for the week to October 4 showed Covid-19 positivity increased with a weekly positivity rate of 9.1% compared with 7.9% in the previous week.

Hospitalisations increased to 2.04 per 100,000 compared with 1.75 per 100,000 in the previous week. Intensive care admissions rose slightly. Dr Alex Allen, Consultant Epidemiologist at UKHSA:

Article continues below

“While COVID-19 activity has shown some recent increases, cases remain at low levels in the UK. “It’s completely normal for viruses to change over time. The strains currently going around, including those known as XFG, are closely related to strains that have been with us for over a year, so this isn’t something new. We’re also not seeing any evidence that these are making people more ill or spreading faster than before, and this year’s autumn vaccine has been specifically designed to protect against them.

“If you are eligible for a COVID-19 vaccine, it is because you are at greater risk of severe illness and being hospitalised. Don’t risk it, get the vaccine and give yourself the best protection.” The strains currently circulating, including those known as XFG, are closely related to strains seen here for over a year, UKHSA said.

Dr Allen said the current vaccination was targeted against the ‘American Covid’ strain, and said it had been circulating for around 12 months - but had only seen a bigger rise in the last couple of months.

News.title: Salford nursery incident - live:  Gun found in building by police as two arrested
News.content:
Multiple police vehicles are outside the Mini Fingers Day Nursery in Salford, with officers seen carrying a weapon from the premises

A gun and a "substantial" amount of ammunition have been found by police in a Greater Manchester nursery with police arresting two men.

Multiple police vehicles have swarmed outside Mini Fingers Day Nursery in Salford which closed for good earlier this week.

Police have been pictured alongside two Tactical Aid Unit vans outside the building in the Irlam area of the city this morning.

Two men have been arrested after a gun and a "substantial quantity" of ammunition was found at the premises, Greater Manchester Police have said. They said the nursery's earlier closure is "entirely unrelated" with their investigation.

An email sent to parents from the nursery manager previously said: "It is with great sadness that I have to inform you that as of today, the owner of the nursery has decided to close the business. We as a staff team are devastated and have no words following this decision."

It is believed parents were sent an email about a collapsed drain and "vermin" at the nursery, reports Manchester Evening News.

News.title: 'Deeply loved' girl, 12, died from allergic reaction to milkshake after blender 'wasn't cleaned'
News.content:
'Deeply loved' girl, 12, died from allergic reaction to milkshake after blender 'wasn't cleaned'

Mia Shay St Hilaire died after a severe allergic reaction to a Twix milkshake which she drank at the Pop Inn Café in London while visiting with her aunt and sister

View 2 Images Mia Shay St Hilaire suffered a severe allergic reaction after drinking a Twix milkshake (Image: Family handout/PA Wire)

A 12-year-old girl who had a hazelnut allergy collapsed and died after drinking a milkshake that was prepared in a blender that had not been cleaned at a café in London, an inquest has heard.

‌



‌



Mia Shay St Hilaire suffered a severe allergic reaction after drinking a Twix milkshake at the Pop Inn Cafe in Bermondsey, central London. The schoolgirl was visiting the café with her aunt and sister and consumed only part of the drink.

‌



The milkshake contained hazelnut from a previous milkshake made in the same blender, the inquest heard. CCTV evidence showed that café operator Baris Yucel had not cleaned the blender before preparing Mia’s milkshake.

‌



Coroner Briony Ballard listened to evidence at London Inner South Coroner’s Court before publishing a narrative conclusion on Mia’s death. She said Mia, from Sydenham in southeast London, had consumed some of a Twix milkshake "which had been cross-contaminated with hazelnut residue from a Kinder Bueno milkshake previously prepared in the same unwashed blender".

View 2 Images Mia was 'deeply loved' (Image: Family handout/PA Wire)

The coroner said: "She developed rapidly progressing anaphylaxis and later collapsed at her aunt’s home." Mia died despite extensive emergency treatment and being transferred to intensive care at the Evelina London Children’s Hospital, the verdict said.

‌



Mia’s parents, Adrian and Chanel, said they will "never forget" they daughter who "was and is deeply loved". In a statement, they said: "We would like to thank the coroner for her careful and thorough investigation into the death of our beautiful daughter, Mia.

“We are grateful for the time and attention given to understanding what happened and for ensuring that Mia’s voice has been heard. We are convinced that significant changes are needed to protect people living with food allergies.

"Consumers rely on food hygiene ratings when deciding where it is safe to eat, but they do not tell us anything about the way a food business runs allergy management systems. There should be a separate, clearly displayed rating dedicated to allergy management, like the food hygiene rating.

‌



"This would mean that people with allergies could make informed choices about where they eat. For families living with food allergies, eating out should not mean they are at risk.

"We hope that lessons will be learned from Mia’s death and that changes will be made to prevent other families enduring the devastation that we now have to live with. No family should ever have to lose a child in these circumstances.

"If the local authority had ensured that the café’s allergy management responsibilities had been properly understood, and put into practice, we believe Mia would still be alive today. We want to make sure that change is Mia’s legacy so that we can help to save lives in the future.

‌



"Mia was, and is, deeply loved and she will never be forgotten." A case was brought against the café by Southwark Council who said in January 2025 that Yucel had pleaded guilty to all six offences in the case.

These included not making allergen advice available or visible to consumers, failing to manage allergen contamination during the food production process, and serving food that contained an allergenic ingredient that was not supposed to be present. Yucel was fined £18,000 and handed a 100-hour community order.

Michelle Victor, partner at law firm Leigh Day, which represents Mia’s parents, said the evidence has highlighted "serious concerns" about the way food allergies are understood, managed and monitored within the food service industry.

‌



She said: "Mia’s death demonstrates the potentially catastrophic consequences that can arise when allergy management systems are not robustly implemented, monitored and enforced. The family therefore call upon the Food Standards Agency and relevant authorities to review the current framework governing food allergy safety and consider meaningful reforms."

Tanya Ednan-Laperouse, who founded Natasha’s Foundation after her daughter died aged 15 from an allergy to sesame in a Pret baguette, said food allergen regulations "should be as important as food hygiene". She said: "The inquest into Mia’s death illustrates just how far we still have to go to improve awareness, understanding and regulation of food allergies.

"Food allergies are not a preference or a choice, they are a serious, unpredictable medical condition which for some, like Mia, can be fatal. Everyone has a responsibility to keep people with food allergies safe – families, schools, workplaces, cafes and restaurants, regulators and government…

Article continues below

"Natasha’s Foundation is working hard with business, schools, communities and the Government to increase awareness and understanding of food allergies to try to prevent other families from having to go through the terrible loss that Mia’s family endure.

"Food allergen regulations should be as important as food hygiene. Yet the current different systems for monitoring food allergen are inadequate."

News.title: Locals who saw filming for new Robson Green TV show 'thought it was police at a real life crime'
News.content:
Locals who saw filming for new Robson Green TV show 'thought it was police at a real life crime'

Exclusive: Green was filming in Alnwick - often voted as one of the best places to live in Britain - when locals became concerned. They contacted local council officials when police cars were seen in scenes for "The Northumbria Mysteries".

They contacted local council officials when "police vehicles" were seen as Green filmed "The Northumbria Mysteries".

News.title: UK facing 'genuine emergency' as racism and hate crimes against Muslims and Jews soar
News.content:
UK facing 'genuine emergency' as racism and hate crimes against Muslims and Jews soar

Harrowing figures show nearly 150,000 hate crimes were reported to police in England and Wales in the year to March 2026 - a 7% rise in a year, with racism and religious-based hatred on the rise

View 2 Images Police at the scene of last year's synagogue attack in Manchester (Image: PA)

Harrowing figures show racist and religious-based hate crimes have hit record levels as campaigners warn of a national emergency.

‌



‌



Stark data reveals overall hate crimes went up by 7% in England and Wales in the year to March, with four in 10 involving violence. This included a 9% rise in race hate crimes and a 13% increase in victims being targeted because of their religion.

‌



There was a 15% rise in hate crimes directed at Muslims and 10% aimed at Jews. Sabby Dhalu, Stand up to Racism Co-Convenor, told The Mirror: “Sadly, it is no surprise that race and religious hate crimes increased in the year ending March 2026.

‌



"This period coincided with a summer of hate targeting hotels housing asylum seekers, with politicians either openly supporting these demonstrations or conceding to the pressure they generated, culminating in the largest far-right demonstration in British history.

“These figures confirm two things. First, when politicians fan the flames of hatred, it has consequences on the ground. Secondly, racism directed at one community can create a climate in which other communities are targeted too.

“That is why we all have a responsibility to stand in solidarity with any community facing racism and hatred, and to unite against racism, Islamophobia and antisemitism. We cannot allow hatred directed at one community to become normalised, because ultimately it threatens us all.”

‌



Andy Burnham revives Labour as Greens and Reform battle conference chaos READ MORE :

Draconian rules tying migrant workers to abusive bosses finally ripped up READ MORE :

View 2 Images Policing Minister Sarah Jones said the rise in hate crimes will not be tolerated

Ilyas Nagdee, racial justice lead at Amnesty International UK said: “The shocking rise in hate crimes show that racism, violence and fear are tragically becoming a day-to-day reality across the UK.

"Behind these statistics are stories of children who are afraid to go to school, families who are scared to leave home and communities divided. When there are over 10,000 racially or religiously aggravated offences record in a single month, and hate crimes are increasing in double digits year on year, we are in a genuine emergency.

‌



"The UK government must act now and resource hate crime investigations to cut down the delays present between hate and non-hate offences, hold perpetrators to account, and send an unambiguous message that racism and all forms of hate will not be tolerated."

The Home Office data showed there were 146,825 hate crimes recorded by police in England and Wales, of which 107,926 were linked to race. A further 11,419 were motivated by religious - with 5,132 directed at Muslims and 3,162 at Jews.

In October last year two British Jews, Adrian Daulby and Melvin Cravitz, were killed in a terror attack at Heaton Park Synagogue in Manchester. In the 12 months to March there were 117 police-recorded religious hate crimes targeted at Jewish people per 10,000 population - the highest rate for any religious group. The next highest rate was for religious hate crimes targeted at Muslims, with 13 per 10,000 population.

‌



Just 10% of hate crimes resulted in a charge or summons, the figures show. Outside of London, religious and racial hatred incidents are at their highest levels since records began in March 2014, the Home Office said.

Policing Minister Sarah Jones said: "These numbers offer a stark warning that hatred continues to blight our communities, both online and on the streets.

“This government will not tolerate people being targeted by threats and violence simply for being who they are. We fully support a robust response from police to any reports of hate crime."

‌



The figures show there were 21,407 sexual orientation hate crimes recorded by police - down 1%. Disability hate crime cases fell by 5% and transgender hate dropped by 4%, but questions have been raised about the data.

Rose Simkins, chief executive of Stop Hate UK, said: "I think we are in bleak times. The positive we always take from it is that people are coming forward, which is good. But we believe there are many, many more incidents that are never reported and never recorded by the police.

"We're not surprised that obviously race and faith have increased with the current climate. I've been in a meeting this morning where people are reporting, that the term 'get out of my country' is being used more and more to people.

Article continues below

"And going back more than 20 years, that was something that was often said to people. And I know of a 17-year-old who tried to die by suicide as a result of just hearing those words. So they really resonate with people and cause considerable harm.

"I'm not surprised that those figures have gone up. I think there is a bigger problem than the figures reflect."

Ms Simkins continued: "The other aspect that really concerns us is the decrease in disability and transgender hate crime figures, because our interactions with trans people do not reflect a reduction in incidents. They're basically living in fear and experiencing many, many incidents."

News.title: Police accept Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor search warrants were unlawful, court hears
News.content:
Thames Valley Police has accepted that the search warrants it used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes earlier this year were unlawful, the High Court has heard.

The force said it accepted the "initial court's decision to issue warrants under the specific piece of legislation used was incorrect" when they were given permission to search the former prince's properties on 18 February.

Andrew was arrested by Thames Valley Police on suspicion of misconduct in public office the day after. He denies any wrongdoing.

The investigation is ongoing and the items seized in the raids on his homes in Norfolk and Berkshire will remain in police custody while his legal challenge over the material taken continues.

They have used a judicial review to challenge the actions of the chief constable of the force and the Central Criminal Court.

His arrest in February arose after the US Department of Justice published documents which suggested he had forwarded confidential information to the convicted sex offender when Mountbatten-Windsor was a UK trade envoy in 2010.

He has consistently denied any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein.

The court heard on Thursday that Thames Valley Police took possession of documents and electronic devices when they raided Andrew's homes.

The conditions for the warrants were that there had to be reasonable grounds for believing that any documents used for business or in a paid or unpaid role in which an undertaking of confidence had been given should not be seized.

Thames Valley Police now admits the judge who granted the warrants could not have been sure of this.

A Thames Valley Police spokesperson said: "The agreement that led to the quashing of the warrants relates specifically to a decision made by the court regarding the legal basis for these and is not a judgement on our ongoing investigation.

"We ensured the court was presented with all the necessary information and paperwork to inform their decision, following the correct legal processes throughout.

"We accept the position that the initial court's decision to issue warrants under the specific piece of legislation used was incorrect and therefore these must be legally quashed.

"Legal proceedings are currently ongoing to decide how material seized during the searches will be managed and whether we can lawfully retain it in support of our ongoing investigation."

The force said its "investigation into alleged misconduct in public office by a man in his 60s from Norfolk remains ongoing, and we continue to pursue all reasonable lines of enquiry to effectively and fairly progress this investigation".

News.title: Royal Navy sailor in court accused of preparing to spy for Russia
News.content:
A junior Royal Navy sailor accused of preparing to spy for Russia has appeared in court.

Able Seaman Teddy Young, who specialised in warfare intelligence, allegedly retained UK defence and intelligence material that he had access to and made preparations to disclose sensitive information, a court was told.

The 24-year-old appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday after being charged under the National Security Act.

The BBC understands that the allegations against Young include translating a message into Russian and looking for a web portal that invited people to submit information to Russia.

Wearing a police-issue grey sweatshirt, Young spoke in court to confirm his name, date of birth and his address in Clapham, near Bedford.

He is formally charged with engaging in conduct in preparation for disclosing protected information, and obtaining, copying, recording or retaining protected information, intending the conduct to benefit a foreign power.

The charges cover a period between 26 November 2024 and 21 May 2025.

"The allegation is that while serving as a Royal Navy warfare intelligence rating with high level security clearance and intelligence-system access, Teddy Stanley Greenidge Young accessed and retained sensitive UK defence and intelligence material and engaged in activity consistent with preparing to pass protected information to a foreign power," the Crown Prosecution Service told the court in a written summary of the allegations.

Police said the alleged offences were not related to the recent RAF Fairford incident that resulted in a number of arrests after suspicious activity was reported near the base.

In total, seven men have been arrested and later released on bail in connection with the incident, which is being investigated by counter-terror police.

Young was arrested at his home address in Bedfordshire on Tuesday.

He is the first member of the armed forces to be charged under the new National Security Act 2023.

Cdr Helen Flanagan, head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, said: "These are very serious charges against a serving member of the armed forces.

"We have worked extremely closely with relevant operational colleagues within the Ministry of Defence as our investigation has progressed to ensure appropriate measures could be taken to mitigate any potential risks linked to this matter."

A Royal Navy spokesperson confirmed a service member had been charged and added: "As legal proceedings are ongoing, it would be inappropriate to comment further at this stage."

Judge Annabel Pilling remanded Young in custody. He will next appear at the Old Bailey on 16 October.

News.title: Three sisters who drowned in sea off Brighton took own lives, inquest finds
News.content:
Three sisters who drowned in the sea off Brighton took their own lives, a coroner has ruled.

Jane Adetoro, 36, Christina Walters, 32, and Rebecca Walters, 31, had been living "very secluded lives" following the death of their mother, who drowned in 2010, senior coroner Penelope Schofield said.

On 11 May, the women - who had all been living together in Greenford, London - visited an area of Birmingham close to where their mother died before travelling the next day to Brighton beach, where they drowned in adverse sea conditions in the early hours of 13 May. The coroner said they could not swim.

Their father Joseph Jacobsen said it was heartbreaking to lose "all three of my precious daughters".

He was among family members who followed proceedings via video link.

In an emotional statement read out on his behalf, he said he watched his daughters grow from little girls to beautiful, intelligent women "with a special place in my heart".

He said: "There are no words that can adequately express the pain of losing a child.

"To lose all three of my precious daughters is a heartbreak beyond anything I could ever have imagined."

He could not understand why his daughters' lives ended so suddenly, and hoped they were reunited with their mother "in God's eternal care", he added.

If you are experiencing emotional stress, help and support is available via the BBC Action Line here.

The coroner told the court: "These three sisters lived very secluded lives, they were incredibly private, we don't know why they took this course of action or indeed why they chose to do it in Brighton.

"It is not for the court to speculate and sadly these reasons may never be known."

News.title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds
News.content:
Asos has told its customers that hackers are in possession of detailed profiles of potentially millions of the online store's users.

It issued the update after BBC News told the retailer it had been contacted by cyber criminals who said this week's breach went beyond the "basic contact details" Asos previously said might have been accessed.

Names, addresses, phone numbers, emails and customer numbers are now in the hands of cyber criminals.

So too are the searches customers have made on the website. Terms like "reclaimed vintage", "glamorous wide fit" and "Asos petite" are visible in the data.

With this information, scammers may be able to craft potent phishing attack emails or phone calls.

The risk to individuals is now higher and customers are being warned about potential impersonation scams.

In its email to customers, Asos confirmed data profiles were taken but said no bank details or passwords were accessed.

"Please remain cautious of unexpected messages or calls claiming to be from Asos," it said.

"We will never ask you to share passwords, security codes or payment details through an unsolicited message or call."

The company did not respond to questions about the scale of the breach.

The high profile hack made global headlines on Tuesday when cyber criminals used Asos's own app system to send a pop up notification to potentially millions of people.

Later that day the firm confirmed to shareholders via the London Stock Exchange that the pop up was sent by an "unauthorised third party" and "basic personal information including name and contact details may have been accessed."

The company then sent an email to customers with similar wording.

On Wednesday evening the cyber criminals responsible contacted the BBC sharing a sample of the stolen data which showed the true extent of the hack.

The BBC held off publishing this article to allow Asos to contact its customers first.

News.title: Watch: Why was the sign at the British consulate in East Jerusalem removed?
News.content:
Israel said in September it would shut the British consulate, in retaliation for UK sanctions on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank which are illegal under international law.

The UK government had made last-ditch efforts to persuade Israel not to close the building ahead of Thursday's deadline, after the Israeli government said it would close the consulate within 30 days of the UK sanctions announcement.

Most diplomats will leave the British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem, Israel says, but the UK insists the building "will not be closing", and will operate as a "UK Mission".

The BBC's Middle East correspondent Yolande Knell says the UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband "sees this as being a good outcome".

The consulate is distinct from the UK embassy in Tel Aviv, which is the UK's main diplomatic hub with Israel.

More on changes at British consulate in East Jerusalem

News.title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings
News.content:
The family of a 12-year-old girl who died after drinking a milkshake made in an unwashed blender at a cafe have called for a dedicated rating that scores food businesses on their allergy management.

Mia St Hilaire, who had a tree nut allergy, suffered an anaphylactic shock and died after she drank a Twix milkshake at the Pop Inn Cafe in Bermondsey, south-east London, in August 2023.

Her order contained hazelnut residue because the blender had not been washed after a Kinder Bueno milkshake was made in it beforehand, an inquest concluded on Thursday.

In a statement, her family said "significant changes" were needed to protect people with food allergies.

In January 2025, the cafe was fined Â£18,000 and its proprietor Baris Yucel was given 100 hours of community service after admitting six criminal charges related to the Food Safety Act.

These included not making allergen advice available or visible to consumers, failing to manage allergen contamination during the food production process, and serving food that contained an allergenic ingredient that was not supposed to be present.

CCTV evidence showed that Yucel had not cleaned the blender before preparing Mia's milkshake.

News.title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows
News.content:
There are "ominous signs" that winter pressures are already affecting the NHS in England, according to senior health leaders.

The warning comes as new data reveals the waiting list for routine hospital treatment in England rose for the second month in a row.

An estimated 7.37 million treatments were waiting to be carried out at the end of August, relating to 6.24 million patients.

The numbers are the highest since October 2025 and have raised questions over whether the NHS will meet a government target of treating 92% of patients within 18 weeks by 2029.

The rise in waiting lists comes despite the NHS in England delivering what were described as record levels of planned, elective care over the summer, while demand for services also reached its highest level ever.

A record 4.7 million planned treatments, procedures and appointments occurred across June, July and August â more than in any previous summer.

But both A&Es and ambulance services also saw a record number of patients for the month of September.

NHS England's national medical director, Professor Frankie Swords, warned that despite the progress delivered by frontline teams, winter pressure was already building.

"Staff are already seeing the ominous early signs of pressure, with more patients coming to A&E with flu and other respiratory viruses than usual for this time of year, and unfortunately many people are still waiting longer than we would like them to," she said.

News.title: 'Bold and inventive' Canadian poet Anne Carson wins Nobel Literature Prize
News.content:
Canadian poet, essayist and translator Anne Carson has been awarded this year's Nobel Prize in Literature.

Carson, 76, is celebrated for works that often cross the boundaries between poetry, fiction and scholarship.

The Nobel Prize committee said they had selected her "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature".

The Nobel Prize is awarded for a lifetime's body of work and is regarded as the most prestigious award in global literature, with the winner receiving 12 million Swedish kronor (Â£900,000, $1.2m).

News.title: UK and Germany will face threats together, says Burnham in Berlin
News.content:
The UK and Germany will face threats together, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said as he reaffirmed a series of defence and security partnerships.

On his first official European trip, apart from visits to Ukraine, Burnham met German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, and was greeted with military honours in Berlin.

Speaking to reporters at the German capital's Federal Chancellery, the prime minister said both countries were facing hybrid attacks "on a regular basis" and "it makes sense" to take them on together.

The pair formally ratified the 2025 Kensington Treaty, a partnership committing both countries to tackle hostile activity.

Burnham said the treaty would "improve our security here in Europe" but also help grow the economy and living standards.

He added that the UK government would now "seek to progress" Germany joining Gcap, the Global Combat Air Programme led by Italy, Japan and the UK to develop a next-generation fighter aircraft.

He outlined partnerships "countering hybrid attacks" and "countering interference in our democratic processes".

He mentioned collaboration on quantum technology and space, adding he was aiming to host the first joint meeting of the UK and German cabinets next year.

The Berlin talks come after intelligence services warned of rising threats, including last month when Germany accused Russia of launching a drone fitted with explosives at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

News.title: 'Come all the way' back to EU, French finance minister tells UK
News.content:
French finance minister Roland Lescure has invited Britain to "come all the way" back to the EU, after Prime Minister Andy Burnham signalled a second Brexit referendum was "possible" in a future Labour election manifesto.

Lescure said being in the bloc comes with some difficulties, but it enables members to better address the challenges facing the world.

Last week, Burnham said the UK needed to "consider the options", ranging from staying as is, rejoining the customs union or single market, or going "all the way".

Asked about the PM's comments, Lescure told the BBC: "British people decided, and that's obviously their 100% right, and if they're willing to come back, they will have to decide."

He added: "But what I can tell them is: come back, anytime."

Burnham recently warned that planned EU rules to help European manufacturers would damage the UK.

The prime minister expressed concerns about how British industry and supply chains could be affected by the planned Made In Europe scheme.

The proposals aim to protect EU industry from Chinese competitors by giving companies inside the bloc priority for public contracts and subsidies. The EU's car industry has called for the UK to be included to prevent disruption to its own supply chains.

Asked about the possibility of Britain being kept out of the scheme, Lescure said: "Come back, and you'll be at the table, and we discuss all these things together."

News.title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab
News.content:
A former councillor has been found guilty of running a bogus coronavirus testing laboratory during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Faisal Shoukat, who served on Calderdale Council, was convicted of causing public nuisance, fraudulent trading and money laundering after a trial at Bradford Crown Court.

Four other people on trial alongside Shoukat - former justice minister Shahid Malik, Lynn Connell, Paul Moore and Dr Alexander Zarneh - were cleared of any wrongdoing.

The verdicts were returned by His Honour Judge Chris Smith after the jury was discharged in April during their deliberations, when one member of the panel was arrested on suspicion of conspiring to pervert the course of justice.

Judge Smith criticised a catalogue of "systemic failures" at the business, for which Shoukat was responsible for the day-to-day running, telling the court: "The overriding thought at the time was simply to make money.

"Put simply, profit was put before professionalism and public safety."

RT Diagnostics was set up in March 2021 with Shoukat and Mr Malik named among the directors, after the government invited private companies to help meet the demand for testing, including so-called 'Fit-to-Fly' tests.

Prosecutors said 39-year-old Shoukat - who was a Labour councillor at the time - was the "controlling mind" of the Halifax-based firm.

However, the court heard that test kits sent out to customers - sourced from Turkey - did not meet the required standards in the UK.

It was also said the lab had returned a "suspiciously low" number of positive tests.

Between May and July 2021 it reported 138,738 tests, but only 45 of these were positive, with 123,058 showing as negative and one indeterminate.

News.title: Husband accused of GP murder appears at Crown Court
News.content:
The husband of a GP who was found dead at her home has appeared before a Crown Court, charged with her murder.

The body of 45-year-old Hannah Cain, known to her patients as Dr Hannah Terry, was found at a property in Fern Hill, Dersingham, Norfolk, on Sunday.

Mark Cain, 45, also of Fern Hill, was charged with murder on Tuesday.

Appearing via video link from HMP Norwich, he spoke only to confirm his name and that he understood proceedings at King's Lynn Crown Court. He was remanded in custody until a plea hearing on 3 December.

Steven Ball, prosecuting, said Mark Cain was accused of the murder of his wife on 3 October into the early hours of 4 October at their family home.

He said emergency services attended and Hannah Cain was found "unconscious and unresponsive".

A post-mortem examination recorded that she had sustained "blunt force injuries to the head" and "neck injuries consistent with compression to the neck", he said.

News.title: Seventh man bailed in connection with RAF Fairford incident
News.content:
A 22-year-old British national who was arrested on suspicion of preparing acts of terror in connection with an incident close to RAF Fairford has been released on bail.

The man was arrested in Westminster, London, under Section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006 on Tuesday, as part of the counter-terror police investigation into the incident near the airbase in Gloucestershire.

In total, seven men - all in their 20s - have been arrested and later bailed in connection with the incident. No one has been charged.

A major incident was declared and dozens of homes were evacuated after police were alerted to three suspicious vehicles near the airbase in the early hours of 27 September.

Five men, aged between 23 and 25, were initially arrested on the day of the incident after vehicles were reported near the base.

They were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing an act of terror.

A sixth man, a 25-year-old dual Iranian-British national, was arrested on 1 October in Westminster. The seventh man, a 22-year-old British national, was arrested in Westminster on Tuesday by counter-terror police.

Both were arrested on suspicion of preparing an act of terror.

RAF Fairford, near the village of Whelford, has been used by the US Air Force for decades.

In recent months, the US has flown B-1 and B-52 bombers from the base to the Middle East, after the UK approved a request for Fairford to be used for defensive strikes against Iran.

But on Sunday, it emerged the US had pulled its bombers out of the base and returned them to America.

US President Donald Trump said the aircraft were removed due to "some threats" to the base without giving specific details.

"There were some threats. And rather than tempting the enemy, we'll capture the enemy and beat the enemy," he told reporters.

"But why should we leave them there? So we moved them around a little bit. Not very far."

Prior to Trump's intervention, a No 10 spokesperson had insisted RAF Fairford was safe and pointed to the US president's previous comments, where he praised the UK's "police, defence and security services" in relation to the base.

News.title: UK bluefin tuna comeback shows nature can recover, says WWF
News.content:
Bluefin tuna have returned in huge numbers off the British coast after almost disappearing from UK waters.

The return of the giant predatory fish is one of several wildlife recoveries highlighted in a major new report from WWF, which it says shows conservation can work.

However, the Living Planet Report 2026 also found that monitored wildlife populations around the world have fallen by an average of 73% since 1970.

The wildlife conservation charity said nature remains in "freefall" but it called the report one of hope.

"It's not too late," Mike Barrett, chief scientific adviser at WWF-UK, told the BBC.

News.title: 'Bendy tree' named UK Tree of the Year
News.content:
A "bendy" wych elm has been crowned the UK's Tree of the Year 2026 - the first time a tree in Northern Ireland has won the title.

The 150-year-old tree on the central promenade in Newcastle, County Down took more than 30% of the national public vote.

The theme of the Woodland Trust's annual competition was Against All Odds, with trees across the UK shortlisted for being impressive, beautiful and sometimes baffling examples of how nature can survive adversity.

The trust's Northern Ireland director John Martin said he had been rooting for the "whimsical" tree to win and said tens of thousands of people across the UK had clearly felt the same.

"It's a great testament to the resilience of nature."

News.title: Holborn and St Pancras by-election gets under way
News.content:
Voting is under way in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election as candidates from across the political spectrum vie to become its new MP.

About 30 polling stations - at churches and community centres - in the north London constituency opened at 07:00 BST and will close at 22:00, when a count will begin.

The seat became vacant after former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer announced he was standing down to focus on a role in international affairs.

Some 15 candidates are standing in the by-election, one of whom is an independent.

Voters will need to show a form of acceptable ID - such as a driving licence or passport - to be able to vote.

Who are the candidates up for election? Read the full list here.
