Here, he notes an early research done by a prophetic teacher in America, stating that some US presidents elected in years ending in zero died before completing their terms, either through assassination or sudden natural death.

The cases are well documented:

Abraham Lincoln, elected 1860, assassinated 1865; James Garfield, elected 1880, assassinated 1881; William McKinley, re-elected 1900, died 1901; John F Kennedy, elected 1960, died 1963.

After Kennedy, no president died in office despite the assasination attempt made on Ronald Reagan, elected in 1980, another year ending in zero. But Reagan’s story took a different turn. According to Dr Perry Stone, someone within Ronald Reagan’s inner circle had been made aware of this prophetic pattern in the aftermath of Kennedy’s assassination. Rather than dismiss it, Reagan’s administration responded with urgency: intercessors were mobilised, prayer was organised even within the White House, and the curse was confronted head-on in the spirit realm, and broken.

Reagan survived two full terms. He was even shot, and still he survived. In fact, after he was shot, one of the intercessors who knew about the “curse of the zero” year was so terrified. But their prayers saved the president’s life.

Dr Perry Stone calls this recurring phenomenon the “zero-curse year.”

The implications for Nigeria are direct and sobering. There are spiritual dimensions to the destiny of nations that no amount of political engineering can override. Nigeria is not exempt from this reality. If anything, Nigeria is one of the most contested spiritual territories on earth. Jihadists, US, UK, Russian, and French imperialists, all have strategic interests in the oil and natural resources rich African nation.

As Nigeria marks sixty-six years of independence, there is very little to celebrate when measured against a standard of genuine excellence. And excellence must be the measure. You do not determine greatness by comparing yourself to mediocrity. You measure yourself against the best, and by that standard, Nigeria has not yet arrived.

Ancient Forces, One Nation

Nigeria is not simply a political problem. It is a deeply contested spiritual battleground, and it has been for generations.

From the advancing forces of Jihad, to the lingering tendrils of the British imperial system, to other highly organised demonic structures with centuries-old interests in this land, multiple forces are actively competing for the soul of one nation. Every Nigerian with genuine spiritual discernment must therefore direct their energy not only toward political solutions but toward understanding and confronting the spiritual root systems that have made those political solutions perpetually elusive.

Nigeria is a deeply religious nation. Its transformation cannot bypass the role of faith and spiritual values. No nation rises above the ceiling of its dominant spiritual climate. While Nigeria is constitutionally a secular state with deeply polarised religious communities, we need not impose a single religion on the nation. What we must do is rigorously examine the values that each faith tradition brings to the table, and collectively commit to the supernatural belief system that most powerfully advances equity, transparency, and genuine national development. If we solve for the spiritual, the political will begin to yield.

The DNA of a Nation Born in Chains

The political instability, the corruption, the ethnic tension; none of it is accidental. To understand Nigeria’s present, we must reckon honestly with its birth.

Let us ask the question plainly: Can you nurture a nation from infancy to adulthood without understanding its spiritual and natural lineage?

Nigeria, Who Gave Birth to You?

You were born from the womb of the British Empire — not out of love, not out of vision for your people, but as the product of economic transactions among greedy imperialists. Your very foundation was constructed on the doctrine of divide-and-rule: the deliberate merging of vastly different ethnic, cultural, and religious peoples into a single state, not to unite them, but to ensure that their divisions would make them permanently manageable and perpetually dependent.

This strategy is not unique in history. It bears a troubling resemblance to the apparatus of Nazi Germany, where division was weaponised as a tool of control. Hitler’s propaganda machinery, led by the notorious Dr Joseph Goebbels, was engineered to create a German society incapable of distinguishing truth from deception. As Dr Erwin Lutzer defines it, propaganda is “the intelligent manipulation of the masses.” Goebbels did not eliminate truth, he buried it beneath layers of orchestrated narrative, sacrificing the welfare of ordinary people to preserve the establishment.

George Orwell captured the same dynamic with devastating precision: “They don’t solve problems, they use them.”

Nigeria’s story is a variation of the same script. Her vast resources have been systematically plundered, first by imperialists, and then by their locally trained successors: the political elite, the entrenched establishment, the corrupt gatekeepers of power who have learnt to profit from the nation’s dysfunction. In this environment, misinformation has become the preferred currency of governance. As Dr Lutzer soberly observed, “The media does not just disseminate information, it alters the consciences of entire generations.”

Nigeria’s media, which should serve as an independent arbiter of truth, has been substantially compromised, leaving ordinary citizens adrift in a sea of competing narratives, unable to locate solid ground.

Sixty-Six Years and Still Waiting to Rise

As Nigeria marks sixty-six years of independence, there is very little to celebrate when measured against a standard of genuine excellence. And excellence must be the measure. You do not determine greatness by comparing yourself to mediocrity. You measure yourself against the best, and by that standard, Nigeria has not yet arrived.

A nation that still cannot guarantee consistent electricity. A nation where clean water is a luxury rather than a right. A nation where the security of life and property remains fragile. A nation where fuel prices, food prices, and housing costs have become unbearable burdens for the average family, such a nation cannot, in good conscience, declare herself great.

She is great in potential. But potential does not fix roads. Potential does not feed children. Sustained, courageous action does.

The battle for Nigeria must be fought on two fronts simultaneously: politically and spiritually. To fight on only one front is to fight with one hand tied behind your back. Nigeria’s redemption is possible. But it will require the full surrender of both our ballot and our altar. Happy 66th birthday to my beloved Nigeria!

There is a passage in Scripture that I believe speaks directly to Nigeria’s past, present, and the promise of its future. It is found in Isaiah 66:7–9:

“Before she was in labour, she gave birth; before her pain came, she delivered a male child. Who has heard such a thing? Who has seen such things? Shall the earth be made to give birth in one day? Or shall a nation be born at once? For as soon as Zion was in labour, she gave birth to her children. Shall I bring to the time of birth, and not cause delivery?” says the Lord. “Shall I who cause delivery shut up the womb?” Says your God.

This is the blueprint, from labour pains to delivery. If God Himself has brought Nigeria to its time of birth, He is fully committed to causing it to deliver. The promise is irrevocable.

But the condition is equally clear: the gods that have entrenched themselves in Nigeria, chief among them the god of greed, which has taken deep root in the hearts of many politicians and far too many religious leaders, must be systematically uprooted. A nation cannot deliver under the authority of a false god.

The Church Must Lead, Or Step Aside

As followers of Jesus Christ, we carry a responsibility that extends far beyond the walls of our sanctuaries. The Bible is unambiguous: contentment is a virtue; greed is a sin at its root. The church of Christ in Nigeria must therefore lead the spiritual revolution of this nation, not through rhetoric, but through the visible, verifiable modeling of the values of Jesus Christ.

These values must govern how we run our churches, how we conduct our ministries, how Christians engage in politics, how Christian professionals operate in the marketplace, and how church leaders steward the platforms entrusted to them. This is what it truly means to be the light of the world.

When the church operates with this kind of moral authority, she earns the credibility to unite people across divides, to pray with genuine spiritual power, to engage political parties and candidates with discernment, and to advance sound moral values that weaken and subdue the wicked spiritual forces that are actively working for Nigeria’s destruction.

Dr Tony Evans said it precisely: “When conscience dies in a nation, truth becomes the first casualty.”

And we must equally remember: a nation is not great because of the value of its wealth. It is great because of the wealth of its values, values that are both spiritual and natural.

A Word to the Advocates and Fighters

I want to close by honouring every Nigerian, at home and in the diaspora, who has refused to give up on this nation. Those who daily defy threats, intimidation, and danger to lawfully advocate for truth, freedom, fairness, equity, and justice. Your courage is not unseen. It is not unimportant.

But I must also urge you to remember this: Nigeria’s problems are not only political and economic.

They carry deep, far-reaching spiritual dimensions that can only be decisively addressed by a superior spiritual force; one wielded by men and women with an unwavering commitment to righteousness, and above all, to the Lord Jesus Christ. This is where the Nigerian church is most urgently needed.

The battle for Nigeria must be fought on two fronts simultaneously: politically and spiritually. To fight on only one front is to fight with one hand tied behind your back. Nigeria’s redemption is possible. But it will require the full surrender of both our ballot and our altar. Happy 66th birthday to my beloved Nigeria!

Ayo Akerele is the senior pastor of Rhema Assembly and the founder of the Voice of the Watchmen Ministries in Ontario, Canada. He can be reached through [email protected]. You can connect with him on: YouTube: @VoiceoftheWatchmen, TikTok: @drayoakerele, Instagram: @drayoakerele, Facebook: @Ayo Akerele

World.title: How IBBU students are rebuilding campus journalism
World.content:
For two days in early July, dozens of student journalists gathered at the ICT Centre at Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida University (IBBU), Lapai, Niger State, for a capacity-building workshop.

They learnt the fundamentals of news writing, investigative reporting, inclusive reporting, hyperlocal journalism, and digital storytelling through the Next Gen Campus Reporter Clinic, organised by the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID).

But beyond notebooks, presentations, and newsroom simulations, another story was unfolding quietly.

For many of the students, the training represented something bigger than learning how to write better stories. It marked the beginning of an effort to breathe life back into the university’s Union of Campus Journalists (UCJ), a body whose activities had dwindled over the years despite a growing population of Mass Communication students.

“When I joined, there wasn’t much activity,” the UCJ president, Beauty Brendan, recalled.

“Most students focused on their academics, and the union wasn’t functioning the way it should.”

The UCJ IBBUL Chapter was created in 2020, with support from the National Union of Campus Journalists (NUCJ), then headed by Ibrahim Adeyemi. The then President of the Mass Communication Students’ Association (MACOSA), Yakubu Mohammed, invited NUCJ to conduct training and to launch UCJ on the campus.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The pioneer president of the UCJ was Zainab Abdullahi, said Mr Mohammed, now an investigative journalist with PREMIUM TIMES.

But the union has struggled to stay afloat since the first set of members left campus.

“All the presidents and vice presidents the union has had were appointed when they were in their penultimate years. This made continuity a problem, because the moment the top executives left, a vacuum set in, leaving their successors and members in some sort of confusion,” said Mr Mohammed.

Ms Brendan believes that inactivity of the UCJ has created an information vacuum on campus.

“We don’t have a reliable source of verified information,” she said. “That’s one of the reasons we’re trying to revive the union.”

Why campus journalism matters

Her concerns are shared by the department’s Staff Adviser, Andrew Ngele, who argues that campus journalism is far more than a student extracurricular activity.

“A university is like a small city within a larger society,” Mr Ngele said. “The role journalism plays here is no different from the role it plays outside the campus.”

According to him, a vibrant campus journalism union creates a culture of transparency by allowing students to question decisions affecting their welfare and the university community.

Mr Yakubu, one of the patrons of the university’s UCJ, said he then advised the outgoing executives to use students in the first and second years as executives so they have more time to grow the association.

He said the patrons and lecturers continue to train them as they look out for successors either in 100 or 200 level.

“We adopted a catch-them-young approach,” he said.

“That strategy started with this current set, and honestly it has been working. They now have a Substack handle, social media accounts where they share news and other content.”

Referencing Section 22 of Nigeria’s Constitution, which assigns the press the responsibility of holding the government accountable, Mr Ngele said student journalists should see themselves as contributors to accountability within the university.

“If there are issues around infrastructure, student welfare, or the use of public resources, students should be able to ask questions,” he said. “Campus journalism creates that space.”

A new generation of student reporters

For students like Deborah Lukman, that message resonated immediately.

Ms Lukman had stumbled on the training after seeing a registration link shared on her departmental platform. Curious, she researched the programme and decided to apply.

“I’ve always wanted to become a journalist,” she said.

By the end of the two-day clinic, she said her understanding of the profession had changed completely.

“I thought investigative journalism was like what you see in movies,” she admitted with a laugh. “Now I understand there are ethical and professional ways of gathering information and uncovering stories.”

She already has several story ideas.

“I’m naturally curious,” she said. “I enjoy asking questions and helping people become aware of what’s happening around them. Journalism is not just about writing stories; it’s about serving the public interest.”

Challenges to reviving IBBUL UCJ

That curiosity, however, will need more than enthusiasm to survive.

Ms Brendan acknowledges that while students are willing to rebuild the UCJ, several obstacles stand in the way.

“The challenge isn’t that we don’t have ideas,” she explained. “We need stronger editorial skills, better equipment, and more support. Sometimes it’s even difficult getting members together because everyone is trying to balance academics with other responsibilities.”

These challenges reflect a broader concern within journalism education.

The President of the Mass Communication Students’ Association (MACOSA), Aminu Turaki, believes many students are attracted to journalism until they encounter the realities of the profession.

“Many students say they want to practise journalism,” Mr Turaki said. “But when they discover the amount of work involved in reporting, writing, editing, and verifying information, the enthusiasm begins to reduce.”

He noted that some students are drawn to the visibility associated with television and media personalities without appreciating the discipline that happens behind every published story.

To bridge that gap, the department has increasingly encouraged practical newsroom experience alongside classroom instruction, giving students opportunities to produce and publish stories while still in school.

“A vibrant UCJ gives students an independent platform to practise journalism before graduation,” he said.

Learning Journalism through practice

Mr Ngele believes those practical experiences are essential because journalism cannot be learnt solely from textbooks.

Students, he said, must learn to ask difficult questions, verify facts, and report responsibly, even when doing so feels uncomfortable.

“I understand why students may be afraid,” he said. “But intimidation is part of the profession. As long as your reporting is factual and motivated by public interest rather than malice, you should not be afraid to tell important stories.”

For the young reporters inside the ICT Centre, that lesson may prove to be the most enduring takeaway.

The clinic did more than teach inverted pyramids, interviewing techniques, or newsroom ethics. It challenged students to see journalism as a public service rather than merely a career path.

The beginning of a revival

By the close of the programme, conversations had shifted from note-taking to story ideas. Students were grouped into teams and were assigned to come up with story ideas on issues affecting their campus and the surrounding Lapai community.

Ms Brendan sees that renewed energy as the beginning of something bigger.

“If we continue applying what we’ve learnt here,” she said, “I believe UCJ can become a trusted platform for credible campus journalism.”

Whether that ambition materialises will depend on sustained mentorship, institutional support, and the determination of students willing to do the difficult work journalism demands.

But if the conversations inside IBBU’s ICT Centre are any indication, the revival of campus journalism has already begun, not with headlines, but with a generation of young reporters learning that the most important stories are often the ones closest to home.

World.title: Outrage as police operatives allegedly harass bailiffs enforcing court order
World.content:
The Anaocha Branch of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) has raised an alarm over alleged harassment of court bailiffs by police operatives in Anambra State.

Anaocha is a local government area in Anambra State.

Chairman of the NBA branch Uzoma Dioha in a statement on Thursday said the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) of B-Division in Awka allegedly instructed his operatives to harass the bailiffs while they were enforcing an order of the Chief Magistrate Court, Awka.

Mr Dioha, who condemned the alleged harassment, said the incident happened on Wednesday.

The chairman said the Chief Bailiff, Francis Nweje, informed him that the court officials were carrying out the “lawful execution of a judgement” pursuant to a warrant issued by the court when the DPO stormed the location.

The NBA branch leader said the police chief directed the court officials to immediately discontinue the execution and accompany him to his police station.

He said the court bailiffs explained to the DPO that they were acting pursuant to a valid warrant of execution and respectfully asked to conclude their court-assigned duties before attending to the officer’s directive.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Rather than allowing the judicial process to proceed, the said officer allegedly summoned police reinforcements, who arrived at the scene and reportedly subjected the court officials to harassment and intimidation,” he said.

Mr Dioha noted that the alleged harassment was captured in a video clip, stressing that the incident represents a grave affront to the judiciary.

“If these allegations are established, such conduct represents a grave affront to the authority of the judiciary and an unacceptable interference with the administration of justice,” he stated.

He argued that the 1999 Nigerian Constitution gives courts the authority to determine people’s civil rights and obligations, and it requires everyone, including government authorities and other courts, to respect, obey and enforce valid decisions made by the courts.

“The duties of court bailiffs, including the execution of warrants and other judicial processes, are governed by applicable laws and rules of court.

“Where a valid warrant of execution has been issued by a court of competent jurisdiction, no police officer, irrespective of rank or designation, possesses an unrestricted power to arbitrarily suspend its execution,” he stated.

“Any legitimate objection to the execution of a judgement must be addressed through appropriate legal and judicial procedures.”

Demands to the police

Mr Dioha said it was ironic that those who were expected to enforce a court order were the people obstructing its enforcement.

He said the NBA, as a body, has asked the commissioner of police in the state to immediately investigate the incident, and identify as well as punish the officers involved in the obstruction of court enforcement orders.

The chairman said the union also asked for adequate protection of court bailiffs carrying out lawful judicial assignments.

He said the body has equally asked for “an appropriate institutional apology” to the judiciary and the affected court officials.

“We shall continue to engage the appropriate authorities and advocate for accountability, institutional discipline and the protection of the judicial process,” he said.

Viral video clip

PREMIUM TIMES sighted a video clip of the incident.

In the clip which has gone viral on Facebook, one of the armed police operatives and another individual in plain cloth were seen grabbing a man said to be one of the court bailiffs in the entrance of what appeared to be a residential building.

The operatives continued to pull the court bailiff violently and appeared to force him into a waiting police vehicle but the court official repeatedly resisted.

“You’re harassing a court bailiff on official duty,” a male voice was heard repeatedly at the background of the clip.

One of the bailiffs was heard saying that they came to the area with a valid warrant to enforce the court order.

One of the officers was later spotted reading the court warrant which was handed to him by the bailiff.

Police react

The police in Anambra State have reacted to the incident.

In a statement on Thursday, the police spokesperson in the state, Tochukwu Ikenga, said the viral video clip of the incident only captured part of the encounter.

Mr Ikenga, a superintendent of police, said the state police command had begun an assessment of the incident with a view to establishing the facts.

The spokesperson, however, said preliminary information indicated that the operatives were responding to a distress call concerning the presence of “unidentified persons and a reported disturbance” at a premises within the jurisdiction of the command.

READ ALSO: Oyo police arrest three suspects over killing of six family members

“Upon arrival at the scene, the operatives met some individuals engaged in the eviction of persons and removal of properties from the premises.

“In the course of establishing the identities of the persons involved and the purpose of their activities, the officers approached them and requested appropriate identification.

“During the interaction, there was a disagreement between the Police Operatives and some of the persons present,” he said.

“The persons subsequently identified themselves as court bailiffs carrying out an enforcement exercise pursuant to a court order.”

Mr Ikenga said the police command, based on the earlier available information, was not previously approached for security assistance before the commencement of the enforcement exercise.

“Upon being informed that the persons were court bailiffs acting pursuant to a court order, the police operatives advised them on the appropriate procedure for requesting police security support during such enforcement exercises and subsequently withdrew from the scene,” he said.

The spokesperson said the police command has reiterated its respect for the authority and independence of the courts and remains committed to providing lawful security support for the enforcement of valid court orders.

“The command has nevertheless taken note of the concerns arising from the incident and has engaged the relevant parties as part of efforts to establish the complete facts and ensure that the matter is handled professionally, impartially and in accordance with the law,” he said.

“The Command will communicate further developments as necessary upon conclusion of the ongoing assessment,” the spokesperson assured, urging Nigerians not to reach hasty conclusions from video clips without full details.

World.title: Oyo govt expresses relief as abducted corps members regain freedom in Imo
World.content:
The Oyo State Government has expressed relief over the release of corps members from the state who were abducted in Imo State, describing their freedom as a welcome development.

Commissioner for Information and Civic Orientation, Dotun Oyelade, stated this in a statement issued on Wednesday evening in Ibadan, the state capital, shortly after the report of the release of the 20 prospective corps members.

Mr Oyelade congratulated the Imo and Oyo state governments as well as the federal government on the successful release of the corps members after being held in captivity.

He, however, urged the federal government to intensify efforts to tackle the persistent challenge of kidnapping and banditry across the country.

According to him, the federal government, which has the greatest power and capacity to effectively address the insecurity crisis, must be more proactive and live up to its promise of making Nigerians safer.

READ ALSO: Army takes over Old Oyo Park for military training in aftermath of school abduction

The commissioner said the release of the corps members was a development worthy of commendation, while stressing that more needed to be done to prevent similar incidents.

MR Oyelade urged relevant security agencies to intensify intelligence gathering and coordinated operations to rescue those still in captivity and prevent further abductions.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He reiterated the Oyo State government’s commitment to the safety and welfare of its citizens, particularly youths serving the nation under the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) scheme.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) recalls that gunmen ‌‍⁠⁠⁠‍⁠⁠‌⁠⁠⁠‍⁠⁠‌on, 1 October, abducted the 20 prospective corps members, travelling from Ibadan, on the Onitsha-Owerri expressway in Imo State.

(NAN)

World.title: Soludo sets up commission to end deadly intercommunal clash
World.content:
Governor Charles Soludo of Anambra State has set up a judicial commission of inquiry to tackle the deadly intercommunal clash between Amaeze Aguleri and Umuoba Anam in Anambra East Local Government Area of the state.

Mr Soludo set up the commission on Tuesday during a stakeholders meeting at the Government House in Awka, according to a statement on Wednesday by the governor’s spokesperson, Christian Aburime.

Mr Aburime said the commission was tasked with “thoroughly” examining all petitions, complaints, and historical grievances between the two warring communities.

“The commission was mandated to submit its comprehensive report within four months,” he said.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that at least five people have been killed, several houses razed and livelihoods destroyed in the violence that engulfed the communities.

The Anambra State Government earlier ordered the immediate closure of the Otuocha Market following the crisis.

Directive to security operatives

At the Tuesday meeting, Mr Soludo decried the tragic loss of lives and the widespread destruction of properties, emphasising that such lawlessness was entirely unacceptable to his administration.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The governor then directed security agencies to maintain a robust, round-the-clock presence in the affected zones to ensure compliance to his earlier ceasefire order in the communities.

He reassured all parties that his administration remains firm, fair, and uncompromising in its pursuit of lasting peace and justice across the state.

Community leaders speak

In attendance at the meeting were traditional rulers from the Anambra South and Central senatorial districts of the state.

The Chairman of the Anambra State Traditional Rulers Council, Chidubem Iweka, was among the traditional rulers in attendance.

The traditional rulers, in their separate contributions, condemned the hostilities, specifically highlighting the tragic killings of a minor and an unarmed person from Umuoba Anam.

They also lamented “the retaliatory destruction” of the Idigo Palace, the historic royal residence of Michael Idigo, the traditional ruler of the Aguleri Community.

Speaking as an observer on behalf of the Umueri Community, Charles Okaa, appealed for restraint.

Mr Okaa, a retired justice, urged the state government to enforce the 1982 Supreme Court judgement concerning boundary matters between Umueri and Aguleri as a step toward permanent resolution.

Prosecution of perpetrators

After the deliberations, the stakeholders reached “a multi-point” resolution to foster reconciliation and security.

They also stressed the need for immediate ceasefire and prosecution of perpetrators.

Mr Soludo condemned the attack on the traditional stool, describing it as “an assault on the heritage” of the state.

The governor then announced that the state government would “actively assist” in rebuilding the destroyed palace to restore “traditional dignity.”

Long history

The Aguleri–Umuoba Anam dispute dates back decades.

It is primarily a land and boundary dispute, with competing claims over ownership of land around the Anambra River and areas adjoining the two communities.

The Anambra State Government had described the matter as a boundary dispute and, in 2025, referred it to the State Boundary Committee for resolution.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that the dispute resurfaces usually after years of state government intervention.

In March 2015 for instance, a clash between the two communities left at least one person dead and several houses destroyed.

After the state government’s intervention, the clash ceased but resurfaced 10 years later in 2025.

Within the time, traditional rulers of the two communities presented different accounts of the origin of the disagreement with all laying claims to the ownership of the disputed land.

The fresh violence in the two communities has also been attributed to the long-standing land dispute.

World.title: N18m Fraud: Police arrest man in Ogun for allegedly impersonating prophet on Facebook
World.content:
The Police Command in Ogun State has arrested a suspect, Adewale Arojah, for allegedly impersonating a cleric on Facebook and defrauding victims of over N18 million.

The command’s spokesman Oluseyi Babaseyi, a deputy superintendent of police, disclosed this in a statement issued on Thursday in Abeokuta, the state capital.

Mr Babaseyi said the suspect was arrested by police operatives of the Ilaro division following a complaint lodged on 3 October by one Muyiwa Akogun, popularly known on Facebook as “Prophet Dr. Muyiwa Akogun.”

He said Mr Akogun had reported that members of the public were complaining about fraudulent activities being carried out through a duplicated Facebook account bearing his identity.

According to Mr Babaseyi, the suspect was a spiritual son of Mr Akogun and has allegedly used the cleric’s identity to deceive unsuspecting members of the public.

He said upon receipt of the complaint, the Divisional Police Officer (DPO), Ilaro, immediately deployed intelligence and detective operatives to track the suspect.

He noted that sustained technological monitoring and intelligence-led investigation led to the suspect’s arrest in a village in Ajegunle in the Ilaro/Ibogun axis.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Upon his arrest, the suspect confessed during interrogation to impersonating Akogun and using his identity to offer fake prophecies and prayer services to unsuspecting victims.

“Preliminary investigation revealed that the suspect targeted people seeking spiritual assistance through the cleric’s Facebook page and allegedly defrauded victims in Nigeria and abroad of over N18 million.

“The suspect has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Eleweran, Abeokuta, for further investigation to determine the extent of the alleged offences and identify possible accomplices,” he said.

Mr Babaseyi quoted the Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, as commending the Ilaro operatives for their vigilance and swift response.

Mr Ojajuni reaffirmed the command’s commitment to tackling cybercrime, identity theft and other forms of criminality in the state.

He also advised members of the public to verify the authenticity of social media accounts belonging to religious leaders and public figures before engaging with them.

He urged citizens to avoid transferring money to unverified persons for spiritual remedies or other services.

Mr encouraged members of the public to report cybercrime, impersonation and suspicious activities through the Gateway Shield toll-free line, 0800 000 9111, or 09164859299 and 09154293464.

(NAN)

World.title: VFD Group creates first-ever deputy managing director role, announces appointee
World.content:
VFD Group Plc has announced the appointment of Ijeoma Emezie-Ezigbo as its Deputy Managing Director, effective 5 October.

The company disclosed this in a statement on Thursday, noting that the appointment marked a significant step in the Group’s institutional development and executive leadership structure.

VFD Group recently created the role, and Ms Emezie-Ezigbo is the company’s first deputy managing director.

The Group Managing Director, Nonso Okpala, said creating the Deputy Managing Director role reflects VFD Group’s commitment to building the Group as an institution with the governance depth, leadership capacity, and succession structures required for long-term sustainability.

“Our ambition is to build an organisation whose strength extends beyond any individual, supported by strong systems, capable leadership and a clear institutional direction,” Mr Okpala said.

He added that Ms Emezie-Ezigbo’s experience in transaction advisory, corporate finance and strategic management will bring valuable depth to its executive leadership as the company continues to build for the future.

Speaking on her appointment, Ms Emezie-Ezigbo expressed her commitment to support the company with sound decision-making and creating sustainable long-term value across the Group.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I am pleased to join VFD Group at this important stage in its institutional journey. I look forward to contributing my experience in corporate finance, transactions and strategic management to strengthening governance, supporting sound decision-making and creating sustainable long-term value across the Group,” she said.

Profile

Ms Emezie-Ezigbo brings more than two decades of experience spanning corporate finance, transaction advisory, mergers and acquisitions, business valuation and strategic financial management across Nigeria, Canada and other African markets.

She most recently served as Partner and Head of Transaction Services, West Africa, at KPMG Nigeria.

Her career also includes senior roles at Stanbic IBTC Group, IBM Canada and Canadian Tire Corporation.

Ms Emezie-Ezigbo’s appointment is expected to deepen VFD Group’s corporate governance framework, strengthen strategic oversight and reinforce leadership continuity as the investment company advances its long-term growth ambitions.

The newly appointed deputy managing director holds a First-Class Honours degree in Business Administration, specialising in Marketing, from the University of Nigeria.

She also holds a Master of Finance degree from Cass Business School, London, and has completed the Advanced Management Programme at Lagos Business School.

Her professional qualifications include Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (FCA), Associate Chartered Certified Accountant (ACCA UK), Chartered Professional Accountant in Ontario, Canada, and Certified Valuation Analyst.

Ms Emezie-Ezigbo joins the Group’s executive leadership alongside Group Managing Director Nonso Okpala and Executive Directors Folajimi Adeleye and Morenike Ominike. The Board is chaired by Olatunde Busari (SAN).

The appointment forms part of VFD Group’s broader commitment to institutionalisation, with a focus on strengthening governance, developing leadership capacity and building a resilient organisation positioned for sustainable growth beyond any single individual.

World.title: ACF ‘congratulates’ Bwala for admitting Tinubu’s reforms deepen poverty
World.content:
Professor Tukur Mohammed-Baba, Publicity Secretary of the ACF and Daniel Bwala, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication.

The Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) has sarcastically “congratulated” Daniel Bwala, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, for acknowledging that the administration’s economic reforms have increased poverty and hardship among Nigerians.

Professor Tukur Mohammed-Baba, Publicity Secretary of the ACF, made the remark during an interview on Arise Television’s News Day on Thursday.

Mohammed-Baba was reacting to Bwala’s comments during an interview on Channels Television on Wednesday, where the presidential aide acknowledged that the government’s economic reforms had contributed to an increase in poverty but argued that the administration had made significant progress since introducing the measures.

“Let’s first of all be very happy and congratulate Bwala. Until now, one would expect that whenever he comes on TV or appears on social media, it is to deny, deny, deny,” Mohammed-Baba said.

“But I think we are making progress since his admitting fundamentally that the reforms have brought untold hardships on Nigerians. Most especially, he has not denied that poverty has been rising.”

The ACF spokesman said multidimensional poverty remained widespread in the country, while criticising attempts by the administration to justify the hardship as a temporary consequence of economic reforms.

“As we speak today, the rate of multidimensional poverty is well over 60 per cent in Nigeria,” he said.

Mohammed-Baba dismissed claims that the benefits of the reforms would eventually outweigh their immediate effects, describing such assurances as “hallucinations” and drawing a comparison with the structural adjustment programme of the Ibrahim Babangida administration.

He said Nigerians were currently struggling with declining purchasing power, rising rents, housing costs, transportation fares and electricity bills, while insecurity had further worsened living conditions.

“Look at the purchasing power of the naira. Look at the living conditions of Nigerians. Look at rent. Look at housing materials. Look at transportation. Look at electricity costs,” he said.

“See the condition of the roads in Nigeria, and above all, see the level of insecurity that has been pervading this country.”

The ACF official, who said he had visited parts of the Northeast, North-Central and Northwest, said insecurity had made basic activities such as farming increasingly difficult.

He argued that the Tinubu administration could not continue to shift responsibility for current challenges to previous governments, saying those who sought political power should have assessed the conditions they would inherit before assuming office.

“That is precisely why we have a democracy. You identify there are problems, and you think you have the answer. You go out, canvass for votes. You get it, and now you spend reminding us other leaders have faced these problems,” he said.

Mohammed-Baba said the administration should accept responsibility for its performance rather than tell Nigerians that it was not responsible for their hardship.

“There is no doubt that if the government were to go into the room, look at itself in the mirror, and tell us honestly whether it has performed optimally or near satisfactorily, I am sure the answer will be negative,” he said.

World.title: Veteran communication scholar Idowu Sobowale dies at 85
World.content:
Professor Idowu Sobowale

LAGOS — Professor Idowu Akanbi Sobowale, a renowned communication scholar and veteran member of Nigeria’s media and communication community, has died at the age of 85.

Sobowale died on Thursday morning, October 8, 2026, according to a statement by a member of his family, Akinniyi Sowunmi.

Sowunmi announced the death in a statement titled, “Transition to Glory,” describing the deceased as a major loss to Nigeria’s communication community, particularly members of the Association of Communication Scholars and Professionals in Nigeria, ACSPN.

The statement read in part: “This is a very sad day for us in the Communication Community in Nigeria and especially for us at the Association of Communication Scholars & Professionals in Nigeria.

“Our father, Pa Deacon Professor Idowu Akanbi Sobowale, OON, 85, joined the saints triumphant this morning, October 8, 2026.”

The family said details of the funeral arrangements would be announced later.

Sobowale’s death comes as a loss to Nigeria’s communication and media community, where he was recognised as a veteran scholar and member of the professional community.

World.title: Lagos Life game is valued at $1bn — Creator, Shalom Rayhamen
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Nigerian software developer and creator of the viral Nigerian browser game Lagos Life, Shalom Rayhamen, has said the game is valued at $1 billion, dismissing a reported $100,000 offer for the game as too small.

Rayhamen made the disclosure in an interview with Nigerian digital content creator Fisayo Fosudo, shared on his Youtube page on Wednesday.

When asked what she thought about people online offering $100,000 to buy Lagos Life and whether she was willing to sell, Rayhamen said the amount was far below the value she places on the game.

She said: “A $100,000 is small. Lagos Life is valued at $1 billion, so if they want to buy, they should talk $1 billion. What is a $100,000? I don’t want to say we’ve, like… or something, but what is that?”

Lagos Life has become one of the most talked-about Nigerian-made digital games since its launch on October 1, 2026.

The browser-based life simulation game allows players to create characters, take jobs, earn virtual naira, rent homes, socialise and explore locations inspired by Lagos.

The game is essentially a Lagos-themed take on the life-simulation concept popularised by games such as The Sims, but its appeal comes from its use of familiar Nigerian experiences, locations and culture.

Players can navigate different aspects of virtual Lagos, including employment, money, housing, entertainment and social activities.

Among the locations featured in the game are Amala Shitta and Quilox, while its wider gameplay draws on familiar Lagos experiences such as transportation, nightlife and food.

Lagos Life does not require users to download an application, as it can be played directly through a web browser on phones and computers.

The game’s rapid growth has also attracted attention from businesses, with virtual advertising spaces providing a potential commercial model for the platform.

However, the money used within the game has no real-world cash value. Players cannot withdraw the virtual naira or convert it into real money.

Rayhamen’s $1 billion valuation comes as interest in the game continues to grow, following its rapid rise across social media and its large player base.

The game’s success has also placed Nigerian-made browser games in the spotlight, following the viral attention received by Lagos Run, another locally themed game built around the experience of driving a danfo through Lagos.

Vanguard News

World.title: I paid N6m for my son’s release, mother of freed NYSC member
World.content:
Photo Credit: Nigeria Police Force/X

A mother of one of the freed members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) says she paid N6 million ransom to secure her son’s release.

Recall the prospective corps members were abducted on October 1 after gunmen attacked two 18-seater buses travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, along the Owerri-Onitsha expressway.

The woman disclosed this in an interview with News Central Television on Wednesday, saying the kidnappers initially demanded N50 million for each victim before eventually accepting N6 million for her son.

“Initially, they asked us to pay N50 million per head. We asked whether the amount was for all of them, but they insisted that no, it was for each person. Later, we started begging them to take N500,000. But they said no and started scaring us,” she said in Yoruba.

“Three days ago, they called and said we should pay N15 million. We kept begging them that all we had was N5.5 million. They said no and insisted on N6 million. So, it’s that N6 million we paid.”

The woman said the abductors asked the parents of the victims to send representatives to meet them in Ibadan as part of arrangements for the ransom payment.

“They called all the parents of all the victims. Twenty of them are in the bush. They then asked us to send three persons each to meet with them in Ibadan. My husband and my son’s elder brother went.

“When they got to the meeting place, they asked them to send the money to an account and that when they got to Imo state, they should change the money into dollars.”

She said her elder son was among those who met the abductors and delivered the ransom.

“It is not rumours. They have all been released and sent to us. His brother is among the people who went to meet with the abductors three days ago. They left with the ransom,” she said.

“It was the brother who called us this evening to say that they had handed the ransom to the kidnappers and that they had released our son. We also spoke to the boy.”

The mother, whose name was not disclosed, said the abduction left her traumatised and unable to sleep throughout the period her son was held captive.

“Since he was kidnapped, I have been stooling. I couldn’t sleep either. But I was relieved when I heard they had been released. It was as though the chains all over me were loosened,” she said.

World.title: Umahi dismisses rift with Wike, says ‘we’re one family’
World.content:
Minister of Works, Dave Umahi, has dismissed reports of a strained relationship between him and the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, describing the former Rivers State governor as a progressive politician and member of the same political family.

Umahi spoke at a press conference in Abuja on Wednesday while reacting to reports of divisions within the All Progressives Congress and speculation over his relationship with Wike.

The minister said there was no basis for the reports of a rift, insisting that both men remained connected by their shared political interests.

“We need Wike as Wike needs us. So, it’s one family,” Umahi said.

He said political differences between him and the FCT minister had been exaggerated by their opponents, stressing that their relationship remained cordial.

Umahi also urged politicians to focus on national development rather than allow political disagreements to create divisions among people who share common interests.

Wike, who remains a member of the Peoples Democratic Party, has continued to maintain his political relevance while backing President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

In January, the FCT minister said his rainbow coalition represented a departure from conventional party politics, describing it as a collective political movement aimed at advancing the interests of Rivers State.

His position has, however, come amid concerns within the ruling APC over political alliances that could affect Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.

The Progressive Governors Forum has said it would not support any alliance or political arrangement capable of undermining Tinubu’s re-election or the electoral prospects of APC candidates in the 2027 elections.

Despite the concerns surrounding political alignments ahead of the 2027 elections, Umahi maintained that his relationship with Wike was not defined by the differences being portrayed by their political opponents.

He reiterated that both men remained part of the same political family and should be viewed within the broader context of their shared commitment to national development.

World.title: Viral video: FCT CP orders probe into N450,000 demand
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

ABUJA — The Commissioner of Police, FCT Command, CP Ahmed Muhammed Sanusi, has ordered an investigation into allegations that police investigators demanded N450,000 from a content creator before investigating a complaint he brought to the command.

The allegation was contained in a video circulating on social media in which the content creator, identified as Tumma Gabriel, claimed that officers at the FCT Police Command Criminal Investigation Department demanded the money as “mobilisation and petition.”

The command’s Police Public Relations Officer, SP Josephine Adeh, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday.

Adeh said the FCT Police Command was aware of the video and stressed that the police did not mandate or encourage its officers to solicit or demand any form of payment before, during or after investigations.

“The Command wishes to state clearly that it does not mandate or encourage its officers to solicit or demand any form of remuneration before, during, or after investigations,” she said.

She said the Commissioner of Police had consequently ordered a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the allegation and identify any officer who might be involved.

“Any person found liable will be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of the Police Act and Regulations,” Adeh added.

The command also urged the complainant to contact it through 08180382808 and visit the Command Headquarters to assist the investigation by providing relevant information that could help identify the officer or officers involved.

The police said the investigation was aimed at establishing the facts surrounding the allegation and taking appropriate action where wrongdoing was established.

World.title: Popular Nigerian rapper Lord of Ajasa becomes US citizen
World.content:
Veteran Nigerian rapper Olusegun Osaniyi, popularly known as Lord of Ajasa, has become a United States citizen, drawing congratulatory messages from fellow artistes, music producers and fans.

The pioneer of mainstream Yoruba rap shared photographs and videos of himself celebrating the milestone on his Instagram page, @lordofajasa, on Wednesday.

In one of the clips, the rapper was seen holding his American citizenship certificate, while another photograph showed him posing with his wife alongside the United States flag.

The development quickly attracted attention from fans and entertainment personalities, with several of Lord of Ajasa’s contemporaries celebrating the milestone in the comment section of his Instagram post.

Music producer and Coded Tunes founder, Olumide Ogunade, popularly known as ID Cabasa, wrote, “Congratulations Lord Oshi.”

Lord of Ajasa replied, “Thanks Cabasa.”

His contemporary, singer Abolore Akande, popularly known as 9ice, also congratulated him, w

riting, “Congrats apase”

Lord of Ajasa responded, “Thanks Baalè.”

The rapper’s citizenship milestone also renewed conversations about his contribution to the development of indigenous Nigerian hip-hop, particularly Yoruba-language rap.

Lord of Ajasa emerged as one of the early artistes to bring Yoruba rap into mainstream Nigerian music, predating the rise of later indigenous rap acts such as Dagrin, Olamide and Reminisce.

His music has remained influential in conversations about the early years of Yoruba hip-hop, with songs including “Le Fenu So,” “Esha Lo Bade,” and “Mai Lo” still remembered by music lovers.

The veteran rapper’s latest milestone has now added a new chapter to his career, as fans and colleagues continue to celebrate his transition to American citizenship.

Vanguard News

World.title: Messi’s farewell: Rohr reveals Benin players were denied photos, shirts
World.content:
Gernot Rohr

Benin head coach Gernot Rohr has criticised the treatment of his players after their international friendly against Argentina, saying they were denied the opportunity to take photographs with Lionel Messi and exchange shirts with the world champions.

Argentina defeated Benin 3-0 at the Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires on Tuesday in Messi’s final appearance for the national team.

Speaking on RMC radio’s Rothen s’enflamme on Wednesday, Rohr said the Benin players attempted to meet Messi and other Argentine players after the match but were prevented from doing so by security personnel.

“Yes, it was extremely difficult. We tried.

“The only shame is that the Argentines gave us nothing. No photo with Messi, no shirt. They didn’t even let us into the tunnel, nor even the dressing room,” he said.

“Security refused to let anyone in. Some players came to swap shirts, so we knew it would be difficult. We tried everything, but we got nothing,” he added.

The Benin delegation also tried to present Messi with a bouquet of flowers in the country’s national colours, but Rohr said the gesture did not lead to a meeting with the Argentine captain.

“We offered a bouquet of flowers in Benin’s colours, yellow, red and green, but that didn’t work,” the German said.

“However, I gave Messi’s 2018 shirt to coach Scaloni, who got him to sign it for me and then returned it to me, but that was all,” he said.

Messi marked his farewell after a 21-year international career with Argentina with a goal and two assists, setting up Nicolás Otamendi and Nico Paz before converting a penalty as Argentina secured the victory.

He ended his Argentina career as the country’s most capped player and leading goalscorer, with 208 appearances and 126 goals.

World.title: Northern Stakeholders Support ACReSAL’s $500m Additional Financing
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The proposed $500 million additional financing for the Agro-Climatic Resilience in Semi-Arid Landscapes (ACReSAL) project has received broad support from stakeholders across northern Nigeria, according to the Think Nigeria First Initiative (TNFI).

Speaking during a press conference in Abuja, the Director General of TNFI, Alhaji Abubakar Tsanni, said governors, traditional rulers, farmers, herders and women’s groups had thrown their weight behind the next phase of the project because of the tangible results recorded in their communities.

Tsanni identified the governors of Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Kebbi, Kaduna, Jigawa, Benue and Plateau States as among those who had personally inaugurated, inspected or flagged off ACReSAL interventions.

He added that Bauchi State had publicly committed its counterpart funding to the proposed next phase.

“Traditional institutions, including the palaces of the Shehu of Borno, Emir of Argungu and Emir of Zazzau, work hand-in-hand with the project. In Wurno, a farmer of 27 years on the irrigation scheme says hope has returned. In Nguru, herders and fishermen have returned to a wetland that was dry for 12 years,” Tsanni said.

According to him, women account for 47 per cent of the project’s 4.4 million direct beneficiaries, while university students in Kogi, Kebbi and Plateau States are being trained in modern greenhouse farming on their campuses.

He further said the Federal Ministers of Environment, Water Resources and Agriculture had jointly participated in the project’s mid-term review in Kaduna.

Tsanni maintained that stakeholders were not seeking charity, but sustainable financing built around continuity, shared responsibility and self-reliance.

He disclosed that participating states had so far released N22 billion in counterpart funding, while the $9.5 million Community Revolving Fund disbursed to 381 communities was being repaid and re-lent.

He also noted that Benue and Nasarawa States had established state agencies to ensure the sustainability of the project’s assets.

The TNFI Director General therefore urged governors, traditional rulers, legislators and community leaders across the north who had witnessed the impact of ACReSAL to “say so publicly, and say so now”.

He also called on the Federal Government and the World Bank to conclude the financing arrangement without further delay.

World.title: Humanitarian Worker, Police Inspector Killed as Bandits Raid Sokoto Communities
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

A humanitarian and field operations professional, Ms Lydia Chinenye Nwankwo, has been killed following an attack by suspected bandits in Sokoto State.

Nwankwo was reportedly attacked alongside members of her team while returning from field operations in Kajiji community, Shagari Local Government Area of the state on Tuesday, October 6, 2026.

The development was confirmed by her sister, Chisom Nwankwo, who announced the tragic incident in a Facebook post on Thursday October 8.

According to the family, the team came under heavy attack from the armed bandits who opened fire on their vehicle, killing the young humanitarian worker on the spot.

The incident has thrown the humanitarian community in Sokoto into mourning, with colleagues describing Lydia as a dedicated field worker committed to serving vulnerable communities in hard-to-reach areas.

Meanwhile, the Sokoto State Police Command has confirmed the attack on communities in Shagari LGA, disclosing that a police inspector also lost his life during the incident.

The Command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Ahmed Rufai, who confirmed the attack to THISDAY, said the Divisional Police Officer in charge of Shagari LGA had briefed the state headquarters on the development.

Rufai, however, noted that the Command was still collating details of the attack to ascertain the full extent of casualties and damage.

“I just spoke with the DPO in charge of Shagari now, who confirmed the attack on some communities in the local government. We are still on it. I cannot give details now until I gather my information about the incident. I will get back to you on it,” the police spokesman stated.

As at press time, the security situation in the affected communities remained tense, with residents calling on the state government and security agencies to intensify patrols and deploy more personnel to Shagari and its environs to forestall further attacks.

World.title: ICRC Moves To Optimise Zungeru Hydropower Plant’s 700MW Capacity, Holds Talks With Power, Water Ministries, BPE, Others
World.content:
*Reviews contractual, operational limitations to plant’s efficiency

The Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC) has stepped up its regulatory oversight of the $1.3 billion, 700-megawatt Zungeru Hydropower Project, with a view to improving the plant’s performance.

The plant, which is operated under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) arrangement, is currently generating about 350 megawatts to the National Grid, according to the ICRC.

The commission said the move was in line with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s charge to unlock the potential of Nigeria’s power sector.

The President had reaffirmed the commitment in his 2026 Democracy Day speech, declaring that, “Electricity is a democratic dividend we owe every Nigerian.”

The ICRC, acting under the ICRC Act 2005, convened a stakeholders’ meeting in Abuja involving the Federal Ministry of Power, Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, Bureau of Public Enterprises (BPE) and the concessionaire, Penstock Limited.

The BPE acts as grantor under a power of attorney from the Ministry of Power.

Speaking at the meeting, ICRC Director-General, Dr. Jobson Oseodion Ewalefoh, said PPP assets such as Zungeru could not be allowed to operate below capacity as the administration works to address the country’s power challenges.

He said the meeting was convened to identify and address the issues hindering the plant’s optimal performance.

“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s promise to Nigerians that he will solve the power problem is not words for the sake of it. It is a statement he meant, and he has charged all of us to support him by playing our roles to deliver on this promise,” he said.

Ewalefoh explained that the ICRC was established as the regulator of PPPs and was therefore not a party to any PPP agreement, but was responsible for ensuring compliance by both the grantor and concessionaire with the terms and obligations contained in the agreement.

Section 20 of the ICRC Act states: “The Commission shall:

a. take custody of every concession agreement made under this Act and monitor compliance with the terms and conditions of such agreement;

b. ensure efficient execution of any concession agreement or contract entered into by the Government;

c. ensure compliance with the provisions of this Act;

d. perform such other duties as may be directed by the President, from time to time and as are necessary or expedient to ensure the efficient performance of the function of the Commission under this Act.”

Ewalefoh said, “Signing a concession agreement is only the first step; implementation of the terms in the PPP agreement is what delivers results. In PPP, risks are shared and no party is doing the other a favour. Our duty is to ensure sustainability, return on investment is achieved, services are delivered, and value for money is secured in the interest of the Nigerian people.”

The ICRC DG disclosed that the ICRC Act 2005 defines the Commission’s reporting line to the President, adding that similar compliance reviews, would be carried out on other PPP- operated power plants, including Kainji, Jebba, Shiroro, Dadinkowa and Kashimbila, and a final report submitted to the President.

Ewalefoh pledged the commission’s commitment to working with all stakeholders, particularly the Federal Ministry of Power, to ensure that PPP power projects contribute optimally to meeting Nigerians’ energy needs.

He said the ICRC would also review other existing PPP arrangements to ensure optimal performance, stressing that efficiency was a key reason government assets were handed over to the private sector.

At the end of the meeting, the ICRC and the stakeholders itemised the legal and operational issues raised and agreed on a date to reconvene.

World.title: SKOT Impact Academy Records Rising Demand, Attracts 450 Applicants for Third Cohort
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

SKOT Impact Academy, the social impact learning programme of SKOT Communications, is set to commence its third six-week, intensive and tuition-free training programme on October 10, 2026, with more than 450 applications received for the latest cohort from Nigeria and other countries.

The academy has received more than 1,300 applications across its three cohorts, underscoring growing demand for accessible professional training among early-career public relations and communications professionals.

According to the organisation, applicants for cohort three came from 14 countries, including Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Ghana, Uganda, Pakistan, Rwanda, Zimbabwe, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Malawi, Bangladesh, Nepal, Tanzania and The Gambia.

Speaking on the commencement of the third cohort, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of SKOT Communications, Tokunboh George Taylor, explained that the development represents a significant expansion of the programme, which began with 40 participants in its first cohort before increasing to 60 participants in cohort two through a hybrid learning model.

The second cohort, she noted, included both physical and virtual participants from Nigeria, Kenya and the United Kingdom, adding that the academy’s growth reflected the depth of talent in the communications ecosystem and the need for greater investment in developing such talent.

“When we launched SKOT Impact Academy, we knew there was a need for more accessible and practical pathways into the communications profession,” Taylor said.

She added that the growing number of applications demonstrated the demand for professional development opportunities emphasising the quality of talent within the industry.

According to her, the academy’s impact should not be measured solely by the number of participants but by the careers and contributions it would influence in the communications industry.

“As the academy grows, our ambition is to reach more people, deepen the quality and relevance of the programme, and extend its impact across Africa and beyond. We believe this is only the beginning of what SKOT Impact Academy can become,” she said.

George-Taylor said the expansion of the academy comes at a time when the communications profession is undergoing significant changes driven by developments in business, media and digital technology.

She noted that communications professionals are increasingly required to navigate reputation management, crisis communication, digital platforms, emerging technologies and complex stakeholder expectations, while also understanding how communication supports broader organisational objectives.

The six-week programme, the CEO said, is designed to complement formal education with practical knowledge, industry exposure and learning from experienced communications professionals.

Its tuition-free model, she stated, was intended to remove the cost of professional training as a barrier for early-career professionals, while providing them with practical skills, professional judgement and confidence.

“The academy is also building a growing community of participants and alumni that could serve as an emerging talent pipeline for the communications industry across Africa and beyond,” the founder stated, adding that it would continue to expand the programme, improve its curriculum and make quality professional development more accessible to young communications professionals.

World.title: ITF Marks 55 Years of Driving Skills, Industrial Growth
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

The Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of the Industrial Training Fund (ITF), Dr. Afiz Oluwatoyin Ogun, has highlighted the institution’s achievements over the past three years, reaffirming its commitment to skills development and human capital advancement as the Fund marked its 55th anniversary in Jos.

Speaking at the anniversary celebration, Ogun said the ITF had sustained its relevance since its establishment in 1971 by adapting to the changing needs of the Nigerian economy and workforce.

He noted that under his administration, the Fund had expanded skills acquisition programmes, strengthened local and international partnerships, digitised key operations, improved staff welfare and upgraded training infrastructure across the country.

The ITF boss identified the Skill-Up Artisans (SUPA) programme as one of the institution’s flagship interventions, designed to train, certify and professionalise artisans nationwide.

He added that the Fund had also advanced Nigeria’s global skills competitiveness through strategic collaborations and the establishment of structures that align vocational training with international standards.

In a goodwill message, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Oil and Gas Free Zones Authority (OGFZA), Alhaji Bamanga Usman Jada, described the ITF as one of Nigeria’s most strategic agencies, given its central role in developing the nation’s human capital.

Jada commended the quality of facilities at the ITF Centre of Excellence in Jos, which he described as being of international standard, and praised the leadership of Dr. Afiz Oluwatoyin Ogun for the progress recorded by the organisation.

He stressed that Nigeria’s future prosperity would depend more on the development of its human resources than on its natural endowments, adding that the ITF remained critical to converting the country’s growing population into a skilled and productive workforce.

He further lauded the Federal Government’s efforts to create an enabling environment for investment and industrial growth, while urging continued support for skills development as a catalyst for economic transformation.

The event brought together government officials, industry leaders, development partners, members of the organised private sector and ITF staff to celebrate the institution’s contributions to manpower development and industrial growth over the last 55 years.

Stakeholders at the ceremony expressed confidence that the Fund would continue to play a pivotal role in enhancing workforce competitiveness and supporting Nigeria’s long-term economic development objectives.

World.title: Another Tragedy Averted as NAF Helicopter Makes Precautionary Landing in Benue
World.content:
* Helicopter, crew members safely return to base, says NAF

Linus Aleke in Abuja

Barely 48 hours after the fatal crash involving a Nigerian Air Force (NAF) ATR-42 aircraft in Igbokoda, Ondo State, another NAF helicopter has made a precautionary landing in Benue State during an air interdiction operation in Ogbadigbo, a border town between Benue and Enugu States.

The incident occurred barely 24 hours after the Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, and the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo (SAN), called for joint aviation safety measures to prevent frequent air mishaps involving military aircraft.

The call became imperative following the military’s record of at least 10 air mishaps in the past decade, some of which resulted in tragic fatalities, including the death of the former Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lt Gen Ibrahim Attahiru, and other senior military officers aboard a Nigerian Air Force Beechcraft King Air 350i (NAF203) aircraft en route to Kaduna on May 21, 2021.

The latest incident occurred at Utur Tse-Igboji, Bar Council Ward, along the Welfare Quarters–Mopol 13 Ring Road in Ogbadigbo Local Government Area of Benue State.

According to eyewitnesses, the pilot made a precautionary landing, prompting residents to rush to the scene to assist the officers on board. All those on board reportedly survived and exited the helicopter safely.

In a statement in response to reports of the incident, the Nigerian Air Force, through its Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, said the helicopter had successfully provided close air support to ground forces during an operation targeting suspected kidnappers in the Ogbadigbo area of Benue State, near the Enugu–Benue boundary.

According to Ejodame, the operation disrupted the activities of the suspected criminal elements and supported the advance of ground forces.

Responding to reports of the precautionary landing, he said: “Following the successful completion of the mission, the pilot, on return to base, exercised his professional discretion to execute a precautionary landing approximately 10 nautical miles from the airfield.

“This is in accordance with established operational and safety procedures following combat missions. The helicopter has returned to base.”

Although the Service did not disclose the specific reason for the precautionary landing, the statement stressed that the NAF remained committed to sustaining pressure on criminal elements, providing close air support to ground forces and protecting communities through coordinated air and ground operations.

Ejodame said the successful outcome of the operation underscored the NAF’s continued resolve to deny criminal elements freedom of action and support efforts to restore safety and security to affected communities.

World.title: Big Tent Decries Tinubu’s Latest Wasteful Jamboree on Incomplete Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway
World.content:
Another expensive ceremony for a fraction of a road while Nigerians starve, die young and live in insecurity

The Utomi-led Big Tent Coalition has strongly condemned the Federal Government’s plan to stage yet another lavish inauguration ceremony for Section One of the controversial Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway.

Minister of Works, Dave Umahi, has announced that the 47.47-kilometre Section One is “ready for commissioning”.

This is barely more than 6% of a project widely described as spanning about 750 kilometres across nine coastal states.

Not long ago—on May 31, 2025—the same Tinubu-led All Progressives Congress (APC) government organised a grand ceremony to “commission” just 30 kilometres, less than 5% of the total length.​

A statement issued by Director of Media and Communications, Big Tent, Charles Odibo, asked that: “Since when did the commissioning of unfinished, partial stretches of road become the new normal of governance in Nigeria? How low has the bar for ‘achievement’ sunk that a government now celebrates fractions of projects with fanfare, motorcades and millions of naira in public funds while the vast majority of the highway remains incomplete?”

According to the coalition, “These wasteful jamborees are an insult to a nation that continues to lag badly on the real measures of performance—human development.”

Big Tent noted that Nigeria ranks 164th out of 193 countries on the latest Human Development Index with a score of just 0.560. Life expectancy stands at approximately 54.5–54.9 years—among the lowest in the world.​

On poverty, World Bank estimates place the rate at around 63% in 2025/2026, meaning roughly 139–140 million Nigerians live below the poverty line. Education remains in crisis, with learning poverty estimated at about 70% for children under 10 (many unable to read a simple sentence) and millions still out of school. Security continues to deteriorate: Nigeria ranks near the bottom of the Global Peace Index (around 142nd–148th out of 163 countries in recent editions) and features among the countries most affected by terrorism.

Underemployment, youth joblessness and the absence of decent work remain widespread realities for millions of families.​

Odibo further stated that while ordinary Nigerians struggle with hunger, insecurity, collapsing public services and a future that looks increasingly bleak, “this government finds the resources and the appetite for repeated expensive ceremonies over incomplete roads. It is a clear demonstration that the Tinubu administration lacks the competence, capacity, compassion and character required to govern a serious nation.”

Big Tent reminded well-meaning citizens that “this election season presents Nigerians with a clear choice”.

The Big Tent Coalition therefore called on citizens to “see through the optics, the photo-ops and the unfinished projects dressed up as legacy achievements. We urge Nigerians to reject this pattern of governance and vote for leaders who are truly committed to a New Nigeria that works for all—leaders such as Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso—who prioritise results over rituals, people over pageantry, and genuine development over wasteful jamborees.

“Enough of the ceremonies. Deliver the full road. Fix the indices that actually matter. Nigeria deserves better”.

World.title: Ex-Rep Member Threatens Atiku’s Lobbyist With Legal Action, Rejects Tinubu Link
World.content:
A former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Ehiozuwa Johnson Agbonayinma, has threatened legal action against Karl Von Batten, also known as Ikemefuna Okeke, over an X post he described as misleading, insisting that his petition to the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) was not politically motivated.

Agbonayinma, a member of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), a Nigerian and a citizen of the United States of America, faulted the use of his photograph in a publication linking his 14-day ultimatum to the EFCC with President Bola Tinubu, rejected suggestions that he was acting on behalf of the president, the All Progressives Congress (APC) or any political interest.

In a statement made available to journalists on Thursday, the former lawmaker said the publication created a false impression about his identity, motives and involvement in the matter, warning that he would consider legal remedies over what he described as a misrepresentation of his position.

He maintained that his demand for the reopening of corruption allegations and reports involving former Vice President Atiku Abubakar was a personal initiative undertaken in the interest of accountability and the rule of law.

“For the avoidance of doubt, I did issue a 14-day ultimatum to the EFCC, calling on the commission to reopen the corruption allegations and reports involving Alhaji Atiku Abubakar. I stand by my call for accountability and the rule of law,” he said.

The former lawmaker, however, denied any connection with Tinubu or the APC in relation to the petition, stressing that he neither acted on the president’s behalf nor pursued the interests of any political party.

“My action was entirely personal, undertaken in my capacity as a Nigerian citizen who believes that allegations of financial impropriety involving public office holders deserve proper investigation,” he stated.

“Both the US senate, homeland security have conducted and concluded investigations. It is only left for the EFCC to do the right thing by prosecuting him,” Agbonayinma said.

He argued that the issues raised in his petition should not be reduced to partisan politics, insisting that allegations against public figures should be subjected to credible investigation irrespective of their political affiliations.

“My call for the reopening of Atiku Abubakar’s corruption reports is not about Tinubu, APC, PDP, ADC, NDC or any political party. It is about accountability, transparency and the principle that no individual should be above the law,” he added.

He urged the EFCC to determine the merits of the allegations through a transparent process, noting that the appropriate authorities should establish whether there were grounds for further investigation.

He also challenged Atiku’s legal team to address the substance of his petition rather than attribute political motives to his intervention.

Agbonayinma warned that the use of his photograph to advance what he considered a misleading narrative would not be treated lightly, adding that he was prepared to pursue legal action against those responsible for the publication.

Reaffirming his position, he said his intervention was driven by the need to promote accountability without fear or favour, irrespective of political considerations.

“I acted as a Nigerian, not as Tinubu’s representative. Let the record be clear,” he declared.

World.title: Travelling abroad this December? These passport mistakes could ground you
World.content:
South Africans travelling abroad this December should check their passports well before they fly. Image: Pexels.

Travelling abroad this December? Your passport might not be as ready as you think.

It could be valid. It could even have months left on it.

And you could still be turned away at the check-in counter.
