Every festive season, South Africans miss flights over small details they never thought to check.

Here’s what to look at now, while there’s still time to fix it.

An unexpired passport isn’t always enough. What matters is the rule in the country you’re visiting.



The Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) advises travellers to check their destination’s rules if their passport expires within the next six months.

Thailand, Indonesia, China, India and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) are among the countries that usually require your passport to be valid for six months from the day you arrive.

So a passport expiring in April 2027 could be fine for one December trip, and rejected for another.



COUNT YOUR BLANK PAGES

Blank pages trip up as many travellers as expiry dates.

DIRCO says your passport should have at least two blank pages.

If you need a visa, immigration advisers recommend having two blank facing pages: one for the visa and one for the entry stamps.



Damaged passports can cause problems at border controls too, so check yours for water damage or loose pages.

If your passport is close to expiring, or nearly full, DIRCO recommends applying for a new one six to 12 months beforeit expires.

Frequent travellers can also ask for a maxi passport, which has 48 pages instead of 32.



APPLY FOR YOUR VISA EARLIER THAN YOU THINK

If you’re heading to Europe or the UK, December is not the time to leave your visa to the last minute.

Schengen visa: You can apply up to six months before you travel.

A decision usually takes about 15 calendar days, but it can take up to 45 days in busy periods.



Demand is high.

According to visa agency Visaline, the European Commission confirmed in June 2025 that Schengen visa requests from South Africans had reached record highs, almost 40% higher than in 2023.

UK visa: A decision usually takes about 15 working days after your biometrics appointment. But getting the appointment itself can take another 10 days or so.



That means a realistic total of four to six weeks. Faster priority services are available, but at an extra cost.

Planning a trip to the US? Visa applicants must list their social media accounts, and some must now make their profiles public.

DON’T FORGET ABOUT TRANSIT RULES

Many South Africans assume a layover doesn’t need paperwork.



That’s not always true.

UK transit: South Africa is on the UK’s visa national list.

That means South Africans usually need a transit visa, even if they never leave the airport.



There are exemptions, such as for travellers flying on to the US, Canada, Australia or New Zealand who hold valid visas for those countries. Check the rules on GOV.UK before you fly.

Dubai transit: You don’t need a visa if you stay in the airport’s transit area. But you’ll need a transit visa if you want to leave the airport during your layover.

You’ll also pass through immigration if you change airlines and have to collect your luggage, so you’d need a visa then too.



TRAVELLING WITH CHILDREN? PACK THE RIGHT DOCUMENTS

If both parents are travelling with a child, the child usually only needs a valid passport.

If only one parent is travelling, the child may also need an unabridged birth certificate or equivalent document, plus a parental consent affidavit from the parent who isn’t travelling.

You’ll also need that parent’s full contact details and a copy of their ID or passport.



A court order or the other parent’s death certificate can replace the affidavit in some cases.

If parents are divorced and share custody, both parents need to give consent.

Children travelling with another adult, including on school tours, need similar documents.



According to Arrive Alive, that means a valid passport, an unabridged birth certificate and a parental consent affidavit, along with the parents’ contact details and copies of their IDs or passports.

COMMON AIRPORT MISTAKES TO AVOID

Using the wrong passport.

South African citizens aged 18 or over must use a South African passport to enter and leave South Africa. It’s illegal to use another country’s passport, even if you’re a dual citizen.



Booking before your visa is approved. Avoid non-refundable flights until your visa is in your hand.

Assuming “visa-free” means “no checks.” You may still need to show a return ticket, proof of accommodation or proof of funds.

Leaving it too late. If something’s wrong, you need time to fix it. Check your documents now, not at the airport.



Speaking from experience, checking passport pages isn’t the fun part of planning a holiday.

But I’d much rather spend ten minutes at my kitchen table than ten hours at a check-in counter.

My advice? Pull out your passport tonight. Check the expiry date, count the pages, and look up your destination’s rules.

World.title: South African passport takes another knock in latest global ranking
World.content:
South Africa’s passport has slipped in the latest global ranking. Image: canva

The South African passport has slipped further down the latest global passport rankings, falling from 79th in 2025 to 86th in 2026.

This is according to latest data from Passport Reports, which revealed South Africa now has a Mobility Score of 108, down from 110 last year.

The score means South African passport holders have access to 108 destinations without needing a traditional visa before travelling, although the exact entry requirements vary between countries.



The ranking covers 199 countries.

Where does the South African passport rank?

South Africa’s 86th position puts it third among the 54 African passports measured by Passport Reports.

It ranks fourth among the 11 BRICS countries, 15th among 19 G20 countries, 26th among 56 Commonwealth countries and 38th among 132 G77 countries.



The country’s Mobility Score is made up of:

59 visa-free destinations

42 visa-on-arrival destinations

7 destinations requiring an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)

Passport Reports says its rankings are based on the total number of destinations offering these forms of easier access.

Different passport indexes can produce different results because they use different methodologies and may classify entry requirements differently.



What does ‘visa-free’ actually mean?

The 108 destinations in South Africa’s Mobility Score don’t all offer completely visa-free travel.

A visa-free destination does not require a visa for entry.

A visa on arrival (VOA) means a visa is required, but it can be obtained after arriving at the destination rather than before departure.



An ETA means a traditional visa isn’t required, but travellers must obtain an electronic travel authorisation before arriving.

An e-Visa, meanwhile, still requires a visa application and approval before departure.

Travellers should therefore check the specific requirements for their destination before booking a trip, as some countries also have additional registration, arrival-card or pre-registration requirements.



South Africans can access 71.7% of Africa

Passport Reports records South Africa’s total access across Africa at 71.7% when visa-free, simplified-entry and ETA access are combined.

Some destinations have additional requirements despite not requiring a traditional visa.

For example, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand have arrival-card requirements, while Côte d’Ivoire requires pre-registration.



Seychelles has a tourist registration requirement, while travellers to Cape Verde can use the EASE system, which is an online electronic pre-registration platform for entering the country.

Maximum permitted stays also vary considerably.

Passport Reports lists stays of up to 360 days in Georgia, 180 days in destinations including Antigua and Barbuda, Barbados and Peru, and 90 days in many other countries.



Full list of destinations available without a traditional visa

The following destinations are listed by Passport Reports as offering South African passport holders visa-free entry, visa on arrival or ETA access.

Visa-free destinations

Region Destinations Africa Angola, Benin, Botswana, eSwatini, Gabon, Kenya, Lesotho, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Réunion, Tanzania, The Gambia, Tunisia, Zambia, Zimbabwe Americas Argentina, Belize, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Guyana, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, Venezuela Asia Hong Kong SAR China, Macao SAR China, Philippines Caribbean Antigua and Barbuda, Bahamas, Barbados, British Virgin Islands, Cayman Islands, Dominica, Grenada, Haiti, Jamaica, Montserrat, St Helena, St Lucia, St Vincent and the Grenadines, Trinidad and Tobago, Turks and Caicos Europe Georgia, Russian Federation Middle East Palestine Oceania Cook Islands, Fiji, Kiribati, Micronesia, Niue, Vanuatu

Visa on arrival

A visa on arrival means travellers do not need to obtain a conventional visa before leaving South Africa, but a visa is issued when they arrive.

Region Destinations Africa Burundi, Cape Verde Islands, Comoro Islands, Djibouti, Ethiopia, Guinea-Bissau, Madagascar, Mauritania, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone Asia Cambodia, Indonesia, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Maldives, Nepal, Tajikistan, Timor-Leste Middle East Armenia, Jordan, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia Oceania Marshall Islands, Palau Islands, Samoa, Tuvalu

ETA and other electronic requirements

An ETA is not the same as a traditional visa. Travellers do not apply for a conventional visa, but must obtain electronic authorisation before travelling.



Region Destination Requirement Africa Ghana ETA Africa Seychelles ETA Asia Malaysia ETA + arrival card Asia Singapore ETA + arrival card Asia South Korea ETA Asia Sri Lanka ETA Asia Thailand ETA + arrival card

Whether or not Rabada is fit in time for the Test starting on Friday, both men are already in the preliminary squad.
