Asian Markets Retreat On Oil And Yield Pressure

Asian equities fell on Thursday, 8 October, as higher oil prices and rising bond-market yields weighed on investor sentiment, the San Antonio Express-News reported on 8 October. The Nikkei 225 fell 1.4 per cent to 69,042.11, South Korea’s Kospi declined 2.6 per cent to 6,625.93, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell 1.3 per cent to 23,809.66, and Shanghai’s Composite slipped 0.8 per cent to 3,811.90.

The context is a region-wide shift from expansionary confidence towards guarded defensiveness. Higher energy costs and expensive funding are overriding the previous appetite for equity gains. For a US reader, the moment matters because it shows how quickly Asian markets can transmit global energy and rate shocks.

The register is risk-off but not panicked. Investors are trimming positions rather than fleeing, watching oil and bond yields as the two clearest signals of how long the unease will last.

Dollar-Bond Issuance Halts Across Asia-Pacific

No Asia-Pacific issuer sold a syndicated US-dollar bond so far in October, while third-quarter regional dollar-bond issuance fell 10 per cent to approximately US$88 billion, the Malaysian Star reported on 8 October. The figures were reported by the Malaysian Star on 8 October.

Japanese issuers accounted for nearly 40 per cent of third-quarter Asia-Pacific dollar-bond issuance, while mainland China accounted for just under 7 per cent, the Malaysian Star reported on 8 October. The slowdown suggests that borrowers are waiting for calmer markets.

The register is cautious and financing-focused. The halt in syndicated issuance is a signal that corporate treasurers and sovereign borrowers are unwilling to pay the current premium for dollar funding.

China Plans For Taiwan Governance And Deep Oil

Chinese policy advisers are working on post-reunification Taiwan governance, the South China Morning Post reported on 8 October.

The twin themes place Beijing in a posture of strategic confidence and energy-security ambition. For a US reader, the Taiwan planning is the sharper edge: it signals that Beijing is preparing for a scenario in which it controls the island, not merely contesting its status.

The register is methodical and forward-looking. China is not negotiating the substance of its claims; it is building the administrative and energy foundations for a longer contest.

India Weighs F-35s As Sensex Slips

India’s Sensex was down 1.2 per cent on 8 October, the San Antonio Express-News reported on 8 October. The South China Morning Post, dated 8 October, listed Indian consideration of US F-35 aircraft as a leading story.

The combination of strategic ambition and market sensitivity is characteristic of India’s current position. A potential F-35 acquisition would deepen defence ties with Washington, while the equity decline shows that domestic investors are not insulated from regional risk aversion.

The register is ambitious but exposed. India is pursuing advanced military capabilities even as its markets absorb the same external shocks affecting the rest of Asia.

South Korea’s Kospi Leads Regional Declines

South Korea’s Kospi fell 2.6 per cent to 6,625.93 on 8 October. The fall signals pronounced risk aversion in a market heavily exposed to technology and trade.

Yonhap’s newspaper roundup, published 8 October, highlighted coverage of South Korea’s first microsatellite constellation, suggesting a parallel national narrative of technological ambition. The contrast between market stress and strategic investment is stark.

The register is volatile and forward-leaning. Seoul is absorbing financial pressure while continuing to invest in space and defence capabilities.

Bank of Thailand Governor Vitai Ratanakorn said there was no rush to raise rates, with the policy rate at 1.00 per cent after an August decision and the next review scheduled for 28 October, US media reported on 8 October. The comments suggest a deliberate, patient approach to monetary policy.

The register is measured and reassuring. Bangkok is signalling that it will not tighten prematurely, even as global yields rise.

No Asia-Pacific issuer sold a syndicated US-dollar bond so far in October, while third-quarter regional dollar-bond issuance fell 10 per cent to approximately US$88 billion, the Malaysian Star reported on 8 October. Japanese issuers accounted for nearly 40 per cent of third-quarter issuance, and mainland China just under 7 per cent.

What is China planning for Taiwan?

Chinese policy advisers are working on post-reunification Taiwan governance, the South China Morning Post reported on 8 October.

What did the Bank of Thailand say about rates?

Bank of Thailand Governor Vitai Ratanakorn said there was no rush to raise rates, with the policy rate at 1.00 per cent after an August decision and the next review scheduled for 28 October, US media reported on 8 October.

Africa Intelligence Dossier — Thursday, 8 October 2026 · Web edition Take it with you. The full dossier is published on the web. Read the web dossier → · The dossier archive →

Kenya — The country records its first Ebola case and death, with the patient having travelled through DR Congo and Uganda before reaching Nairobi. South Africa — President Cyril Ramaphosa meets South Sudan’s Salva Kiir in Tshwane to press for a credible December election. Sudan — The African Union Peace and Security Council condemns the Rapid Support Forces-led parallel government announcement. Nigeria — Nurses in Abuja begin a seven-day warning strike over pay and working conditions after talks collapse. Africa-wide — The African Union launches the African Credit Rating Agency (AfCRA), headquartered in Port Louis, Mauritius, on 7 October 2026 under the African Peer Review Mechanism. Nigeria — A passenger dies aboard a Kenya Airways flight from Nairobi to Lagos shortly before landing.

Africa’s temper this Thursday is the anxiety of movement. A man who had lived in the Democratic Republic of Congo for seven years travelled by road to Uganda, flew to Nairobi, tested positive for Ebola in a hospital and died on Monday, 5 October, Africanews reported on 8 October. The route crossed three countries before detection. The continent is not only fighting a virus; it is fighting the speed at which a virus can outrun institutions built to catch it.

The register is a set of official responses that are precise about what they reject and vaguer about what they can deliver. The African Union Peace and Security Council condemned the Rapid Support Forces-led Sudan Founding Alliance’s announcement of a parallel government, rejected fragmentation and urged member states not to recognise the proposed authority, Gulf Times reported on 8 October. In South Africa, Ramaphosa told Kiir that remaining obstacles must be addressed to make the 22 December vote peaceful, credible and inclusive, Africanews reported on 8 October. These are statements of principle, and they are being issued at a moment when principle is under pressure from disease, war and electoral fragility.

What steadies the continent is the machinery of diplomacy and public-health response. Kenya’s Health Ministry increased surveillance at border crossings and established a public Ebola hotline, Africanews reported on 8 October. Ramaphosa met Kiir in Tshwane on Wednesday, 7 October, to address election logistics and peace-agreement implementation, Africanews reported on 8 October. These are not dramatic acts; they are the quiet, methodical work of states trying to keep their people inside the circle of protection and their neighbours inside the circle of dialogue.

The through-line is that Africa is managing movement across borders while its political settlements remain incomplete. Disease travels faster than institutions. Elections and ceasefires remain instruments of hope contested by armed and political actors. The African Credit Rating Agency (AfCRA) is launched in Port Louis, Mauritius, while nurses strike in Abuja. The continent is not collapsing; it is negotiating, in public, the distance between what it says and what it can prove.

Key Facts —Kenya’s Ebola case. A Kenyan man who had lived in DR Congo for seven years travelled by road to Uganda and then flew to Nairobi, tested positive and died on Monday, 5 October, Africanews reported on 8 October. —Border response. Kenya’s Health Ministry increased surveillance at border crossings and established a public Ebola hotline, Africanews reported on 8 October. —South Sudan diplomacy. Cyril Ramaphosa met Salva Kiir Mayardit in Tshwane on Wednesday, 7 October, to address the planned 22 December 2026 elections and the 2018 Revitalised Peace Agreement, Africanews reported on 8 October. —Sudan’s parallel government. The African Union Peace and Security Council condemned the Rapid Support Forces-led Sudan Founding Alliance’s announcement of a parallel government and urged member states not to recognise it, Gulf Times reported on 8 October. —Al-Burhan’s defiance. Sudanese leader Abdel Fattah al-Burhan rejected talks and vowed to retake territory held by the Rapid Support Forces, GhanaWeb reported on 8 October. —Abuja nurses’ strike. Nurses in Abuja began a seven-day warning strike on Wednesday, 7 October, over pay and working conditions after talks failed, Gulf Times reported on 8 October. —Emergency financing. US$150 million of a funding package would support emergency responses in Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, Chad, Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger, Cameroon, Afghanistan, the occupied Palestinian territory, Cuba and Yemen, AllAfrica reported on 8 October. —Credit-rating agency. The African Union launched the African Credit Rating Agency (AfCRA), headquartered in Port Louis, Mauritius, on 7 October 2026 under the African Peer Review Mechanism.

Kenya Confronts A Cross-Border Ebola Death

A Kenyan man who had lived in the Democratic Republic of Congo for seven years travelled by road to Uganda and then flew to Nairobi, where he tested positive for Ebola in a hospital and died on Monday, 5 October, Africanews reported on 8 October. The Health Ministry’s stated response, as reported indirectly by Africanews, was to intensify border surveillance and create a symptom-reporting hotline.

The case is a test of regional detection. The patient’s route crossed three countries before a diagnosis was made, which means the window for contact tracing extends beyond Kenya’s borders. The public-health machinery is now moving.

The register is vigilance with an open question. A first death is a threshold; the next days will show whether it is an isolated import or the beginning of a wider transmission chain.

Ramaphosa Presses Kiir On A Credible December Vote

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa met South Sudanese President Salva Kiir Mayardit in Tshwane on Wednesday, 7 October, to address South Sudan’s planned 22 December 2026 elections, implementation of the 2018 Revitalised Peace Agreement, political dialogue and security and logistical risks, Africanews reported on 8 October.

Ramaphosa chairs the African Union’s high-level ad hoc committee on South Sudan, which gives South Africa a formal role in the peace process. His position, reported indirectly, was that remaining obstacles must be addressed to make the vote peaceful, credible and inclusive. The meeting signals that Pretoria is investing diplomatic capital in a vote that remains fragile.

The register is responsibility. South Africa is presenting itself as a guarantor of a difficult neighbouring peace, and the December date is now the organising political fact.

The AU Rejects Sudan’s Parallel Government

The African Union Peace and Security Council condemned the Rapid Support Forces-led Sudan Founding Alliance’s announcement of a parallel government, Gulf Times reported on 8 October. The Council reportedly rejected fragmentation, urged member states not to recognise or support the proposed authority, reaffirmed Sudan’s sovereignty and called for an immediate unconditional ceasefire and inclusive national dialogue.

The condemnation is a line drawn against the fragmentation of a member state. It comes as Sudanese leader Abdel Fattah al-Burhan rejected talks and vowed to retake territory held by the Rapid Support Forces, GhanaWeb reported on 8 October. The two reports together describe a war that is hardening rather than softening.

The register is defiance. The AU is saying no to partition, and the Sudanese leadership is saying no to negotiation. The space between those positions is where civilians continue to suffer.

Abuja Nurses Walk Out Over Pay

Nurses in Abuja began a seven-day warning strike on Wednesday, 7 October, over pay and working conditions after talks between the National Association of Nigeria Nurses and Midwives and the government failed, Gulf Times reported on 8 October. The union’s stated position, reported indirectly, was that the strike followed the collapse of negotiations.

The strike is a signal of institutional strain. Health workers are on the front line of public-health emergencies, and a warning strike over wages suggests that the state’s capacity to respond to crises is being eroded by its own fiscal pressures.

The register is exhaustion. The nurses are not walking out over ideology; they are walking out over the basic terms of their labour, and the timing is not good for a country that needs its health system ready.

A Passenger Dies On A Lagos-Bound Flight

A passenger died aboard a Kenya Airways flight from Nairobi to Lagos after becoming unresponsive roughly 20 minutes before landing at Murtala Muhammed International Airport, AllAfrica reported on 8 October.

The death is a reminder that aviation connects the continent’s health systems in ways that are not always visible. A medical emergency at altitude becomes a border-crossing event, and the response involves airline crews, airport authorities and public-health officials in two countries.

The register is quiet concern. The incident is not yet a story of failure, but it is a story of how much depends on the ordinary protocols of air travel.

The AU Launches A Regional Credit-Rating Agency

The African Union launched the African Credit Rating Agency (AfCRA), headquartered in Port Louis, Mauritius, on 7 October 2026 under the African Peer Review Mechanism.

The launch is a structural answer to a long-standing complaint: that African sovereigns are rated by agencies outside the continent, with methodologies that do not always capture local realities. A regional agency is meant to provide an alternative view, though its credibility will depend on its independence and the quality of its analysis.

The register is ambition. The AU is building institutions, and the test will be whether they are trusted by the markets they are meant to serve.

Emergency Financing Reaches Across Crises

US$150 million of a funding package would support emergency responses in Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, Chad, Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger, Cameroon, Afghanistan, the occupied Palestinian territory, Cuba and Yemen, AllAfrica reported on 8 October.

The list of countries is a map of the world’s current emergencies, and Africa is heavily represented. The inclusion of Cuba alongside African crises suggests that humanitarian financing is being discussed in a global frame, not a regional one.

The register is scale. The amount is specific, but the needs are larger, and the allocation is a reminder that emergency response is always a matter of triage.

What This Means From Latin America

The reported US$150 million emergency allocation that includes Cuba alongside Sudan and South Sudan is a signal that African humanitarian financing is being discussed in a global frame, AllAfrica reported on 8 October. Latin American governments with Caribbean interests will note that the same funding conversations now span both regions.

The Kenya–Uganda–DRC travel route in the Ebola report demonstrates how African aviation and overland corridors create shared surveillance obligations, Africanews reported on 8 October. Latin American countries with air links through Europe or the Middle East will be watching Kenya’s contact tracing closely, because a virus that crosses three African borders can cross an ocean.

The AU’s rejection of a parallel government in Sudan is a precedent for how regional bodies handle competing claims to sovereignty, Gulf Times reported on 8 October. Latin American states that debate recognition of contested governments will see a model of collective refusal, even if the enforcement mechanisms remain unclear.

The comparison is set out at greater length elsewhere. The dossier carries the leader, the country health check and the outcome table with its Latin America column — open the Africa Intelligence Dossier.

What We Are Watching

World.title: Best Places to Live in Colombia for Expats 2026
World.content:
Expats · Colombia

For most American expats, Medellín is the best place to live in Colombia, followed by Bogotá. The catch is money and safety, not climate. Average asking rent for an apartment in Medellín was about US$1,520 a month in early 2026, and a deadly earthquake in August changed the case for Pereira and Cali.

Key Facts —Who. US retirees, remote workers and families choosing a base in Colombia. Dollar budgets matter more than peso budgets. —What. Seven cities ranked on rent, safety, climate, health care and natural hazards. Average asking rents in the first quarter of 2026 were about US$1,520 in Medellín and US$1,160 in Bogotá. —Why it matters. Homicide rates range from 14.5 per 100,000 in Medellín to 48.6 in Cali. The 10 August earthquake killed at least 329 people nationwide, according to the disaster agency UNGRD. —Watch. Annual inflation was 6.29% in September, against 6.24% in August, according to the EODHD economic calendar. The central bank, which raised its policy rate to 12.25% on 30 September, decides again at the end of October. —Prediction markets. Polymarket traders put 51.0% on no change at the central bank’s October rate decision and 37.5% on a 25 basis-point rise (US$34,073 traded). Bets, not forecasts. Read 8 October 2026, 07:13 ET.

Free download · Expat checklist Get the free checklist as PDF Moving to Colombia 2026: the step-by-step checklist. This guide condensed into 2 printable pages with tick boxes and the key official links. Email address Get the PDF Free. The same address also receives The Rio Times Brief, our daily briefing with an expat desk. We send a confirmation link first and nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves. Privacy policy. Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

The Short Answer: Medellín First, Bogotá for Services

Medellín ranks first because it combines a mild climate, a modern metro and the best recorded safety figures among the big cities. Bogotá ranks second for its hospitals and lower average rent. Cartagena, Barranquilla, Pereira, Santa Marta and Cali follow, each with a clear caveat.

This ranking is our editorial judgement, not a statistical index. We weighed rent, homicide rates and natural hazards, which can be measured. We also weighed how easy daily life is for a foreigner, which cannot.

Rank City Altitude and climate Average asking rent, apartment, Q1 2026 2025 homicides per 100,000 Main drawback 1 Medellín 1,479 m; about 24°C COP 4.92 million (about US$1,520) 14.5 Higher average rent than Bogotá 2 Bogotá 2,640 m; about 13°C COP 3.76 million (about US$1,160) 15.1 Cold, grey and rainy twice a year 3 Cartagena Sea level; about 27°C No city average found 40.5 Heat, humidity and a high homicide rate 4 Barranquilla Coast; 26–28°C No city average found 36.3 No reliable rent data found 5 Pereira 1,411 m No city average found Over 200 cases Hit hard by the 10 August earthquake 6 Santa Marta Caribbean coast No city average found Not verified Armed strike and embassy alert in September 7 Cali About 1,000 m; about 24°C No city average found 48.6 Highest homicide rate of the seven

Rents are average asking prices for apartments reported by the property portal Ciencuadras for the first quarter of 2026. They are asking prices, not signed leases, and unit sizes differ. We found no comparable city average for Cartagena, Barranquilla, Pereira, Santa Marta or Cali. Homicide rates are Medicina Legal figures as reported by the civic group Cartagena Cómo Vamos. Pereira is shown as a case count because we found no annual rate.

How We Ranked, and Which Dollar Rate We Use

Every conversion in this guide uses 3,240 pesos per US dollar. That is the EODHD quote on 7 October 2026 (3,238.25). The official daily rate, the TRM, was 3,209.78 on 6 October, so the choice moves figures by about 1%.

We rank on safety first, because it is the filter most newcomers cannot undo after signing a lease. Cost comes second, then health care and climate. The peso floats freely, and a stronger peso makes every city here dearer for anyone paid in dollars.

1. Medellín: El Poblado, Laureles and Envigado

Medellín sits at 1,479 metres in the Aburrá Valley, with an average temperature of 24°C, according to the city government. It is the city most often chosen by remote workers, which is why we start here.

Average asking rent for an apartment was COP 4.92 million a month (about US$1,520) in early 2026, higher than in Bogotá. El Colombiano reported the figure from Ciencuadras.

Safety is the best of the large cities, though not low by US standards. Medicina Legal counted 14.5 homicides per 100,000 people in 2025. Check the latest local figures before you sign.

For health care, Hospital Pablo Tobón Uribe is third on Newsweek’s 2026 list of the best hospitals in Colombia. The honest drawbacks are rents above Bogotá’s and homicide rates that are not low by US standards.

Residential Envigado, south of Medellín, with the Andes behind. File photo. Photo: Castillogrande, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

RT Ask Rio Times Straight answers about living in Colombia, from our reporting. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesCost of living, safety, visas in Colombia › RT Ask Rio Times Straight answers about living in Colombia, from our reporting. × Cost of living Is it safe? Visas Neighborhoods Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

Our deeper price guide is here.

2. Bogotá: Chapinero, Usaquén and the Cold

Bogotá sits at 2,640 metres, and the national weather service IDEAM puts the average temperature near 13°C. Evenings are cold, and rain comes in two seasons, from March to June and from September to December. Newcomers should pack a coat.

Average asking rent for an apartment was COP 3.76 million (about US$1,160) in the first quarter of 2026, for an average of 79 square metres. On these two portal figures, that is roughly a quarter below Medellín.

Medicina Legal’s figure for 2025 was 15.1 homicides per 100,000, and the city government counted 1,173 homicides. Fundación Santa Fe de Bogotá is second on Newsweek’s 2026 list of the best hospitals in Colombia.

The price of the big-city services is the cold, the traffic and a bigger-city feel.

Budget details are in our Bogotá cost guide.

3. Cartagena: Caribbean Heat and Colonial Streets

Cartagena is the postcard of Colombia. Average temperature is about 27°C, according to IDEAM, with daily highs of 31°C to 33°C. Air conditioning is a budget line, not a luxury.

We found no reliable city average for rent, and prices differ by barrio, so compare like with like.

The drawback is safety. Medicina Legal recorded 40.5 homicides per 100,000 in 2025. Treat the rate as approximate. Ask residents which streets to avoid at night.

Rents, utilities and barrio notes are in our Cartagena guide.

4. Barranquilla: The Port City With Carnival

Barranquilla is a business port on the Caribbean coast, with an average temperature of 26°C to 28°C. It hosts a famous carnival each year before Lent. We found no data on how many foreigners live here.

Medicina Legal’s city rate was 36.3 per 100,000. We found no reliable average rent, so test the market with a one-month furnished stay.

Our local budget is in the Barranquilla guide.

5. Pereira and the Coffee Region

Pereira lies at 1,411 metres above sea level. It is a quiet, green base for people who want cooler air than the coast.

The 2026 numbers now cut against it. A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck on 10 August 2026, with its epicentre in San José del Palmar in Chocó at a depth of roughly 100 kilometres. Colombia’s disaster agency, UNGRD, reported 329 deaths nationwide by 22 August. Pereira and Cali were among the cities affected.

Pereira also recorded more than 200 homicides in 2025. The Colombian Geological Survey places the Coffee Region among the areas of highest seismic acceleration. Ask any landlord about the building’s structural inspection and repair history.

The government’s recovery plan is covered in our quake-fund report.

6. Santa Marta: Beaches and a Tense September

Santa Marta is the base for Tayrona National Park and the Sierra Nevada. We found no verified 2025 homicide figure for the city.

An armed strike by the Autodefensas Conquistadoras de la Sierra Nevada began on the night of 21 September and burned vehicles. The group extended the strike until 7:00 on 25 September. The US Embassy issued a security alert for the area on 23 September.

The strike’s economic cost is in our September report. We recommend a short rental first, and a check of the latest embassy alert.

7. Cali: Salsa, Altitude and the Hard Numbers

Cali lies in a valley at about 1,000 metres and averages 24°C. It is the salsa capital, and its Fundación Valle del Lili tops Newsweek’s 2026 list of the best hospitals in Colombia.

The numbers on safety are the worst in this ranking. Cali recorded about 1,065 homicides in 2025, up from 938, a rate of about 48.6 per 100,000. Cali was among the cities worst hit by the August earthquake. The US State Department’s Level 4 area for Valle del Cauca explicitly excludes Cali itself.

Rents depend on the building’s estrato, a one-to-six classification that sets utility tariffs. See our Cali cost guide.

Safety, Visas and Health Cover for Americans

The US State Department rates Colombia Level 3, “Reconsider travel”, in an advisory issued on 31 March 2026. Level 4, “Do not travel”, covers Arauca, Cauca except Popayán, Valle del Cauca except Cali, Norte de Santander and a 10-kilometre strip along the Venezuelan border. Our safety guide explains the habits that matter.

Colombia’s visa money tests are written as multiples of the monthly minimum wage. For 2026 that wage is 1,750,905 pesos (about US$540). A final court ruling on the decree that set it is still pending.

The digital-nomad visa needs bank statements showing income of at least three minimum wages, about 5.25 million pesos (about US$1,620) a month. The Foreign Ministry says it is valid for up to two years. The rentista visa for passive income, such as rents and dividends, needs ten minimum wages, about 17.5 million pesos (about US$5,400).

Holders of old permanent resident visas have until 31 October 2026 to transfer them, the Foreign Ministry says. Our residency guide covers every route, and the residency how-to covers fees.

Medicare.gov says Medicare “usually doesn’t cover health care while you’re traveling outside the U.S.” and that you pay all costs in most cases. Americans on Medicare should buy private cover. Our health-care guide sets out the local system.

US citizens must report worldwide income to the IRS wherever they live. See our Colombia tax guide for the 183-day residency rule.

What Prediction Markets Say

Prices are the implied probability of each outcome. They are bets, not polls. Read on 8 October 2026 at 07:13 ET. Polymarket, Central Bank of Colombia decision in October, US$34,073 traded: no change at 51.0%; a 25 basis-point rise at 37.5%; a rise of 50 or more at 11.3%. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What to Watch

Annual inflation rose to 6.29% in September from 6.24% in August, according to the EODHD economic calendar. That is still more than double the central bank’s 3% target and keeps pressure on rents and services.

The central bank raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 12.25% on 30 September, with four of seven board members backing the rise, according to Vanguardia. Its next decision is due at the end of October. Higher rates often support the peso, which makes Colombia dearer for dollar earners. The visa transfer deadline for old resident visas is 31 October.

What It Means for You

Retirees who want a calm base should start with Medellín or Bogotá, then rent for a month before signing a lease. Remote workers on a US salary can use the nomad visa and compare two cities. Pereira and Cali make sense only after you have read the building inspection reports.

Budget in dollars and expect peso prices to keep rising. Buy health insurance that covers evacuation before you land, because Medicare will not follow you. If safety is your first filter, Medellín and Bogotá have the lowest recorded rates, and the Caribbean coast and Cali the highest.

What Is Not Known

We found no city-wide average rent for Cartagena, Barranquilla, Pereira, Santa Marta or Cali, and the two averages we use are asking prices. We could not read the State Department advisory page itself, so the level and areas come from its published summary. We did not verify the pensioner income test or the rules on joining the national health scheme.

Homicide counts differ by source, and 2025 annual rates are not available for Pereira. Final casualty totals for the 10 August earthquake are still provisional, and we could not confirm the date of the central bank’s next rate decision.

More: Colombia news in English, every day from The Rio Times. See also our Colombia cost-of-living guide and Peru versus Colombia comparison.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best place to live in Colombia for expats?

Medellín ranks first in our editorial ranking for its climate, safety record among big cities and services. Bogotá ranks second for hospitals and lower average rent. The ranking is a judgement, not an official index.

How much does rent cost in Colombian cities?

In the first quarter of 2026 the average asking rent for an apartment was about 4.92 million pesos (about US$1,520) in Medellín and 3.76 million pesos (about US$1,160) in Bogotá. These are asking prices from the property portal Ciencuadras.

Is Colombia safe for American expats?

Medicina Legal recorded 2025 homicide rates of 14.5 per 100,000 in Medellín, 15.1 in Bogotá and 48.6 in Cali. The US State Department rates Colombia Level 3, Reconsider travel, and Level 4 areas do not include Bogotá, Medellín or Cali.

Which Colombian cities were hit by the August 2026 earthquake?

A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck on 10 August 2026, with its epicentre in Chocó. Cali and Pereira were among the worst hit. Colombia’s disaster agency reported 329 deaths nationwide by 22 August.

Is there a digital-nomad visa for Colombia?

Yes. It requires bank statements showing income of at least three monthly minimum wages, about 5.25 million pesos (about US$1,620), and is valid for up to two years, according to the Foreign Ministry.

Will Medicare pay for care in Colombia?

Generally no. Medicare.gov says Medicare usually does not cover health care outside the United States, apart from rare exceptions, and you pay all costs in most cases.
