World.title: Croatian Protest Against Rising Taxes and Levies Announced
World.content:
October the 7th, 2026 – Another Croatian protest has been announced against rising taxes, levies and costs on the 10th of October in Zagreb.

The association Glas poduzetnika (Voice of Entrepreneurs) and the association Spasimo male obiteljske iznajmljivače (Save Small Family Renters) are organising the protest “Enough of the levies” on Saturday, the 10th of October, at 12:00 on Zagreb’s Zrinjevac. As Index, they want to protest to warn about the rising costs of living and doing business and to demand a lower tax burden, more responsible spending of public money and safer working conditions.

taxes and the real cost of wages

Dario Kožul, member of the Management Board of UGP, pointed out that the amount a worker receives in their account represents only part of the total cost of their wage. A significant portion goes to taxes and contributions, and the worker additionally pays VAT when spending their net wage on products and services. “The worker sees how much has been deposited into their account, but that is not everything the employer paid for their work. When they spend that money, they pay tax again. That is why we must talk about how much people have left for living, how much the state takes and what we get for that money,” Kožul said.

relief proposals

UGP Management Board member Kristina Bakula presented a series of concrete demands. She called for the abolition of the so-called anchor prices and the mandatory daily publication of price lists on the internet, as well as amendments to the Consumer Protection Act in the part that regulates base prices. She stressed that a serious discussion about prices must include taxes, VAT, labour costs and energy. “The price will not fall because it is published in one more place. Costs and VAT need to be reduced. If the Government is increasing the minimum wage, at the same time it should increase the non-taxable part of income and relieve the burden on labour. The simplest test of every measure is: how much more did the worker get, and how much did the state? The answer must be — more for the worker,” Bakula said.

Among the demands is also a reduction of contributions for lower income brackets and the abandonment of additional taxation of higher ones. Bakula supported the introduction of voluntary membership in chambers and tourist boards, as well as the application of the principle of warning and correction before punishment for minor omissions that can be corrected immediately. “If an organisation is worth something, people will want to stay in it. If the law has to keep them, maybe the problem is not with the members but with the organisation. And for a minor omission the state’s first reaction should be to correct the error, because a mistake is not fraud,” she said. She also emphasised the state’s obligation to respect its own decisions and protect existing permits and categorisations, which is particularly important for family renters. She believes that citizens who have invested according to the permits obtained must have clear and predictable conditions and protection of acquired rights.

attitudes towards business owners

She also commented on the way representatives of the authorities communicate with citizens and entrepreneurs. “The minister is there to talk to people, listen to them and offer solutions. He is the minister of all citizens who fill the budget from which his function is paid. The ministry is not a private lodge, and citizens are not extras in the minister’s film. We expect him to solve problems and to discuss people’s existence seriously, responsibly and with arguments,” Bakula emphasised.

UGP President Bruno Samardžić added that the discussion about price increases must also deal with the state’s decisions. He explained that taxes, levies and administrative obligations affect business costs, and their burden can spill over onto citizens through higher prices and less room for wage growth.“If you’re asking all of us to tighten our belts, show where you have tightened yours. Before new burdens, review your own costs, political employment and the accumulation of administration. I call on everyone to deal with the real problems: productivity and competitiveness, and not to keep going round in circles chasing our own tail. For entrepreneurs this Saturday is not just a struggle, but also an opportunity for their voice to finally be heard,” Samardžić said.

The organisers demand that for every new administrative obligation at least two existing ones be abolished. They also demand that tax changes and new levies must go through public consultation instead of being adopted under urgent procedure, and that regulations be drafted in cooperation with those to whom they apply. They rejected claims that political parties are behind the protest and emphasised that the gathering is organised independently, motivated by the problems of their members. “We have nothing against political support from all sides. Anyone who supports our demands is welcome. But no one stands behind us except ourselves. We determine our own demands, make decisions and organise the protest,” Samardžić stressed. Entrepreneurs, craftsmen, renters, workers, pensioners, students and all citizens who, as they state, want more money for living and more responsible management of public money have been invited to the protest.

World.title: Iraqi Airways resumes flights to Iran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Airways resumed flights between Najaf and Tehran on Thursday, with the first flight arriving in the Iranian capital after the airline obtained a US exemption allowing it to restart flights to Iran.

Iranian media reported that the Iraqi aircraft landed at Imam Khomeini International Airport (IKIA) at 7:30 a.m., marking the return of daily direct flights on the Najaf-Tehran route.

Iraqi Airways announced on Monday the resumption of direct flights to Iran starting October 8, as part of a plan to operate regular daily flights between Najaf International Airport and airports in Tehran, Mashhad, and Isfahan.

The Iraqi Ministry of Transport stated that the plan aims to facilitate passenger travel and provide regular air transport options between Iraq and Iranian cities.

The ministry revealed in late September that Iraq’s national carrier will resume flights to Iran in October, amid flight suspension due to US sanctions limiting services to Iranian airlines.

Iraq previously imposed a ban on flights to and from Iran to adhere to US sanctions. The Iraqi government sought exemptions for travel related to pilgrimage, medical treatment, and education.

According to a source in Iraq’s transport ministry, the US Treasury Department approved a one-month exception.

The US administration offered Iraqi Airways a one-month US Treasury waiver to fly between Iran and Najaf, with the possibility of a permanent exemption.

Baghdad offered to provide passenger screening and information exchange to prevent airplanes from transporting weapons, sanctioned individuals, or illegal funds.

World.title: Iraq’s oil revenues hit $5 billion per month
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, said on Thursday that the country’s oil exports during October are stable at a level of 2.7 million barrels per day, with the majority shipped from the southern terminals via the Strait of Hormuz.

Al-Rikabi explained that financial revenues generated from oil exports and other products range between $4.5 billion and $5 billion monthly, bolstering the country’s general budget.

Iraq’s oil exports increased in October to around 2.7 million barrels per day; approximately 2.4 million barrels come from the southern region, while export volumes from the northern region—including crude from Iraqi Kurdistan oilfields—range between 250,000 and 300,000 barrels per day.

These quantities are maintained despite the present crisis and challenges associated with production cuts, according to al-Rikabi.

The Iraqi official stressed that maintaining these export levels represents a big success for the Ministry of Oil.

Iraq’s oil exports include not only crude oil but also various petroleum products, such as fuel oil. The revenue generated from these exports contributes to the country’s federal budget.

World.title: ISIS claims responsibility for attack on Iraqi police in Kirkuk
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – ISIS claimed responsibility on Tuesday for an attack targeting Iraqi police forces southwest of the city of Kirkuk, which killed one police officer and injured others.

The attack is the first against Iraqi security forces since the withdrawal of the US-led international coalition from Iraq on September 30, ending the US military mission in the country.

The United States had led an international coalition to support Iraqi forces in their war against the terrorist group, including efforts to prevent the militant organization from regrouping.

Washington announced that it would continue to provide limited training and intelligence support following the withdrawal, with Iraqi forces assuming full responsibility for the country’s security and the suppression of the terrorist group’s remnants.

Prior to the pullout, Iraqi security officials cautioned that the group still has sleeper cells across Iraq, despite its defeat and the collapse of its rule in 2017.

The U.S. withdrawal raised concerns about a potential security vacuum that could give ISIS an opportunity to regain its strength, as some officials warned that Iraqi forces would now be compelled to contain the organization without foreign military presence.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: Stocks fall further as oil spike fans fresh inflation worries
World.content:
Hong Kong – Equities extended losses Thursday as inflation fears were stoked by a fresh jump in oil prices following a report that said Donald Trump was considering more Iran strikes ahead of next month’s US midterm elections.

The selling tracked a retreat on Wall Street, where tech firms pulled back from recent gains, having weathered concerns over spiking borrowing costs and geopolitical uncertainty.

Crude had started the week on the back foot thanks to signs that exports from the Middle East were heading back towards pre-war levels and that G7 nations had agreed to tap their stockpiles.

But anxiety returned as figures showed Tehran had increased strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, Houthis rebutted claims they had lost key territory and top oil officials warned that global reserves were running worryingly low.

And on Wednesday, The Atlantic reported that the White House had asked the Pentagon to draw up options to hit sites in Iran ahead of the midterms, with Trump’s Republicans in danger of losing both houses of Congress.

The article said the size and targets were still being discussed, but added that a wider operation could be in the works after the polls on November 3.

It added that even its proponents did not think the attacks would bring Tehran to talks or see Hormuz reopened, but hoped they would show strength leading into the vote.

Both main crude contracts rose more than one percent Thursday, with supplies also hit by the loss of more than 500,000 barrels of Gulf of Mexico output owing to producers shutting up shop as Tropical Storm Isaias approaches.

News that International Energy Agency members were ready to tap more oil from reserves did little to assuage worried traders.

The spike in oil prices fanned inflation fears again and put fresh upward pressure on government bond yields to multi-year highs.

After all three main indexes on Wall Street dropped — with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq off records — Asia followed suit.

Tokyo, Hong Kong, Sydney, Singapore, Seoul, Wellington, Taipei and Manila were all well down, though Shanghai edged up as investors returned from a week-long break.

– Tech earnings –

US Federal Reserve officials expect to hike interest rates again before the end of the year, according to minutes of their September meeting, where everyone agreed to the first increase since July 2023.

“With regard to the outlook for monetary policy beyond the current meeting, most participants assessed that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end,” the minutes said.

Several participants said they viewed the previous policy rate as not being adequately restrictive of economic activity, while they saw signs of renewed strength in the economy.

Investors are also gearing up for earnings season, with tech firms in the spotlight as questions over their profitability and elevated valuations swirl in light of the vast sums they have pumped into the AI sector.

“The headline earnings numbers may still be very strong. But with expectations elevated, valuations demanding and Treasury yields near multi-decade highs, the investment hurdle has become higher as well,” warned Charu Chanana at Saxo Markets.

“This season should therefore be less about simply identifying who beat consensus by the largest amount,” she said.

“The stronger businesses may be those that can deliver growth above expectations, convert that growth into cash, fund future investment from a strong balance sheet and still offer enough earnings upside to justify their valuation.”

South Korean titan Samsung’s shares fell as it forecast a more than 780 percent leap in third-quarter operating profit — thanks to high memory chip prices — but missed expectations.

It estimated July-September profit of 107.4 trillion won ($80.3 billion), up 782.5 percent on-year, but analysts on average had tipped 108.7 trillion won.

On currency markets, the euro remains wedged at lows last seen in June last year following another heavy fall amid worries about France’s high debt levels, which have spooked bond markets.

World.title: Samsung expects 780% quarterly operating profit jump on AI boom
World.content:
Seoul – Samsung Electronics forecast Thursday a more than 780 percent leap in third-quarter operating profit from a year earlier, buoyed by high memory chip prices as AI fuels a global supply shortage.

The South Korean giant is the world’s largest maker of memory chips — components now in huge demand as advanced types are snapped up for use in data centres powering artificial intelligence.

It estimated July-September operating profit at 107.4 trillion won ($80.1 billion), up 782.5 percent on-year, according to a company statement.

That would mark the first time a South Korean company has surpassed 100 trillion won in quarterly operating profit.

Revenue likely rose 127 percent to 195 trillion won, Samsung said.

With both numbers hitting all-time highs, the company will have broken its own records for both sales and operating profit for four consecutive quarters.

Samsung is expected to release its final quarterly earnings report at the end of October.

The AI boom has already helped Samsung and other semiconductor giants around the world post record profits this year.

Analysts at South Korean brokerage Shinhan Securities have struck a bullish stance on Samsung’s trajectory, writing in a note last week that they expected to see “even stronger earnings” from the company next year.

“Samsung Electronics now appears all set for a rapid increase in market share,” they said, as the company ramps up production of a new generation of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, called HBM4.

– Worker demands –

Samsung, its South Korean rival SK hynix and US giant Micron dominate the global market for HBM — advanced chips used in AI data centres alongside other powerful data-crunching semiconductors.

“The transition to next-generation HBM will open up the opportunity to renegotiate prices” for Samsung, “helping to guarantee solid margins,” the Shinhan Securities note said.

While Samsung’s earnings have surged on strong demand for the memory chips it produces, the boom has also pushed up prices for DRAM and NAND flash used in smartphones — forcing the company’s mobile division to pay more for the same chips.

Analysts say rising production costs have become increasingly difficult to absorb as Samsung seeks to limit price increases to maintain shipment volumes and market share.

In August, Samsung announced a buyback of up to $80 billion of its own stock to boost shareholder returns.

It said the shareholder return plan was designed to ensure that the “fruits of the company’s growth translate into tangible benefits” for shareholders.

As earnings skyrocket for chipmakers including Samsung, many workers are demanding a bigger cut of the profits.

Samsung averted a strike in South Korea earlier this year by agreeing to a deal to distribute bonuses equivalent to 10.5 percent of operating profit to its semiconductor employees.

The agreement means around 78,000 employees from Samsung’s 125,000-strong domestic workforce are eligible to receive a bonus of roughly $370,000 this year, based on a market estimate of profits.

But in Taiwan on Wednesday, union representatives said hundreds of workers at a Micron plant had voted in favour of a strike, after talks with the US company over bonus reforms collapsed.

World.title: Microsoft pushes AI vision with new, expensive Surface laptop
World.content:
San Francisco – Microsoft is pushing a “hybrid intelligence” future with a new Surface Ultra laptop that runs on Nvidia artificial intelligence (AI) chips and will cost more than $2,500, the company announced Wednesday.

The launch is part of a broader push by tech companies to release hardware that can handle more AI computing on-device and offline, so users don’t have to rely solely on remote cloud data centers, where running AI is slower and more expensive.

It also sees Nvidia, whose data center processors power the AI revolution, make a move into personal computing, a sector dominated for decades by chips from Intel and Qualcomm.

“The trajectory for me is so clear. There will never be a moment where we will go and look and say: ‘Oh, this runs locally, this runs in the cloud.’ You will expect this hybrid intelligence to be everywhere and pervasive,” CEO Satya Nadella said during an event in San Francisco.

He was joined onstage by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who echoed the idea that AI will be integrated into all computing going forward and on all devices.

Agentic AI, in particular, will be central to software development, Huang said, referring to systems programmed to be autonomous and perform tasks without supervision.

With all the changes from AI, “the computer has to be revolutionized,” Huang said.

The partnership between the two US-based tech titans helps them compete with Apple, Intel and AMD in the personal computing market.

Apple unveiled two desktop computers in September, the Mac mini and Mac Studio, which it touted as powerful new options capable of processing AI software locally.

Microsoft has been working on building “AI PCs” since at least 2024, when its laptops were powered by Qualcomm chips.

The new Surface Ultra will use Nvidia’s state-of-the-art AI chip, RTX Spark, which the semiconductor giant announced earlier this year.

It will cost $2,599 and begins shipping on October 16.

Some AI computing power and data will be processed locally, or on the device, while other applications are still handled remotely via Microsoft’s cloud computing services.

“We built it for developers and creators pushing the limits of performance,” Microsoft Executive Vice President of Windows and Device Pavan Davuluri said on Wednesday.

The news comes just a couple of weeks after Microsoft announced it would integrate Word, Excel and Powerpoint into its AI-powered assistant Copilot, in an effort to make AI the entry point for its famous suite of productivity software.

OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, and Claude-maker Anthropic each launched their own document creation tools in recent months.

The two San Francisco-based AI labs are also key suppliers for Microsoft, since Copilot runs primarily on their models.

Microsoft’s in-house models currently only power a few products, such as GitHub’s Copilot coding tool.

In June, Microsoft also unveiled its own cutting-edge artificial intelligence models — a crucial step toward reducing its dependence on OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT.

Microsoft, the first company to have invested massively in OpenAI, has for several years been seeking to reduce its reliance on its Sam Altman-led partner.

It renegotiated their alliance last year and retains only a non-exclusive license on its technology until 2032 though is OpenAI’s biggest shareholder.

World.title: Iraqi dinar’s exchange rate slightly rises following sharp decline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the Iraqi dinar compared to the US dollar slightly declined on Wednesday evening in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil, following a sharp rise earlier in the morning.

The US dollar exchange rate declined in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,670 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,685 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,675 Iraqi dinars and 1,665 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also declined, fluctuating between 1,667 and 1,666 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on Wednesday morning, following the cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved on Tuesday the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Iraq’s foreign reserves may fall to $60 billion by end of 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A Standard Chartered economist said on Wednesday that Iraq may resort to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) if oil revenues continue to fall and the currency’s devaluation fails to boost state finances as intended.

Standard Chartered chief economist for the Middle East and Pakistan Carla Slim said that any potential program with the IMF could entail structural reforms, particularly regarding the public sector wage bill, to enhance fiscal sustainability, Bloomberg reported.

If the current pace of depletion continues, Iraq’s foreign reserves might fall to roughly $60 billion by the end of the year, down from over $100 billion at the beginning of the year, according to Slim.

The economist indicated that the local currency’s exchange rate may be adjusted again in the future months, based on changes in oil earnings and foreign reserves.

According to IMF data, Iraq’s foreign currency reserves currently stand at approximately $85 billion.

Standard Chartered is a leading British multinational banking and financial services company headquartered in London.

World.title: Bajrang Dal says no volunteers to be mobilised at Jantar Mantar on October 10
World.content:
Bajrang Dal firmly refuted claims of organizing a gathering at Jantar Mantar on October 10 for their demonstration.

NEW DELHI: Bajrang Dal denied having any plans to gather its volunteers at Jantar Mantar on October 10 during the planned demonstration against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in response to claims that right-wing groups have been organized to use violence against the protesters.The Bajrang Dal said it had consistently opposed "anarchic protest" in the country and objected to demonstrations being held in the name of targeting Kumar, according to a post on X."Some people are engaged in spreading misleading propaganda about Bajrang Dal workers coming to Jantar Mantar. There is no such plan from the Bajrang Dal," it said.The statement followed an allegation by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Ashutosh Ranka, who claimed on X that a person "higher up in the BJP ranks" had told him that right-wing fringe groups were being mobilised from across the country to target peaceful protesters with violence, according to the PTI report.Ranka said the CJP's proposed October 10 demonstration would remain peaceful and warned that violence against people would not be tolerated.The Bajrang Dal, meanwhile, said the "so-called agitation" would meet its "natural death" without public support, similar to other such movements in the past.

World.title: India’s data silos cost up to 7% of welfare spending, threaten AI push: Report
World.content:
Citing a 2025 NITI Aayog assessment, the report estimated that poor-quality data causes leakage of 4-7% of India's annual welfare spending.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Even as India processes over 20 billion UPI transactions every month and has enrolled more than 1.4 billion people under Aadhaar, fragmented government databases continue to cause financial losses, exclude eligible beneficiaries from welfare schemes and threaten the countryâs AI ambitions, according to a report released on Thursday.The Tony Blair Institute for Global Change (TBI) report, From Digital Scale to Data Power: A Data Operating Model for Indiaâs States, said Indiaâs next digital challenge is not building more infrastructure but making existing government data accurate, accessible and usable across departments.Citing a 2025 NITI Aayog assessment, the report estimated that poor-quality data causes leakage of 4-7 per cent of India's annual welfare spending.It highlighted how past data-cleaning exercises helped remove 1.71 crore ineligible PM-KISAN beneficiaries, saving an estimated Rs 9,000 crore. Similarly, eliminating 3.5 crore bogus LPG connections saved Rs 21,000 crore over two years, while removing 1.6 crore fake ration cards is saving approximately Rs 10,000 crore annually.Despite these gains, government databases covering health, education, land records, taxation and welfare largely operate independently, limiting their usefulness for policy decisions.The report warned that deploying AI on fragmented or unreliable databases could amplify existing errors rather than improve public services.âIs the data good enough to trust an AI system, or a human official, to act on it? Right now, in most states, the honest answer is not yet,â said Vivek Agarwal, TBI country director and report co-author.Drawing on initiatives in Karnataka, Odisha and Rajasthan, the report proposed seven reforms, including common data standards, independent quality checks, stronger accountability and legal safeguards.It also recommended a State Data Balance Sheet to help governments track data assets and risks, arguing that reliable information must precede large-scale AI deployment in governance.

World.title: 'Dhappa' gets a Day 3 twist as police allow Rahul, INDIA bloc MPs to protest at Raj Ghat
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Thursday allowed opposition leaders to reach Raj Ghat, where they staged a brief protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. This came after two days of police stopping INDIA bloc leaders from marching to their chosen protest sites.

"INDIA alliance MPs staged a peaceful sit-in at Raj Ghat today. Here, they paid homage to Bapu and prayed for the Modi government to be endowed with sound judgment. Modi, Shah, and Gyanesh Kumar are together snatching away the public's right to vote. We will not allow this to happen under any circumstances," Congress said.

The change in police approach came on the third day of the opposition's protests over the report of "dissent" in the Election Commission, its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and allegations of "vote chori".

On Tuesday,

and opposition MPs were stopped as they marched near the Election Commission office. Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi subsequently ducked the cops and staged an eight-hour sit-in at the Akashvani Bhawan complex.

The Congress described the surprise move as "dhappa", a Hindi expression for a game of tag or hide-and-seek, and shared a map showing how Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi changed their route to enter the complex after policestopped their march.





The opposition met in central Delhi on Wednesday for lunch and, within an hour, attempted to march to Jantar Mantar but was stopped by police, with several leaders, including the Gandhi siblings, being detained. Police also registered FIRs in connection with the two flash protests.

On Thursday, the opposition once again came up with a new destination and decided to head to Raj Ghat after a lunch meeting hosted by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge at a restaurant in Connaught Place.

The leaders left the venue in buses, with Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other INDIA bloc leaders travelling together.

The convoy then reached Raj Ghat, where the leaders held a short protest before leaving.

The development was notable because Delhi Police had imposed prohibitory orders at Raj Ghat earlier in the day itself. However, despite the restrictions, the opposition leaders were allowed to reach the memorial.

Unlike the previous two days, there was no prolonged face-off between the protesters and police, or mass detention of opposition leaders.

The police action and detention of opposition leaders had itself become a major part of the political messaging in the last two days, with Congress leaders accusing the government of preventing them from exercising their right to protest.

Ahead of the protest, Rahul Gandhi continued his attack on the government and the Election Commission, alleging that Prime Minister Narendra Modi, home minister Amit Shah, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and CEC Gyanesh Kumar had "hijacked" India through a "criminal conspiracy".

He said they would be "brought to justice".

Kharge, meanwhile, said the INDIA bloc leaders would hold a peaceful sit-in at the Gandhi memorial and "pray" for Modi and Shah to be blessed with wisdom.

The BJP, meanwhile, hit out at the Congress. Addressing a press conference, spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari questioned Rahul Gandhi, alleging a lack of trust in the Supreme Court to deal with the appeals regarding the SIR exercise.

Attacking the Congress, the BJP leader framed it as a fight between the Gandhi-Vadra family and the people of India.

"The Congress party is fighting against 'We, the People of India.' This battle has become one of the Congress partyâits workers and the Gandhi-Vadra familyâversus the people of India, who are silently witnessing the party's hooliganism. They used to speak about returning to ballot papers. Yet, we recently saw elections held in places like Assam and Tripura; the Congress party lost there too, even though EVMs were not the only factor," Bhandari said.

World.title: Air India Delhi-Riyadh flight returns after Houthi attack on Saudi airport; flights ops suspended till October 10
World.content:
Air India Delhi-Riyadh flight returns after Houthi attack on Saudi airport

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: An Air India flight from Delhi to Riyadh is currently returning to Delhi after Houthi attacks on airports in Saudi Arabia left one person dead and eight injured, according to the latest information.Air India and Air India Express have suspended their operations to and from Riyadh until October 10, 2026, PTI reported citing Air India officials.Air India flight AI2243 had departed from Delhi and was flying south, over Gujarat, before proceeding over the Arabian Sea. The pilots subsequently turned the aircraft around and are currently flying back towards Delhi.The turnaround comes amid heightened concerns over safety in Saudi airspace following Houthi attacks targeting airports in the country, including King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.In a separate attack on King Khalid International Airport, one person was killed and eight others were injured, according to Saudi authorities cited by the BBC. The attack was among a series of strikes on Saudi airports over October 6 and 7.The Houthi group has claimed responsibility for the attacks, with its military spokesperson Yahya Saree saying the group targeted Saudi airports using ballistic missiles and drones.India on Thursday condemned the attacks on Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, calling the targeting of civilian infrastructure âcompletely unacceptableâ.âIndia condemns the attacks over the past few days targeting Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which have resulted in civilian deaths and injuries,â the MEA said.âThe targeting of civilian infrastructure is completely unacceptable. We express our deepest condolences to the families of those who have lost their loved ones. We wish speedy recovery for those injured. We express solidarity and stand with the people and government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,â it added.According to Saudi authorities cited by the BBC, attacks on the two airports over two days killed three people and injured 36 others. Two people were killed and 28 wounded in an attack on Abha International Airport, while one person was killed and eight injured in the attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.The latest attacks come amid renewed fighting between Saudi-backed government forces and the Iran-aligned Houthi group in Yemen.Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the attacks were carried out in âresponse to the Saudi aggression against our countryâ, claiming that Saudi Arabia had conducted â60 airstrikes and missile attacks in the past 24 hoursâ.The Houthi group also issued a âlast warningâ to global airlines operating flights through Saudi airspace, saying the area had become a âtheater for our military operationsâ.Saree claimed that a ballistic missile targeting King Khalid International Airport âstruck its target with precision and caused the disruption of airport operations.ââWe reiterate our call and warning "for the last time" to all global airlines regarding the consequences of continuing to operate flights in Saudi airspace, which has become a theater for our military operations,â Saree said.He added that airspace over the âsacred areasâ in Mecca and Medina was exempt from the warning.The US Mission in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday also urged American citizens to exercise heightened vigilance amid the Houthi threats, warning that the situation could lead to flight cancellations, airspace closures and other travel disruptions.

World.title: Centre to unveil AI regulation roadmap within a month; industry to shoulder safety responsibility
World.content:
New Delhi: The Centre will release a consultation paper within a month to lay the groundwork for India's next set of artificial intelligence (AI) regulations, focusing on safety, human welfare, skilling, inclusivity and protection against emerging risks such as deepfakes and psychological harm.

Announcing this at the launch of the World Bank's World Development Report 2026 on Thursday, electronics and IT minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the government would adopt a techno-legal approach rather than rely solely on legislation, with industry expected to shoulder the primary responsibility for ensuring safety.

"Bulk of this regulation will have to be taken by the industries. Bulk of the responsibility will have to be taken by the industry," he said, flagging cybersecurity, deepfakes and psychological harm as major concerns.

The minister also announced the next phase of India's AI computing infrastructure expansion, with the government initiating long-term procurement of 10,000 graphics processing units (GPUs), including an initial tender for 5,000. The proposed procurement arrangement would provide demand visibility for five years.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

In another development, Vaishnaw said India now has a visible three-to-four-year roadmap for developing indigenous GPUs capable of running AI models, particularly for inference.





Further details would be announced in the coming months.

The government will also empanel AI models and solutions for official use, allowing selected companies and startups to subsequently compete for departmental contracts.

Emphasising wider access to AI, Vaishnaw said its benefits must extend beyond large technology companies to farmers, students, researchers and small businesses.

World.title: Evening news wrap: Nana Patekar passes away, stock market crash, Rahul Gandhi's Day 3 protest and more
World.content:
Nana Patekar passed away, stock market crash, Rahul Gandhi escalates attack on govt

42 former judges in an open letter extended their support for chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Veteran actor Nana Patekar passes away at the age of 75 due to cardiac arrest and his last rites to be held in Pune.

Canadian author Anne Carson has won the 2026 Nobel Prize in literature, announced by the Swedish Academy.

Rahul Gandhi alleged that the government and the Election Commission had "hijacked India" and "stolen votes".

BSE Sensex and Nifty50, the Indian equity benchmarks, crashed in trade, with both indices down over 1%.

Here are the top stories of the day:

'Campaign driven by political interests': 42 ex-judges back CEC in open letter

Nana Patekar passes away at 75: Actor's last rites to be held at his Pune farmhouse

Canadian author Anne Carson awarded 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature

'Criminal conspiracy to hijack India': Rahul ups ante against government, CEC
