Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex tanks over 1,000 points; Nifty50 at 22,231 - top reasons for fall

Forty-two former judges on Thursday voiced concern over protests targeting chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, objecting to the labels such as "puppet", "thief" and "compromised" being used against him.In an open letter, the former judges described the criticism as a "calculated campaign driven by vested political interests" and cautioned against attempts to undermine election officials through public attacks and intimidation.The signatories also took exception to election officers being subjected to name-calling and public shaming, along with "warning of reprisal once power changes hands"."This appears to be a calculated campaign driven by vested political interests, with little regard to the potentially devastating consequences of destabilising the worldâs largest democracy," the 42 former judges said.Veteran actor Nana Patekar has died at the age of 75 after suffering a severe cardiac arrest. He was found unconscious at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa, following which he was taken to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead.Dr Shekhar Salkar, chief of the oncology department at Manipal Hospital, said that doctors attempted to revive the actor through continuous CPR for 45 minutes, but were unsuccessful. A medico-legal case (MLC) has been registered, and a post-mortem examination is underway.Hungarian novelist and screenwriter LÃ¡szlÃ³ Krasznahorkai has been awarded the 2025 Nobel Prize in literature for what the Swedish Academy called his "compelling and visionary oeuvre that, in the midst of apocalyptic terror, reaffirms the power of art".Born in 1954 in Gyula, Hungary, Krasznahorkai is recognised for novels featuring lengthy, intricate sentences, bleak settings, absurdity and a recurring sense of impending disaster. His works frequently portray individuals navigating societies characterised by collapse, disorder and uncertainty.The standoff between the INDIA bloc and the Election Commission intensified as opposition leaders gathered in Delhi for the third consecutive day of protests.Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi said around 300 MPs from both Houses of Parliament wanted to hold a peaceful demonstration but had been prevented from doing so for the past two days.Rahul, who was detained during Wednesday's protest, said the opposition would continue its campaign against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He alleged that the government and the Election Commission had "hijacked India" and "stolen votes".The Congress leader also said the opposition would pursue the matter until those it holds responsible are brought to justice.Indian equity benchmarks BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty50 fell sharply on Thursday, with both indices declining more than 1%, as investors reacted to the Reserve Bank of Indiaâs policy tightening and repo rate hike, continued foreign institutional investor (FII) selling and other negative market cues.The Sensex dropped more than 1,000 points during the session, while the Nifty50 slipped to around the 22,231 level.At the close, the Nifty50 stood at 22,231.80, down 371.25 points, or 1.64%. The Sensex ended at 71,593.24, lower by 1,045.46 points, or 1.44%.The sharp sell-off wiped out more than Rs 11 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of companies listed on the BSE.

World.title: Delhi liquor shops to remain closed on Oct 9-10 amid ‘prevailing’ situation
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Liquor shops in the national capital will remain closed on October 9 and 10 in view of the âprevailingâ situation in the city, according to an order, cited by news agency PTI.

The department said the decision to shut liquor vends was taken on the basis of inputs from the Delhi Police and as a preventive measure to maintain âpublic orderâ. The closure comes amid protests by opposition parties and other groups demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations linked to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

A protest has also been called at Jantar Mantar on October 10 by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), while several student groups have joined demands for Kumarâs resignation.

The groups have alleged that lakhs of voters were deleted from electoral rolls during the SIR exercise.

More than 20,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across Delhi ahead of the planned protest, a senior police officer said on Thursday. The officer said no permission had been granted for any protest at Jantar Mantar and appealed to people to stay away from unauthorised gatherings.

âWe are well prepared and motivated to handle the law-and-order situation in the city on Saturday. No permission has been granted so far for any protest at Jantar Mantar,â the officer said.

The deployment has been made as a precautionary measure to prevent any breach of peace and ensure the smooth movement of traffic and people. Prohibitory orders are already in force in the area, police said.

World.title: CBI busts multi-state IBPS exam impersonation racket; CGST inspector among 4 arrested
World.content:
NEW DELHI: CBI has busted a widespread impersonation and cheating network operating in banking exams across Delhi, Bihar, Haryana and West Bengal and arrested four key operatives including a CGST inspector.

Following a First Information Report (FIR) registered on a complaint filed by the institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS), the CBI Special Task Branch Mumbai executed coordinated, multi-state raids and arrested four individuals.

The gang fraudulently infiltrated multiple stages of the selection process including written examinations and interviews by physically posing as candidates undermining the integrity of public examinations and depriving genuine, hardworking aspirants of their rightful opportunities.

"The CBI's investigation is ongoing in respect of others involved in the racket," the agency said.

World.title: Tamil Nadu government relaxes domicile clause for Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram scheme
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) relaxed the eligibility criteria for the Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam, amending the guidelines to include children whose mothers were born in Tamil Nadu but had moved to another State after marriage, provided their parents reside permanently in Tamil Nadu.

Under the scheme, a one-gram gold ring is provided to children born in government hospitals in Tamil Nadu. The scheme was launched by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on September 28 and is being implemented retrospectively from June 22, 2026.

The Government Order, issued by the Health and Family Welfare Department, prescribes the guidelines for the scheme.

“While implementing the scheme, it came to the government’s notice that in some cases, women from Tamil Nadu who had been living in another State after marriage, but whose parents continued to reside permanently in Tamil Nadu, returned to their parental homes for childbirth and delivered their babies in the government hospitals in Tamil Nadu,” said Darez Ahamed, Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, in an official release.

One such case was that of Uma Maheswari, who, after marriage, has been living with her husband at Udayagiri in Mysuru district of Karnataka. Her parents reside in Karaikudi in Sivaganga district. She came to Tamil Nadu, for childbirth and delivered a baby at the Karaikudi Government Headquarters Hospital on September 17.

Under the conditions that were in force, the family was initially unable to benefit under the scheme, as the mother who had delivered the child was required to be a permanent resident of Tamil Nadu. Considering this, the government has decided to expand the eligibility conditions under the scheme, the release said.

As per the new guidelines, if the mother of a child born in a government hospital was born in Tamil Nadu and had moved to another State after marriage, but her parents are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu, the child will also be provided a gold ring on submission of relevant documentary evidence. Accordingly, Ms. Maheswari was provided a one-gram gold ring.

The amendment will also apply retrospectively to eligible children from June 22, 2026, the release added.

World.title: JOSH team introduced in Thoothukudi to intensify TB awareness and prevention activities
World.content:
As part of the TB-free India campaign, the JOSH (Joint Squad for Health) team comprising youth and volunteers was introduced in Thoothukudi district to intensity awareness and preventive measures against tuberculosis (TB).

District Collector Vishu Mahajan introduced the team on Thursday and presented certificates of appreciation and shields to 75 village panchayats in the district that had been identified as TB-free.

Speaking on the occasion, the Collector said that the Central Tuberculosis Division in collaboration with MY Bharat is conducting a nationwide community-based survey across 55 districts to assess awareness about tuberculosis under the TB-Free India campaign.

Pointing out that Thoothukudi, Tiruchi, Cuddalore, Dharmapuri and Theni districts have been selected for the initiative from Tamil Nadu, he noted that in the selected villages in these districts various community level activities will be carried out with the support of MY Bharat and NCC Students.

He appealed to the public to actively participate in TB elimination efforts and extend full cooperation to JOSH team members during the door-to-door assessment.

People experiencing cough or fever for two weeks or more, unexplained weight loss, excessive night sweats or other symptoms associated with TB should approach the nearest Primary Health Centre (PHC) for TB screening and appropriate medical treatment, Mr. Mahajan added.

The Collector also called upon officials from all government departments, local bodies, educational institutions, youth organisations, NCC, MY Bharat volunteers and the general public to work together to make Thoothukudi a TB-free district.

In the financial year 2025-2026, of the 403 village panchayats in the district, 75 were selected as TB-free gram panchayats based on prescribed criteria. Of these, 12 gram panchayats received silver awards and 63 received bronze awards.

Earlier participants took the tuberculosis elimination pledge under the leadership of the District Collector.

Joint Director (Health) G. Priyadharshini, Deputy Director (Tuberculosis) Sundaralingam, Medical Superintendent of Thoothukudi Government Medical College Hospital R. Padmanabhan and other officials were present.

World.title: Chennai Night Run to promote fitness and women’s safety
World.content:
The prelude event to the Mindspace REIT Chennai Night Run 2026 was held on Thursday ahead of the run scheduled for October 17. Organsied by SportzPro in association with the Tamil Nadu Athletic Association (TNAA) and supported by the Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu (SDAT), SIMS Hospital and State Bank of India with Mindspace Business Parks REIT headlining the event.

The run will start at 7 p.m. from Island Grounds and will include two categories: 10K timed run and 4K family run. The fastest runners will be awarded cash prizes. C. Latha, Chairman - Planning & Execution Committee, Tamil Nadu Athletic Association, spoke about how the run aims to promote athletics, especially encouraging women to participate.

“When we did our survey with our employees post COVID-19, many were reluctant to work from office. That is when we received feedback that sports facilities are very integral. This run is taking the philosophy beyond our campus gates,” said Ramesh Nair, MD and CEO, Mindspace REIT. Asian Games’26 bronze medallist Abinaya Rajarajan spoke about how runs and marathons could contribute to improving fitness levels among people in the long run.

Promoting women’s safety is the primary focus of the event. The night run, organisers said, is symbolic of the need for women to feel safe navigating the city even after dark. Chief guest of the event Sabarinathan R., MLA of Virugampakkam constituency; Raju Sivaswamy, vice president, SIMS Hospitals; Vivekanand Choubey, Chief General Manager at State Bank of India, also spoke. Registrations for the run are currently open through the official website www.chennainightrun.com

World.title: Karnataka’s pending dues: ‘Good news’ after talks with Finance Minister, says Shivakumar
World.content:
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Thursday said he had received “some good news” regarding Karnataka’s pending dues following a discussion with the Union Finance Minister. He, however, declined to disclose details.

“I will talk about it later,” Mr. Shivakumar told reporters in Delhi after attending the GST Council meeting. He said the meeting had gone well and that Karnataka’s concerns had received broad support.

Sources indicated that the “good news” referred to pending dues of Upper Bhadra Project, to the tune of ₹5,300 crore that was announced in the Union Budget of 2023-2024.

The issue of initiating criminal proceedings and arresting those who fail to pay GST was also discussed at the meeting, he said. Mr. Shivakumar said such action should not be taken indiscriminately by officials and that the focus should be on recovering the tax dues in accordance with the applicable rules.

“Provisions of the Income Tax Act and rules should be followed. It is not right for officials to unnecessarily arrest traders. Let the amount that is due be recovered from them. Arresting them is not right,” he said.

According to the Chief Minister, all States except one supported the view during the discussion.

World.title: JSS STU-Bajaj initiative to train 720 youth in three years
World.content:
JSS Science and Technology University (JSSSTU), in association with the Bajaj Auto Foundation, Pune, has launched a free three-month skill training programme for unemployed youth in two-wheeler repair and maintenance.

The Service Technician Excellence Programme (STEP) Skill Training Centre was inaugurated at the JSS Technical Institutions Campus here. The programme is being offered as a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative of the Bajaj Auto Foundation.

The hands-on programme, including on-the-job training, is aimed at equipping young men and women with industry-relevant skills and improving their employment prospects in the growing two-wheeler service sector, a press release said.

The inaugural batch will have 60 seats, with 30 seats each for Electric Vehicle (EV) repair and servicing and Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) repair and servicing.

The details were shared at a press conference here on Thursday by B. Elangovan, deputy director, Technical Education Division, JSS Mahavidyapeetha; Dr. Maheshan, associate professor and assistant registrar (Administration), JSSSTU; and Dr. Manjunatha B., associate professor and skill development officer, JSSSTU.

Candidates who have passed PUC, Diploma or ITI and have knowledge of Science and Mathematics are eligible for the EV course. For the ICE course, candidates who have passed SSLC, PUC, ITI or Diploma can apply, the release added.

The university plans to conduct a series of such programmes, targeting about 240 candidates annually and 720 candidates over three years. Successful trainees will be provided placement assistance in service stations, authorised dealerships, showrooms and automobile enterprises.

Interested candidates can collect and submit application forms on or before October 25. They should submit copies of marks cards or educational certificates, Aadhaar card, income/caste certificate and two recent passport-size photographs to the Coordinator, JSSSTU–Bajaj-STEP, Technical Education Division, JSS Technical Institutions Campus, Mysuru–570006. For details, contact 9901628639.

World.title: CITU backs strike by contract health employees
World.content:
The Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU) Andhra Pradesh State committee has extended its support to the indefinite statewide strike by 14,600 employees of the Andhra Pradesh Medical and Health Contract Employees Joint Action Committee (JAC), with the agitation entering its third day on Thursday.

CITU State president Ch. Narsinga Rao, who addressed the strike camp at King George Hospital, urged the State government to intervene and resolve the employees’ grievances.

He demanded that the showcause notices issued to the striking employees be withdrawn and that officials stop threatening them. He said direct-contract staff nurses, laboratory technicians, pharmacists and other paramedical personnel who had been working in the medical and health department for 16 years should be regularised.

Mr. Narsinga Rao also urged the government to take into consideration the High Court judgment cited by the employees in support of their demand for regularisation.

He said the CITU would directly join the strike across the State if the government failed to resolve the issue. He assured the striking employees of the union’s support.

Visakhapatnam district CITU general secretary R.K.S.V. Kumar, district treasurer S. Jyothiswarao and vice-presidents P. Mani and P. Venkatarao were present.

EOM

World.title: Ola Electric ordered to refund scooter cost with 10% interest
World.content:
The Dharwad District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed Ola Electric to refund ₹1,03,999 paid by a Hubballi resident for an electric scooter, along with 10% annual interest, after finding deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.

The Commission also directed the company to pay ₹50,000 as compensation for the inconvenience and mental agony caused to the consumer, besides ₹10,000 towards litigation expenses.

The complaint was filed by Satish Miskin of Hubballi, who had purchased an Ola Electric scooter from the company’s outlet at Unkal Cross in Hubballi for ₹1,03,999.

According to the complaint, the scooter developed battery-related and other defects and was handed over to the company’s service centre for repairs. Despite repeated requests, the company allegedly failed to return the vehicle, stating that the required spare parts had not arrived.

When the complainant subsequently visited the service centre, he found it closed. His attempts to contact the company and ascertain the whereabouts of the vehicle were unsuccessful, while the scooter remained in the company’s possession.

The consumer filed a complaint before the Dharwad District Consumer Commission on January 22, 2026, seeking the return of his vehicle and action against the company for deficiency in service.

The Commission, comprising president Eshappa Bhute and members Vishalakshi A. Bolshetty and Prabhu S. Hiremath, observed that the complainant had purchased the vehicle by investing over ₹1 lakh for his personal convenience. The records showed that the scooter had developed battery and other defects and had been handed over to the company for repairs during the warranty period.

The Commission held that the manufacturer was obliged to rectify the defects and return the vehicle to the consumer. Retaining the vehicle without repairing and returning it amounted to deficiency in service and an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act, it said.

The Commission also took note of complaints regarding problems faced by consumers with Ola Electric scooters and proceedings before consumer authorities and courts concerning the quality and service of such vehicles.

On these grounds, the Commission ordered Ola Electric to refund the scooter’s purchase price of ₹1,03,999 with 10% interest, besides paying ₹50,000 as compensation and ₹10,000 towards litigation costs.

World.title: Sensex hits a three-year low amid rising crude prices, reaction to RBI policy
World.content:
The benchmark index Nifty 50 closed at its lowest level since 18 months on Thursday (October 8, 2026) while the BSE Sensex dropped 1.4%, to its lowest level since February 13, 2024.

Market analysts suggest multiple factors including rising global crude oil prices, persistent decline in the rupee, and cautionary onset of Q2 (July-September) earnings season contributed to the market’s movement.

Thursday’s (October 8, 2026) fall followed a sharp reaction by the markets on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) to the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee’s (MPC) decision to hike interest rates by 5 bps and change its stance, with the rupee dropping as low as 96.85 per dollar and the stock indices declining from 1.4%-1.6%.

Expect further fall

“During the session, the Nifty breached the previous swing-low support at 22,217 as well as the key April 2026 swing low of 22,182,” Nandish Shah, deputy vice president, HDFC Securities said in a report. “The decisive breakdown of these levels indicates a further escalation in selling pressure and an intensification of the ongoing downtrend.”

Ajit Mishra, senior vice-president of research at Religare Broking added that the market recovery that occurred between April and August is over now and that the market will likely fall further.

“For our markets, the factors are mixed including crude at $103 per barrel, rupee near 97 per dollar and caution ahead of earnings season,” Mr. Mishra said. According to him, in the near-term, the Nifty 50’s immediate support range is seen between 21,700 to 22,000.

Oil prices rose 4% on Thursday (October 8, 2026) following no signs of easing in the West Asia conflict and on worries over supply from the region amid increasing attacks on shipping. Brent crude futures rose $4.14 to $102.28 per barrel while the West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures rose $3.71 to $91.99 per barrel.

Carryover from day before

The domestic market extended the losses from Wednesday (October 7, 2026) following worries over uncertainty about the tightening domestic and global monetary conditions.

Though the markets priced in the 25 basis points rate hike by the MPC, what surprised them was the change in policy stance to ‘calibrated tightening’ from neutral, leaving markets unsure of how much the rates will be hiked going forward and for how long.

“Looking ahead, the market focus shifts to the Q2 earnings season, where management commentary on demand sustainability and input cost absorption will provide critical near-term direction,” Vinod Nair, head of research, at Geojit Investments Limited said in a note.

Meanwhile, Asian markets too traded lower on Thursday (October 8, 2026) as global investors amid increased risk-averse appetite to rising crude prices and elevated U.S. Treasury yields. Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell nearly 1.13% while South Korea’s KOSPI declined 2.26%. Hang Seng was down 1.4%.

World.title: 'Fake and fabricated': Info ministry rejects NYT report claiming PAF jets being used against Yemen's Houthis
World.content:
The Ministry of Information dismissed on Thursday a news report claiming that Pakistan Air Force (PAF) aircraft were being used against the Yemen’s Houthis as “fake and fabricated”.

A New York Times report published on Oct 7, a screenshot of which the ministry shared in an X post, cited an unnamed source as saying that PAF fighter jets were being employed against the group, amid the latter’s escalating conflict with Saudi Arabia.

But the information ministry denied the report, saying in a post on X that the NYT story “attributing the employment of PAF aircraft against Houthis is fake and fabricated”.

“International media houses are again asked to avoid speculative reporting with regards to employment of Pakistan’s military forces under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.

“Details of any deployment, if necessary, will be given by the authorities concerned,” it added.

Earlier this week, the ministry also termed a Reuters report claiming the deployment of 30,000 to 40,000 Pakistani troops in Saudi Arabia as “speculative”.

The development comes after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agreed to the deployment of military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom during an emergency meeting of the Makkah Defence Alliance in Riyadh on Monday.

The defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Monday’s meeting under the alliance was held to address the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia.

A statement issued by the Foreign Office after the meeting said the member states had “decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the kingdom, in accordance with the approved arrangements and the national legislation of the parties, thereby enhancing readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats”.

Separately, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who was part of Pakistan’s delegation in the meeting, joined Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’ via telephone the same day and said Saudi Arabia had made “gains and recovered some areas” in Yemen in the ongoing fighting with the Houthis.

Asked about a possible operational role by Pakistan and Turkiye, the defence minister replied that both nations had a “presence in theatre”, but only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations.

On Wednesday, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry also said Pakistani troops are in Saudi Arabia, adding that they had been in the kingdom “for decades” and across multiple domains.

Escalating tensions

The Houthis have declared a maritime blockade on the kingdom and targeting its ships in the Red Sea. Both sides have claimed strikes on each other as tensions remain high.

On Thursday, the Houthis claimed that they had struck the Saudi capital’s main international airport with a ballistic missile, in another attack on the kingdom claimed by the group.

A day ago, Saudi authorities said three people were killed and 36 injured in attacks on two of the kingdom’s international airports including in the capital Riyadh, after Yemen’s Houthis claimed to have fired on both transport hubs.

For its part, a Saudi-led coalition that backs pro-government forces in Yemen said on X that it “destroyed the ballistic missile launch platform” used in the attack on Riyadh.

The Houthis, who control most of the country’s northwest, are battling for territory against the Saudi-backed forces after the civil war reignited in July and they captured swathes of coastal land.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government this week declared a major counter-offensive and said Houthi fighters were pushed out of strategic areas on the Red Sea and the port city of Mocha.

But the Houthis say they are holding their territory, and military sources from both sides contacted by AFP have not reported any major changes on the ground.

Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify with the situation moving fast and access for journalists difficult.

Meanwhile, Pakistan has expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia.

On Sept 18, Lt Gen Chaudhry said Pakistan would go to “any extent” to defend the Gulf state, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security is “unconditional”.

Asif has also reaffirmed that Pakistan will “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalates. The defence minister said that Pakistan would fulfil all its obligations under the Makkah Defence Alliance in accordance with the terms of the agreement between the three countries.

At the same time, Pakistan has also asserted that the alliance is intended for collective deterrence and defensive in nature.

World.title: Bahrain working to 'speed up' approval of Pak-GCC free trade pact, foreign minister says
World.content:
Bahrain on Thursday said it was working to “speed up” the approval of a free trade agreement between Pakistan and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC).

The remarks came after the two countries held the third session of their Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) in Islamabad.

Bahrain’s FM Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani — who arrived in Pakistan last night on a two-day visit — co-chaired the JMC session along with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.

Addressing a joint press briefing with Dar, the Bahraini minister noted that the JMC meeting covered “more than 15 fields”.

He said both sides agreed to establish a joint working group on trade and investment, as well as to convene the joint working group on energy next month on oil, gas and minerals.

They also agreed to take forward cooperation in food security, information technology, law enforcement, media, labour mobility, health, education, culture and sports.

“We also committed to finalising the GCC-Pakistan free trade agreement,” he said, referring to the potential deal that was said to be near finalisation in late 2025.

The minister said that Bahrain, having the GCC presidency, was working to “speed up the signing or the approval of the GCC-Pakistan FTA”.

Responding to a query, the visiting dignitary described the bilateral relationship between Pakistan and Bahrain as “very healthy and strong”.

He added that it was “radiant and well-looked after” by Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and Crown Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa. “It is really valued by the people of Bahrain,” he added.

Highlighting recent bilateral exchanges between their countries, FM Al Zayani said: “We have a very truthful relationship; we are so frank with each other. We understand the constraints on each other and work accordingly.”

Emphasising the consistency in their ties, with no “ups and downs”, he said, “We are consistent and growing. We feel safe in this relationship.”

Al Zayani expressed Manama’s appreciation for Islamabad’s “principled positions on the ongoing crisis”, including its support in March for a United Nations Security Council resolution condemning Iranian attacks on GCC countries.

The minister also praised Pakistan’s “efforts alongside other partners to facilitate US-Iran dialogue and de-escalation, including by hosting the Islamabad Talks” in April.

The Bahrain FM went on to strongly condemn the recent deadly “terrorist attacks” on Saudi Arabia’s Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport.

He also condemned the “Houthi terrorist militia’s attacks on civilians and civilian facilities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and its assault” on the holy cities of Makkah and Madina.

Noting that targeting of civilian facilities was a “flagrant violation” of international law, Al Zayani affirmed Bahrain’s solidarity with Saudi Arabia “whose security is an integral part of our own and of the GCC”.

The Bahrain FM said he and Dar also discussed the crises in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, where “commercial vessels continue to come under attack”.

They underscored the importance of freedom and safety of navigation and respect for international law, he added.

Al Zayani vowed Bahrain and Pakistan will continue “close coordination” at the UNSC and between their Missions in New York.

Furthermore, the visiting FM noted that the two countries will mark 55 years of diplomatic relations on Oct 14.

Al Zayani remarked that the “bonds of brotherhood, trust and solidarity […] gained fresh momentum with the official visits to Bahrain” of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in November 2025 and of President Asif Ali Zardari in January this year.

The minister noted that more than 140,000 Pakistanis in Bahrain contributed to its progress and “form a living bridge between our peoples”.

The Bahrain FM said he would also meet with PM Shehbaz, President Zardari and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir during his visit.

Gulf situation, Palestine, IWT discussed

In his remarks, Dar thanked Al Zayani and his delegation for “their constructive engagement and their very valuable contribution to the success of today’s JMC session”.

Noting that the discussions were held in a cordial and constructive atmosphere, he said both sides “reaffirmed our shared commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation across a broad spectrum of sectors”.

“A key outcome of the session was the strengthening of our institutional framework through the operationalisation of several joint working groups,” Dar said, adding that these mechanisms will help ensure effective implementation of the decisions taken by the JMC.

“Both sides also agreed to enhance cooperation in trade and investment promotion, industrial collaboration, agriculture and food security, skills development, higher education, information technology, logistics and maritime affairs, among many other areas.”

They “particularly welcomed closer engagement between the business communities of the two countries”, the deputy premier added.

Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in labour mobility, vocational training and human resource development, with a view to creating new opportunities for skilled Pakistani professionals and workers.

Dar noted that he and Al Zayani also exchanged views on the “evolving situation in the Gulf and emphasised the importance of restraint, de-escalation, dialogue and diplomacy”.

“We discussed the need to ensure the safety and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab, given their importance to regional and global food and energy security.”

The ministers also discussed the “grave situation in Palestine” and expressed concern over the “continued expansion of illegal settlements and attempts to alter the status of Al-Quds Al-Sharif”.

Dar also raised the issue of India’s unilateral decision to place the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, terming it a “material breach of international law”.

“Such actions jeopardise the water, food and energy security of Pakistan’s 250 million people,” the deputy premier stressed.

“Pakistan-Bahrain friendship remains strong and forward-looking, and we are brotherly nations, with long fraternal ties, cooperating on international foras and meeting very frequently wherever we get an opportunity like brothers,” the DPM affirmed.

He expressed Pakistan’s commitment to “building an even more prosperous future together, God-willing, and taking the trade and economic ties to a new height”.

Dar said Islamabad looked forward to the convening of the JMC’s fourth session in Bahrain in 2027, as both sides will try to hold the meetings every year.

President Zardari meets Bahrain FM

Separately, President Zardari met with the Bahrain foreign minister, who called on him at the President House.

According to a press release by the president’s secretariat, the two leaders first held a restricted meeting, which was followed by a delegation-level meeting.

Zardari, in conversation with Al Zayani, said that Pakistan was “keen to translate strong bilateral political relations into deeper trade and investment ties”, according to the statement.

Noting that the country attached “great importance” to its relations with Bahrain, he expressed the desire to further strengthen bilateral cooperation, highlighting opportunities for this cooperation in “food security, IT and digital services, construction, mining, port handling, research and development, tourism and healthcare”. He also encouraged greater business-to-business engagement between the two countries.

“The president appreciated Bahrain’s warm welcome of the Islamabad MoU and the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and its recognition of Pakistan’s efforts for regional peace, security and stability,” the press release said.

It added that President Zardari also appreciated Bahrain’s support and opportunities for over 134,000 Pakistanis residing in the kingdom, and welcomed continued cooperation on matters regarding the Pakistani diaspora.

“The president said Pakistan and Bahrain share a long-standing and trusted defence partnership, reflected in joint exercises, high-level exchanges and institutional cooperation,” it said, adding that he expressed Pakistan’s readiness to further strengthen cooperation in manpower, logistics, training and defence hardware.

On the topic of the regional situation, he expressed Pakistan’s commitment to constructive engagement with all parties to “build trust, bridge gaps and promote lasting peace, security and stability in the region”.

During the meeting, Al Zayani conveyed the greetings of King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, the crown prince and prime minister of Bahrain, to the president, the statement added.

He termed the JMC meetings “highly productive” and noted that the president’s visit to Bahrain had left “a significant and positive impact on bilateral relations”.

He commended Pakistan’s courageous efforts to mediate amid the current regional situation and bring warring parties to the table, saying that Pakistan’s actions had “helped save many lives”. He appreciated Pakistan’s peace efforts and congratulated it on its successful tenure as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council.

Meeting with PM Shehbaz

The foreign minister also called on PM Shehbaz, who warmly welcomed him and conveyed his best wishes to the leadership and people of Bahrain, according to a press release by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

He reaffirmed Pakistan’s “deep appreciation for the longstanding and brotherly relations between Pakistan and Bahrain, founded on shared values, mutual trust, and close people-to-people ties”, the PMO said.

PM Shehbaz expressed his satisfaction over the positive trajectory of bilateral relations. He emphasised Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening cooperation with Bahrain in diverse fields, “including trade, investment, energy, and human resource development”.

FM Al-Zayani, meanwhile, conveyed the greetings and well-wishes of the leadership of Bahrain to the premier, and reaffirmed Bahrain’s commitment to further enhancing bilateral cooperation across mutually beneficial areas.

“The two sides exchanged views on regional and international developments and emphasised the importance of continued consultations and coordination on issues of mutual interest,” the statement said.

Al-Zayani “appreciated Pakistan’s constructive role and mediation efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability in the region”, the PMO added.

The prime minister expressed confidence that the JMC session would provide “further impetus” to bilateral cooperation and help deepen the relationship between the two countries.

“The meeting was held in a warm and cordial atmosphere, reflecting the close and longstanding fraternal ties between Pakistan and Bahrain,” the statement added.

JMC meeting

During the JMC meeting, Islamabad and Manama “agreed to deepen collaboration in trade and investment, energy, agriculture and food security, information technology, health, education and labour”, FO said.

They also discussed measures to strengthen connectivity and promote people-to-people exchanges.

Dar “underscored the importance of translating the longstanding and fraternal ties between Pakistan and Bahrain into tangible benefits for their people”.

He further stressed effective implementation of the agreed outcomes through joint working groups, institutional partnerships and regular follow-up, FO added.

The JMC was attended by high-level delegations from both sides.

The Pakistani team included the secretaries of the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) and the Economic Affairs Division, along with the acting foreign secretary. The Bahraini side included senior officials and representatives of the Bahrain Chamber of Commerce and Industry.

In his address to the JMC meeting, Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to increase bilateral trade with Bahrain to the $1 billion target set earlier.

Noting the target of doubling trade in three years, of which one has already elapsed, Dar quipped, “But God forbid, if we miss [the target by] a few months, we have a great excuse that this period has been very turbulent.”

Dar also referred to the potential Pakistan-GCC FTA, noting that the GCC secretary general told him the deal was “almost ripe”, with one country yet to give a green light to it.

“I’m sure the signing of the free trade agreement between the GCC and Pakistan will surely help us in achieving our goals,” the deputy premier said, adding that it would lead to an increase in imports and exports.

He requested the Bahraini side to work towards recognising degrees and professional qualifications, while facilitating greater mobility of skilled labour between the two countries.

Later, the two ministers signed the protocol recording the minutes of the JMC session at the foreign ministry, according to the FO.

“The minutes record understandings on cooperation in trade and investment, agriculture and food security, oil, gas and minerals, maritime affairs, information technology and telecommunications, health, education and labour, among other areas,” the FO statement said.

It added that both sides agreed to establish a Joint Working Group on Trade and Investment at the government level, as an institutional mechanism for “regular consultations, coordination and cooperation on bilateral trade and investment”.

Bilateral meeting

Prior to the Pakistan-Bahrain JMC, the two foreign ministers also held a separate meeting after Al Zayani’s arrival at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

In a post on X about the “cordial” meeting, the Foreign Office (FO) said the two ministers “reviewed Pakistan–Bahrain relations and expressed satisfaction at the positive momentum in high-level engagement between the two countries”.

“They discussed ways to further expand bilateral cooperation across areas of mutual interest, particularly in trade, economic and investment relations, as well as through engagement at multilateral fora.”

The two sides also exchanged views on “regional and international developments of mutual interest and underscored that dialogue and diplomacy remain the most viable means of addressing challenges and resolving disputes”, the FO added.

According to an earlier FO statement, the two sides were to “review the entire spectrum of bilateral relations and discuss ways to further strengthen cooperation across diverse areas of mutual interest, including trade, investment, economic cooperation, defence and security, labour and manpower, and cultural exchanges”.

“Pakistan and Bahrain enjoy close, brotherly relations founded on shared faith, common values, mutual respect, and longstanding people-to-people links,” FO noted.

Dar and Al Zayani last met in September on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, where they discussed bilateral relations, including preparations for the JMC session.

They also exchanged views on regional and international developments, with Al Zayani appreciating Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability.

Pak-Bahrain exchanges

Islamabad and Manama had agreed to establish the JMC in 2014, when King Sheikh Hamad bin Isa bin Salman Al-Khalifa paid a three-day visit to Pakistan.

Following the last JMC session in July 2021, which was held in Manama, the two countries signed a memorandum of understanding to promote business between the two countries.

Earlier this month, Dar chaired an inter-ministerial meeting to review preparations for the Pakistan-Bahrain JMC and directed the ministries concerned to pursue concrete outcomes from the Bahrain FM’s visit.

The Pakistani leadership has also undertaken official visits to the Gulf kingdom in recent years.

PM Shehbaz, accompanied by Dar, made a two-day trip to Bahrain in November 2025, during which he met with the king and crown prince there.

Then, in January this year, President Zardari made a four-day trip to the kingdom, where he highlighted economic opportunities that Pakistan offers.

World.title: Afridi-led convoy enters Peshawar as PTI long march continues for 5th day
World.content:
PESHAWAR: A PTI convoy led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi entered Peshawar on Thursday evening.

The route plan for the march, being carried out to demand the release of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, has undergone multiple changes.

While the party initially vowed to march towards Islamabad, its final destination seemingly remains tentative as the KP CM has yet to announce the plan for the trek after Oct 8.

A post by the PTI’s official X account shortly after 6pm said the Afridi-led convoy had reached Hayatabad Toll Plaza in Peshawar. It also shared pictures of hundreds of supporters gathered to welcome the KP CM.

“The public has shattered the idols of fear and is standing firm with their leader Imran Khan and their elected chief minister,” the post said.

“God-willing, by the time it reaches Swabi, this caravan will become the largest long march in Pakistan’s history,” the PTI asserted.

Ahead of the protesters’ arrival, an unannounced disruption of mobile and cellular internet services was reported since last night in several areas of the provincial capital.

PTI’s march began from Lakki Marwat on Oct 4, from where the protesters trekked to Kohat on the second day and then camped overnight on Oct 6 in Mattani, located on the outskirts of Peshawar. It then reached Khyber on Oct 7.

The Centre had warned the party against any protests or gatherings in Islamabad. However, the PTI decided to embark on the march after weekend talks with the federal government failed to bridge their differences for multiple reasons , particularly over the counterterrorism policy.

The march was announced as part of the PTI’s nationwide protest, initially scheduled for Sept 27 but was later postponed to Oct 4.

Gohar calls for reviewing counterterrorism policy

PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan said on Thursday that his party had never supported terrorism, adding that, however, the country’s counterterrorism policy needed to be reviewed in the light of changing circumstances.

Gohar was speaking to the media in Charsadda, which is expected to be the next stop of the PTI’s march after Peshawar.

The PTI chairperson visited the residences of KP Public Health Engineering Minister Fazal Shakoor and MNA Fazal Mohammad Khan, whom the PTI alleges were abducted by unidentified men amid reports of detentions of its workers and members ahead of the march.

Gohar expressed concern over their disappearance and demanded their immediate and safe recovery.

Speaking to the media at their residences, he noted that 18 days had passed since Shakoor’s alleged abduction and his family had no information about his whereabouts.

He urged the relevant authorities to take immediate notice of the matter and ensure that Shakoor and Khan were recovered and reunited with their families.

PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan speaks to the media in Charsadda on Oct 8. — Photo by Faiz Muhammad

Gohar said the “enforced disappearances” were a matter of serious concern and stressed the need for rule of law and protection of citizens’ constitutional rights. If such incidents were taking place in KP, they could also occur in other provinces, he further warned.

He also rejected the imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency as a solution to the prevailing situation in KP, as federal ministers continue to indicate the possible enforcement of either of the two, citing terrorism. The warning of a possible emergency or governor’s rule had come ahead of the PTI’s long march and as talks between the opposition party in the Centre and the federal government failed earlier this month.

For his part, Gohar said political issues should be resolved through constitutional and democratic means. He called upon the decision-makers to respect the public mandate and elected governments.

On the security situation, he asserted that the PTI, its workers and supporters had never supported terrorism. He said the party stood with the state in the fight against terrorism, but the country’s policy on the issue needed to be reviewed in light of changing circumstances.

“Terrorism, whether in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan or Sindh, is against Pakistan,” he said, adding that the loss of any Pakistani’s life in the fight against terrorism was a national loss. He called for the implementation of the National Action Plan through a unified national policy rather than politicising the issue.

Gohar also defended CM Afridi, saying he had never issued a statement in support of terrorists. He criticised what he described as attempts by some federal ministers to portray PTI as a supporter of terrorism.

The PTI chairperson said his party was still ready for meaningful and positive dialogue with its political opponents and expressed hope that Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman would play a constructive role in the prevailing situation. He thanked the JUI-F, Awami National Party and Jamaat-i-Islami for opposing the imposition of governor’s rule.

On the PTI’s long march, he said it would continue as per the decided schedule, with gatherings planned in Mardan on Oct 10 and Swabi on Oct 11, after which the future course of action would be decided by the party leadership.

He also criticised the imposition of Section 144 in parts of KP, saying elected representatives should be taken into confidence in matters concerning law and order.

He urged all political parties, whether in government or opposition, to play their role in strengthening democracy, an independent judiciary, free elections and the rule of law.

Gohar said the federal government and the opposition needed to set aside their differences and engage in sincere, unconditional dialogue to help the country overcome its political crisis.

Mobile services disrupted

Though there was no word from the provincial government on the unannounced cellular disruption, a Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) official, however, confirmed to Dawn that the authority had ordered the suspension at the directives of higher authorities.

The official told Dawn the suspension was temporary and taken as a security precaution during the long march. The official said the orders were conveyed on Wednesday night.

Special Assistant to the Chief Minister on Home and Tribal Affairs Tariq Saeed Marwat did not respond to whether his department requested the interior ministry cell phone service suspension. KP Information Minister Shafi Jan was also not available for comment.

Meanwhile, some major private schools across Peshawar also remained closed on Thursday. However, government schools, colleges and universities remained open.

Many parents found out about the school closure on Thursday morning when their children returned home after finding the school gates locked.

Yousaf Khan, a resident of Ring Road, told Dawn that he found out on Thursday morning. “My children were told at the school gate to go back,” he said, adding that he did not hear about the closure due to the suspension of cellular service.

“Due to the prevailing political situation in the city, the school will remain closed tomorrow, i.e, on Oct 8”, a notice from one of the private schools read, adding that classes will resume from Friday.

However, Private Schools Regulatory Authority (PSRA) officials said no order for school closure was issued, and action will be taken against schools that remained closed without government directions.

The authority has also written to the principals of all private schools, stating that certain private educational institutions had been closed by their respective administrations in connection with the ongoing long march, without any notification from the PSRA.

“In view of the above, all heads/principals/administrators of private educational institutions are hereby directed to keep their respective institutions open and ensure regular academic activities until clear directions/notification are issued by this authority,” the letter, seen by Dawn, read.

It said that failure to comply with the directions would be viewed seriously, and strict disciplinary action would be initiated against the concerned institution/management under the relevant rules and regulations.

PHC seeks CM Afridi’s reply to contempt plea

Separately, the Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Thursday sought a reply from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to a contempt petition alleging that he violated a court order by using an official helicopter to participate in the PTI long march.

A bench comprising Chief Justice SM Attique Shah and Justice Ijaz Khan issued notice to the chief minister on a petition filed by PML-N MPA Zahir Khan.

The petitioner alleged that the chief minister violated the court’s Oct 23, 2025 judgment, which barred the use of government vehicles, machinery and manpower for protests, rallies, long marches or political activities.

According to the petition, Afridi used a KP government helicopter on Oct 4 to travel from Peshawar to Lakki Marwat to participate in, launch and lead the PTI’s long march.

He contended that the violation was not confined merely to the CM’s journey, but the official helicopter’s use necessarily involved deployment of its pilots, crew, fuel, technical staff, ground arrangements, security personnel, protocol officials and other public resources.

He added that the entire official machinery accompanying and facilitating the said flight was employed to enable the chief minister to reach and lead the political long march, in direct violation of the 2025 ruling.

The petitioner sought contempt proceedings against CM Afridi and asked the court to summon him and seek details of the helicopter’s authorisation, flight log and expenditure. The hearing was then adjourned.

World.title: Turkiye's FM Fidan says Istanbul assessing aid to Saudi Arabia as part of Makkah agreement
World.content:
Turkiye is assessing how it can help Saudi Arabia counter attacks from Yemen’s Houthis under the Makkah defence pact signed between Islamabad, Riyadh and Istanbul, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Thursday.

The defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

“The technical evaluations are [being] carried out, and these continue among our military officials,” Fidan said during a joint press conference in Ankara with his Hungarian counterpart, adding that officials were working out what contributions could be made, particularly on air defence.

Ankara’s top diplomat also stressed that the pact was a defensive agreement, not an offensive one.

“When a country of this agreement is attacked, you have to side with them,” Fidan stated. “This is not an attack agreement. Turkiye is not carrying out an attack by sending troops to another country’s land.”

The Turkish foreign minister added that the process of sending the text of the agreement to the Turkish parliament for ratification had been finalised.

Fidan’s remarks came after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Monday agreed to the deployment of military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom during an emergency meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh.

The emergency meeting of the alliance’s Strategic Political and Defence Committee addressed the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia.

“The committee decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the kingdom, in accordance with the approved arrangements and the national legislation of the parties, thereby enhancing readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats,” a statement issued by the Foreign Office after the meeting said.

While the statement did not specifically name any threat, the development comes against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in the Yemen conflict.

A day prior, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry told CNN that Pakistani troops were already in Saudi Arabia, adding that they had been in the kingdom “for decades” and across multiple domains.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar has also described the agreement as defensive, without an offensive agenda. Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has said Pakistani and Turkish forces would play a supporting role, including reconnaissance, while Saudi forces conduct combat operations.

World.title: Nepra notifies consumers of Rs1.11 per unit higher fuel costs in Oct billing
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) on Thursday notified electricity consumers of an additional burden of Rs16 billion by allowing Rs1.11 per unit in higher fuel costs in October billing.

In a notification, Nepra said it had decided that the “positive fuel cost adjustment (FCA) for August 2026, i.e. Rs1.1086/kWh … shall be applicable to all the consumer categories of K-Electric and ex-Wapda distribution companies (XWDISCOs), except lifeline consumers, electric vehicle charging stations and prepaid electricity consumers of all categories who opted for the prepaid tariff”.

The regulator said the higher FCA would also be applicable to consumers under the incremental consumption package.

DISCOs and KE are required to reflect the fuel cost adjustment for August 2026 in the October 2026 billing month.

The Central Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA) had reported that the actual average fuel charges component for August 2026 amounted to Rs8.8265/kWh, against the reference fuel charges component of Rs7.0998/kWh approved in the applicable notified consumer-end tariff.

Accordingly, it had demanded an additional FCA of Rs1.73 per unit for electricity consumed in August 2026.

After certain adjustments, Nepra worked out the actual fuel component of the tariff at Rs8.2084, instead of Rs8.8265 as claimed by CPPA, thus allowing an additional FCA of Rs1.11 in October billing, instead of the Rs1.73 per unit demanded by CPPA.

The higher additional fuel cost in August stemmed from expensive RLNG imports from the spot market, as contracted supplies from Qatar remained under force majeure, besides higher coal imports and lower-than-estimated availability of cheaper hydropower and nuclear generation.

Hydropower was originally targeted to account for about 41 per cent of total power generation, but its share was slightly below 38pc, while the share of nuclear power was estimated at 16.4pc but turned out to be 10pc due to an outage at the Karachi’s nuclear power plants.

As a consequence, the share of imported coal-based generation increased to 15.6pc, instead of 7.4pc as originally planned.

Hydropower has no fuel cost, while the average nuclear fuel cost increased to Rs3.15 per unit due to lower utilisation, instead of Rs2.5 per unit.

In contrast, the cost of imported coal-based generation came to Rs17 per unit. The cost of local coal-based generation was reported at Rs5.5 per unit.

The cost of RLNG-based generation was reported at Rs45.93 per unit, even higher than the Rs45.25 per unit cost of furnace oil-based power generation, which also includes a petroleum levy of Rs73,000 per tonne.

The FCA is reviewed every month under the tariff regime applicable across the country and is usually applicable to consumers’ bills for one month only.

Under the tariff mechanism, changes in fuel costs are passed on to consumers only on a monthly basis through an automatic mechanism, while quarterly tariff adjustments on account of variations in power purchase prices, capacity charges, variable operation and maintenance costs, and use-of-system charges — including the impact of transmission and distribution losses — are built into the base tariff by the federal government.

World.title: Pakistan Bar Council declares Ahsan Bhoon's law degrees genuine
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Bar Council (PBC) on Thursday declared that the degrees of its elected members, including prominent lawyer Ahsan Bhoon, were genuine.

The announcement by the PBC — the supreme regulatory body of lawyers — follows a debate over lawyers’ degrees, with the qualification of Bhoon, a member of the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP), particularly being questioned.

In an official statement on Thursday, the PBC noted that the returning officers (ROs) for the council’s 2020 and 2025 elections had gotten the elected members’ degrees verified from their respective universities before notifying them as PBC members.

“It is, therefore, clarified that the verification of the degrees of the returned candidates, including that of Bhoon, was undertaken through the relevant universities in accordance with the prescribed procedure,” the council said.

It explained that the RO for PBC Election-2020, the Attorney General for Pakistan (AGP), had the degrees verified by the universities soon after the elections, following which the successful candidates were notified as PBC members.

Similarly, the RO for PBC Election-2025, also the AGP, again initiated the process of verification of the elected members’ degrees.

“Some members whose degrees were already verified in the last elections, their degrees too were sent again for verification to the relevant universities as well as the Higher Education Commission (HEC),” the council maintained.

The statement comes over a week after former MNA and retired Capt Muhammad Safdar called for verification of the degrees of prominent lawyers, including Bhoon, a close associate of Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar.

The debate also comes ahead of the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) elections scheduled for Oct 29.

Bhoon, a former SCBA president, heads the Independent Group, also known as the Asma Jahangir Group. Safdar has announced the formation of his own group, the Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah Group.

Days later, Safdar moved a complaint with the JCP to seek verification of Bhoon’s educational qualifications, enrolment and professional credentials.

The complaint had also sought verification of his original degrees, transcripts, result cards and registration records; independent confirmation from the degree-awarding institution; verification from the HEC; his complete enrolment record with the relevant provincial bar council and the PBC; and the dates and basis of his enrolment as an advocate.

On the other hand, Bhoon has served a Rs5 billion defamation notice on Capt Safdar, demanding an unconditional public apology and retraction of the allegation that his LLB degree was fake.

According to the notice, Safdar made the allegations while speaking publicly outside the Supreme Court on or about Sept 23, with remarks repeated in later media appearances and video messages.

World.title: Canadian writer Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
World.content:
Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature “for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature,” the award-giving body said on Thursday.

The prize is awarded by the Swedish Academy and is worth 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2m).

Canadian poet and essayist Carson’s work often blends verse, prose, dialogue and translation in a genre-defying mix.

She is widely known for her translations of classical Greek literature, which heavily influences her work which ranges from opera libretti to literary criticism and verse novels such as Autobiography of Red from 1998.

Her style is exemplified in Norma Jeane Baker of Troy from 2019, a performance piece which mixes the stories of Helen of Troy in Euripides’ play Helen and Marilyn Monroe.

Carson takes a place beside luminaries such as Alexander Solzhenitsyn, Alice Munro and Ernest Hemingway as a recipient of the award, which often divides opinion among book lovers.

The Academy has been lambasted for ignoring some of the literary titans of the last 120 years such as Leo Tolstoy, Virginia Woolf and Jorge Luis Borges, criticised for snubbing US authors, though it gave the prize to singer-songwriter Bob Dylan in 2016, and accused of being too obscure in its choices.

Defenders say the Academy has made popular picks, such as Colombia’s Gabriel Garcia Marquez in 1982 and Doris Lessing in 2007, arguing that part of its task is to highlight lesser-known literary traditions and encourage readers to broaden their horizons.

Established in the will of Swedish dynamite inventor and businessman Alfred Nobel, the prizes for achievements in literature, science and peace have been awarded since 1901.

Last year’s prize was won by Hungarian writer Laszlo Krasznahorkai, dubbed the “master of the apocalypse” by American critic Susan Sontag.

World.title: Pakistan, IMF reach staff-level agreement for $1.2bn tranche
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Thursday reached a staff-level agreement (SLA) with the Pakistani authorities on the fourth review under the $7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the third review under the $1.4bn Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF), qualifying Pakistan to draw about $1.2bn from the Fund’s resources within four to five weeks.

“The IMF team has reached an SLA with the Pakistani authorities on the fourth review of the 37-month Extended Arrangement under the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the third review of the 28-month arrangement under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF)”, the lending agency announced in an early morning statement.

The SLA is subject to approval by the IMF Executive Board. Upon approval, Pakistan will have access to about $1bn (SDR 760 million) under the EFF and about $210 million (SDR 154 million) under the RSF, bringing total disbursements under the two arrangements to about $5.7bn, it said.

The two sides also concluded Article IV consultations, the IMF announced from Washington headquarters.

“Program implementation under the EFF has remained broadly on track despite a challenging external environment. The authorities remain committed to preserving macroeconomic stability, strengthening public finances, ensuring that inflation returns durably to the State Bank of Pakistan’s target range, enhancing energy sector viability, strengthening social protection, and accelerating reforms to foster sustainable, private sector-led, and inclusive growth,” the IMF statement said.

The authorities have also continued to advance their climate reform agenda under the RSF to strengthen Pakistan’s resilience and reduce vulnerabilities to climate-related risks, it added.

The fund team led by Iva Petrova was in Pakistan and held discussions under the 2026 Article IV consultation and on the 4th review EFF and the 3rd review under the RSF from September 23 to October 7.

“Supported by the EFF, the authorities have successfully navigated the impact of the Middle East conflict, and strong policies have helped preserve macroeconomic stability. Real GDP growth reached 4 per cent in the first three quarters of FY26, and although higher energy prices and supply disruptions weakened somewhat the momentum, FY26 growth is estimated at 3.6pc.”

Headline inflation moderated to about 10.3pc in September after peaking in May, while core inflation remained contained, the fund said.

It added: “The current account was broadly balanced in FY26 supported by strong remittances, and gross reserves rose to about $21.5bn by end-September. Sovereign rating upgrades and renewed international market access also point to stronger policy credibility. Nevertheless, the fund said risks remain high, particularly from geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices, tighter global financial conditions, and trade disruptions.”

The authorities remain committed to sound macroeconomic policies, which are critical to safeguarding stability amidst the ongoing shock-prone environment, it further stated.

The authorities’ policy priorities would continue to maintain strong fiscal policies. Steadfast implementation of the FY27 budget, anchored by an underlying primary surplus of 2pc of GDP and supported by tax policy and revenue administration measures, is critical to placing public debt on a durable downward path, it noted.

Revenue administration reforms, including improved risk-based audits, digital invoicing, and use of third-party data, will help safeguard the revenue targets. A comprehensive medium-term tax reform strategy should make the system fairer, simpler, and more growth-friendly, while protecting revenues and reducing distortions, the statement said.

The authorities will stay the course in enhancing public financial management, it said, noting that they were “making progress in strengthening public financial management to improve the efficiency and transparency of the budget process, public investment, procurement, and government cash management.

“They remain committed to reducing debt rollover risks and servicing costs amid elevated gross financing needs, while advancing the development of the domestic government securities market and diversifying the investor base,” the IMF said.

On social protections, the IMF said authorities had arrested the long-term decline in health and education spending, raising it from 2.2pc of GDP in FY24 to 2.5pc of GDP in FY26.

It noted that the authorities were “committed to increasing it further to 2.8pc of GDP in FY27, closely monitoring implementation, and reallocating resources as needed to meet this objective.

“The planned increase in targeted cash-transfer benefits, together with continued improvements in beneficiary coverage and payment systems, will strengthen protection for vulnerable households and support more inclusive growth.”

The fund called for phasing out the fuel support scheme promptly, given its high cost and broad targeting. Any future fuel support—should oil prices surprise on the upside—should be limited, time-bound, targeted using established social assistance programs, and accommodated within the FY27 budget envelope, it said.

It called on the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) to maintain an “appropriately tight” policy stance to ensure inflation returns durably to the SBP’s target range.

“Exchange rate flexibility should continue to serve as an important shock absorber, while further reserve accumulation, gradual liberalisation of the foreign exchange regime, and deeper domestic financial markets will strengthen resilience and support private sector development,” it directed.

The fund also called for timely tariff adjustments and cost-reducing reforms essential to prevent renewed circular debt accumulation while protecting vulnerable consumers.

“Priorities include improving sector efficiency, advancing private participation in distribution, deepening electricity market competition, maintaining gas sector cost recovery, and reducing unaccounted-for gas losses”, it said.

The fund said that Article IV consultation focused on reforms to support the structural transformation of the economy to higher value-added activities and reduce gaps relative to peer countries in key areas, including by strengthening competition, reducing regulatory and trade barriers, advancing privatisation, enhancing SOE governance and transparency, and strengthening governance and anti-corruption institutions.

Together with efforts to introduce a simpler and fairer tax system, allocate greater public resources toward human and capital development, ensure a more cost-efficient energy sector, and deepen financial markets, these reforms are critical to raise productivity, increase labour force participation and job creation, and support private investment and exports, it noted.

“Supported by the RSF, the authorities are continuing efforts to strengthen resilience to climate change, with recent progress in mainstreaming climate considerations into public investment planning and strengthening disaster risk financing and coordination.

“Further reforms are advancing on irrigation water pricing and collection, better-targeted electricity subsidies, energy-efficiency standards, and transport decarbonization.”

Later in the day, the Ministry of Finance, in a post on social media platform X, said that Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb held a “wrap-up session” with Petrova at the conclusion of the review.

EFF and RSF packages

Pakis­tan and the IMF had reached the 39-month $7bn aid package deal in July 2024, with the programme set to allow the country to “cement macroeconomic stability and create conditions for stronger, more inclusive and resilient growth”.

In March 2025, the two sides reached an SLA on the first biannual review of the EFF programme and on unlocking the $1.3bn RSF arrangement.

Subsequently, in May that year, the IMF’s Executive Board allowed a $1bn disbursement under the EFF — bringing total released funds under the package to about $2.1bn — and also approved the RSF loan.

In October 2025, the government and the Fund reached an SLA on the second review of the EFF, securing another $1bn under the programme and $200 million under the RSF after the Board’s approval in December.

A Petrova-led mission held talks with Pakistan in March this year for the third review of the EFF and the second review of the RSF, but the two sides failed to reach an agreement and decided to continue negotiations.

Then in May, the IMF’s Executive Board allowed Pakistan to draw about $1.1bn under the EFF and about $220m under the RSF, bringing total disbursements under the two arrangements to roughly $4.8bn.

World.title: Fizz takes three in Mumbai rout
World.content:
Pace sensation Mustafizur Rahman recorded his best bowling figures of the Indian Premier League today when he finished with 3 for 16 in Sunrisers Hyderabad’s 85-run victory over Mumbai Indians at Vishakhapatnam.

The three-wicket haul took the left-armer to joint-second in the wicket-takers’ list with a total tally of 13 scalps from nine matches. He is one short of Mitchell McClenaghan, who has taken 14 wickets in 10 matches.

The 20-year-old currently has the best bowling average, 15.61, and best economy rate, 6.15, amongs bowlers who have played at least eight matches in the tournament.

The Sunrisers Hyderabad might have depended on Mustafizur a number of times in the ongoing Indian Premier League, but today was a collective effort. Ashish Nehra, Bhuvaneshwar Kumar and Barinder Sran had reduced the Mumbai Indians to 49 for 6 in nine overs before Mustafizur was given the ball.

The wily left-armer sent back Hardik Pandya with his first ball with a cutter which Pandya failed to adjust himself against. Pandya attempted a slice through point, but the ball curled away to the hands of the keeper, with the umpire judging that out even though the television replays were inconclusive.

Then in the very first ball of his second over again, Fizz bowled yet another slower delivery which moved away from the batsman, getting the edge of Tim Southee on the way to the keeper.

The man from Satkhira returned got the scalp of McClenaghan in the final delivery of his third over, getting the batsman to offer a loopy catch to midwicket.

Mustafizur did not get to bowl a fourth over as David Warner gave the other bowlers their chance to mop up the tail. And they did efficiently, bundling out the hosts for just 92 runs in 16.3 overs.

Earlier, brilliant performances from Hyderabad openers, Warner and Shikhar Dhawan helped the team post 177. Dhawan scored 82 off 57 while Warner smacked 48 off 33. Yuvraj Singh also had a good time with the bat, scoring 39 off 23.
